# [LEGACY] Release v2.47.12

### Fixed

- fix: remove `engines` restriction in `package.json`.
It blocked installs on some Node versions even though SunEditor has no Node runtime dependency. #1689

### Enhancement

* Improved editing performance in frequently-run operations such as content cleaning, line format changes, and list merging.

### Changes

* Components (image, table, hr, ...) are now treated as atomic units in tree traversal and are no longer traversed into.
* An explicit `tagStyles` tag entry is now merged with its `@line`/`@text` category styles instead of replacing them.

### Bugfix

* Fixed a bug where styles applied across an entire list item (`font-family`, `font-size`, `color`, ...) were stripped when the HTML was cleaned. [#1682](https://github.com/JiHong88/suneditor/issues/1682)
* Fixed a bug where the content structure was broken when pasting into Google Docs. [#1683](https://github.com/JiHong88/suneditor/issues/1683)
* Fixed a bug where the `placeholder_line` hint overflowed past the line on center- or right-aligned lines.
* Fixed a bug where Backspace and Delete did nothing on an empty list item. [#1681](https://github.com/JiHong88/suneditor/issues/1681)
* Fixed a bug where Delete did nothing on the line before a list and did not pull the following line up at the end of the last list item.

### New Feature

* A `blockHandle.onPlusClick` option has been added — a hook that runs after the plus button inserts a new line, letting the host decide what opens next.
* `blockHandle.maxHeight` / `blockHandle.minWidth` and `slashCommand.maxHeight` / `slashCommand.minWidth` options have been added to size the menu.
* A `table.insert(cols, rows)` method has been added to insert a table without going through the size picker.
* The block handle is now shown for top-level components (image, table, ...) so they can be reordered like any other block.

### Changes

* The default value of the `slashCommand.limitSize` option has been changed to no limit; set it explicitly to restore a cap.

### Bugfix

* Fixed a bug where code view failed to close and dropped every image after the first when a single inline wrapper held multiple images.
* Fixed a bug where the `plugins` option in array form (`plugins: [image, link]`) registered nothing and editor creation failed.
* Fixed an issue where cleaning HTML left behind empty lines that had no caret position.
* Fixed an issue where a dropdown-free flyout (table, fontColor, ...) stayed open while the arrow keys kept navigating the menu behind it.
* Fixed a bug where a menu's sub-panel closed the entire menu on the next keypress when a second menu existed.
* Fixed a bug where the text fields inside a dropdown-free flyout, such as the color picker's hex box, could not be focused or typed into.
* Fixed a bug where the table size picker inserted a table with no rows or columns when it was clicked before a size had been hovered.
* Fixed a bug where the toolbar button group order was scrambled when `textDirection` was set to `rtl`. [#1680](https://github.com/JiHong88/suneditor/issues/1680)
* Fixed a bug where global `window` listeners survived `destroy()` and kept firing against the destroyed editor.
* Fixed an issue where picking a dropdown-free plugin from the slash command menu with the keyboard made its picker vanish.
* Fixed a bug where an exception thrown from a plugin `retainFormat` hook aborted the entire HTML cleaning pass. [#1679](https://github.com/JiHong88/suneditor/issues/1679)

### Design

* Redesigned the full editor icon set.
* Increased the corner rounding (`border-radius`) across the editor UI for a rounder look.

### New Feature

* A `lineBreakClearStyle` option has been added — when `true`, pressing Enter at the end of a line starts a fresh line without carrying the caret's inline style nodes (bold, italic, color, links); the line-level element and its attributes are preserved. Affects the end-of-line case only.
* `toolbar_sticky` option now accepts a `position: 'sticky' | 'fixed'` field (default `'sticky'`); `'fixed'` forces the JS `position: fixed` sticky engine over native CSS `position: sticky` for environments where CSS sticky misbehaves.
* `placeholder_line` option now accepts an object for per-type hints, keyed by tag name (`pre`, `blockquote`, ...) or a category sentinel (`@line`, `@normalLine`, `@list`, `@brLine`, `@closureBrLine`, `@block`, `@closureBlock`), resolved most-specific to least. The string form is unchanged.
* A `menu.subscribeDropdownOff(callback)` method has been added to subscribe to dropdown-off events; it returns an unsubscribe function.

### Enhancement

* Added `Esc` key support to close open toolbar dropdown menus, including dropdown-free menus like fontColor.
* Updated the table cell controller so the unmerge button is hidden instead of disabled when there are no merged cells, matching the merge/split button toggle.

### Bugfix

* Fixed an issue where the off-screen focus-temp input (`.__se__focus__temp__`) was a keyboard tab stop; it is now `tabindex="-1"` and no longer reachable by Tab. [#1677](https://github.com/JiHong88/suneditor/issues/1677)
* Fixed a bug where the finder toolbar button did not toggle the finder panel closed when pressed again.
* Fixed an issue where pressing Enter on an empty line inside a block (e.g. `<blockquote>`) with content below placed the new line and caret below the lower chunk instead of between the two chunks.
* Fixed an issue where opening a dropdown-free plugin's sub-panel from the command menu (e.g. fontColor's color-picker hue slider) closed the entire menu; the flyout now closes only when the plugin commits.

## AppPorts v1.9.0 更新说明 （in English） · [直链下载](https://file.shimoko.com/AppPorts) ·  [赞助](https://pic.cdn.shimoko.com/thanks.png)

### 总结

这次，我们想让你更省心地给 Mac 腾空间。**1.9.0 加入了保留应用原始签名的 APFS 容器数据迁移**，让聊天记录、图片视频等适用的应用数据也能搬到外置盘，应用仍按原来的路径读取。希望你能少一点因为空间不足而做取舍，多留一些喜欢的应用和想留住的内容。我们还加入了数据卷自动接回，让日常连接外置盘后的准备工作更轻松。

打开 AppPorts，你也会发现找数据、看空间更顺手了。我们重新整理了目录树，加上搜索筛选、展开动画、可调高度的信息栏和零字节目录开关，**哪些数据占地方、这次能腾出多少空间，看得更明白**。针对部分应用迁移后或恢复到本地后找不到关联数据的问题，我们也补上了识别支持；这项修复无需重新迁移或重新签名，更新后重新扫描即可。

第一次使用有新的分步引导，权限没准备好、应用信息没读全，也会告诉你下一步该怎么做。我们还完善了原始应用备份、失败恢复和 macOS 27 修复指引，希望你从第一次搬家到日常使用，都能少一点摸索，多一点安心。感谢大家把使用中遇到的问题告诉我们，这些反馈都在帮助 AppPorts 变得更好用。

### 升级提示

**准备升级 macOS 27：请先更新并打开一次 AppPorts。** 新版需要这次启动来更新已经安装的后台重签名脚本，加入系统版本保护；只下载新版还不够。升级后打开 AppPorts，会关闭「开机自动重签名」并停止、移除旧任务；若未能完成清理，设置页会提示重试。

**旧方式迁移的应用打不开时，先查看修复步骤。** 连接原来的外置盘，完全退出要修复的应用，然后在应用列表中找到带「签名已替换」标记的应用，点击「修复」。先还原通过旧符号链接迁移的容器数据，再恢复原始签名或从官方渠道重装。保留现有数据和备份，不要再次重签名。详细步骤见 [macOS 27 升级与修复说明](https://docs-appports.shimoko.com/macos-27.html)。

已经通过 APFS 挂载迁移的目录无需仅为签名修复而还原。更新 AppPorts 不会自动转换旧迁移，也不会自动恢复曾被替换的签名。

### 新功能

**APFS 容器数据迁移** — 支持将 `Containers`、`Group Containers` 下的应用数据迁移到外置盘，在原目录挂载专用的数据卷，保留应用原有签名和访问路径。提供挂载、卸载和还原操作。默认模式下，容器数据使用这套方案；其他数据目录继续使用各自适用的迁移方式。

**容器数据卷管理与自动接回** — 数据目录新增「已挂载」「待挂载」「外置盘未连接」等状态，按当前情况提供挂载、卸载和还原操作。迁移成功后安装后台挂载任务，在登录或连接外置盘时尝试接回数据卷；最后一条挂载记录还原后自动移除任务。后台任务独立运行，不需要打开主窗口；旧系统的管理员授权限制见下方使用提示。

**全新首次使用引导与准备检查** — 首次启动按步骤介绍迁移方式，并检查完全磁盘访问权限、App 管理权限和外部存储。缺少权限时可直接前往对应的系统设置；还没选外置盘也可以先进入应用。完成引导后记住进度，后续可在「设置 → 准备情况」重新检查。

**核对当前运行的 AppPorts** — 准备检查中显示当前进程对应的应用版本、构建号和实际路径，并提供「在 Finder 中显示」和「复制路径」。完全磁盘访问检查区分通过、被拒绝和无法确认三种结果，方便排查升级后授权仍指向旧副本的情况。此功能检查当前进程的实际访问能力，不能直接读取并比对系统授权列表中的版本。

**零字节目录显示开关** — 工具目录和应用数据默认隐藏已经确认是零字节的本地目录，可通过「显示零字节目录」开关恢复显示，并记住选择。仍在计算、读取不完整，以及已链接、已挂载或待接回的目录继续保留；有匹配子目录时保留必要的父级层次。

**签名问题识别与修复面板** — 根据 AppPorts 的原始签名记录和真实应用当前的签名判断是否发生替换，在应用行提供修复入口。修复面板按实际情况展示容器数据还原、原始签名恢复或官方重装步骤，并提供重新检查和文档入口。

**完整原始应用备份与恢复** — 重签名前保存完整的原始应用，恢复时还原其签名、授权及文件元数据，无需开发者私钥。只有旧签名记录的用户，可以选择匹配的官方原版应用补救。当前应用与备份不匹配时，会说明原因并保留恢复材料。

### 界面与目录浏览

**更清楚的数据目录树** — 保留左侧应用列表，右侧按目录类型展示父子关系。目录行采用系统文件夹图标，类型由分组图标和标题说明；调整行高、缩进、字号与间距，对齐名称、大小、状态和操作。迁移、还原等常用操作直接显示在对应行。

**展开与折叠合并为一个按钮** — 顶部按钮根据当前状态切换「展开全部」和「折叠全部」。分组、文件夹及全部目录的展开收起加入过渡动画，箭头随状态旋转，并遵循系统「减少动态效果」设置。

**可上下拖动的信息栏** — 拖动目录列表下方的把手调整信息栏高度，为目录列表或路径详情分配更多空间。信息栏可压缩为紧凑的单行路径，同时保留复制和 Finder 定位操作；展开后展示本地路径、外部路径和目录说明，长内容可单独滚动。

**搜索与键盘浏览** — 支持按目录名称、路径和说明搜索，与类型、状态和优先级筛选配合使用。匹配结果保留父级上下文并自动展开。支持方向键选择、展开和折叠目录，以及复制所选目录路径；鼠标选择不再强行将目录滚动到列表中央。

**各页面的视觉风格统一** — 应用迁移保留原有双栏和操作流程，微调本地、外部面板的标题、图标和按钮比例，使其与下方列表对齐。数据目录、目录迁移及顶部工具栏采用更一致的底色、圆角和间距，减少分隔线、厚重阴影和突兀的白色区块；以轻量的颜色区分区域、选中和悬停状态，并兼顾浅色与深色外观。

### 改进

**应用数据识别更完整** — 改进迁移到外置盘的原生应用、iOS 包装应用，以及恢复到本地后的应用数据扫描，按真实应用信息查找关联目录，并保留原有的名称匹配。这项修复不改变迁移、签名或 Dock 的操作流程，也不需要重新迁移、重新签名或额外授权；更新后重新扫描即可。

**应用信息没读全时给出明确提示** — 应用信息无法读取时，保留通过名称找到的数据，在页面内提示结果可能不完整，不再把识别失败简单显示为「未找到关联数据目录」。如果真实应用路径不可用，会提示检查路径；应用位于外置盘时，连接磁盘后刷新即可重新识别。切换应用或重新扫描时清除旧提示，避免混淆。

**可释放空间估算更准确** — 只汇总当前筛选范围内可迁移的本地目录，父子目录及重复路径只计算一次；已链接、已挂载到外置盘的数据及其子目录不再计入本机可释放空间。对于微信等包含受保护父目录的应用，仍正确统计其中允许迁移的子目录。

**读取不完整时明确说明** — 目录枚举或大小测量失败时，保留已读取结果，目录显示「至少…」或「无法读取」，汇总区域显示「空间统计不完整」，避免把部分数据或读取失败当成完整大小、零字节目录。权限被拒绝时提供「检查访问权限」入口，并可查看受影响路径。

**刷新重新测量目录大小** — 刷新时重新读取大小，避免沿用应用写入数据前的旧结果；目录挂载状态变化或子目录内容变化时同步处理相关缓存。扫描状态持续到大小计算结束，期间使用固定尺寸的系统进度指示器，避免刷新图标旋转偏心。

**迁移前先说明条件和下一步** — 点击「迁移」后，先检查外部存储是否连接、格式、加密状态及可用空间。可以直接选择或更换存储，继续检查刚才选中的目录；条件不满足时说明原因，并提供保留现状和查看准备方法的选项。

**重签名先在工作副本完成** — 校验备份、在工作副本上重签名并确认结果后，再替换真实应用。操作期间应用内容发生变化、备份损坏或替换失败时，保留现有应用和恢复材料；恢复原始签名前等待旧后台重签名任务停止，避免刚恢复又被改写。

**应用更新后的备份更准确** — 识别经过验证、开发者身份一致的官方更新或重装版本，建立新的恢复点，并归档旧记录与旧快照，避免用旧版本备份覆盖新版本应用。选择官方原版补救时，同时核对应用标识、版本和开发者签名。

**登录与插盘后的挂载更及时** — 调整后台任务的启动方式，减少重复磁盘查询；外置盘识别较慢时持续等待连接事件并有限重试，等待期间让出操作资源。每次挂载后检查卷是否真正落在原目录，遇到系统提前挂到其他位置的情况，会重新定位并接回。

**后台任务路径更可靠** — 更新或移动 AppPorts 后，启动时同步后台任务的程序路径。从 DMG 或系统临时隔离路径运行时，先提示将 AppPorts 放入「应用程序」，避免安装指向临时位置的任务。旧系统需要管理员权限时，可通过系统密码框重试挂载。

**减少辅助数据卷的干扰** — 数据卷默认不显示在 Finder 边栏和桌面，并添加 Spotlight 索引排除标记，减少额外占用。还原数据时跳过卷自身的索引、事件记录等辅助文件；后台任务无事可做时减少日志输出。

**外置盘未连接时保护原目录** — 未挂载的目录保持不可写，减少应用在本机另建一份数据的风险。重新挂载前检查目录是否为空；发现本地文件或其他卷占用时停止操作，避免遮住已有数据。使用应用前仍需先连接外置盘并确认挂载完成。

**迁移失败后保留明确的恢复入口** — 迁移前检查外置盘空间，切换路径前保留本地安全副本。操作失败时尝试恢复原目录；无法完成恢复时，保留可用副本并说明所在路径和数据卷信息。

**还原与清理分别处理** — 还原前检查本机空间，先停用对应目录的自动挂载，再切换回本地数据。数据已恢复但后续清理失败时，单独保存待清理记录并提供重试，重试不会再次复制或覆盖已经恢复的数据。还可明确选择仅移除清理记录、保留现有副本。

**更严格的操作对象与记录校验** — 挂载、卸载和还原前核对数据卷身份，只处理 AppPorts 管理的目标。迁移记录无法读取时保留原文件；卸载后只删除空挂载点。后台挂载、手动迁移和签名操作协调执行，避免同时修改同一份数据。

**长操作之后重新检查应用状态** — 等待后台任务、获取操作权限或完成签名备份后，再次确认应用是否运行、入口是否仍指向同一应用。批量还原过程中应用重新启动时，停止后续目录的操作。经典模式的沙盒重签名仍需针对当前真实应用单独确认。

**确认弹窗更清楚** — 统一迁移、还原和签名相关提示，长说明可滚动，标题与操作按钮保持可见。取消和 Esc 行为一致，需要确认风险的操作在勾选后才可继续；执行下一步前先关闭当前弹窗，避免按钮无响应或后续弹窗被覆盖。

**经典模式保留为可选项** — 「经典数据迁移模式」默认关闭，开启前需要确认风险，设置卡片新增「查看完整说明」。macOS 27 上仍可手动开启经典模式，但开机自动重签名保持停用；推荐使用保留原始签名的挂载迁移。

**更多异常场景的回归覆盖** — 新增挂载与还原、外置盘延迟上线、目录占用、备份损坏、应用更新、后台重签名停用和清理重试等测试；补充可释放空间去重、读取失败、零字节筛选、当前应用权限检查，以及赞助名单线上优先与离线回退测试。本次应用数据识别修复另新增 48 个回归测试，覆盖迁移与恢复后的应用、外置目标缺失后恢复、短名称误匹配及异常链接等情况；本地全量 474 个测试通过，相关测试已加入持续集成。

## English Release Notes

### Summary

We want freeing up space on your Mac to feel less like a chore. **Version 1.9.0 adds APFS container data migration that preserves your apps’ original signatures**, so supported app data, including chat history, photos, and videos, can move to an external drive while apps keep reading from their familiar paths. That means fewer difficult choices about which apps or memories to keep. We have also added automatic data-volume reconnection to make getting ready after connecting your drive easier.

Finding your data and understanding your storage should feel easier, too. We have refreshed the directory tree with search and filters, expansion animations, a resizable information panel, and a zero-byte directory toggle. **It is clearer what takes up space and how much a migration can free.** We have also fixed missing data results for some migrated or restored apps. This discovery fix needs no repeat migration or re-signing: update AppPorts and scan again.

New step-by-step guidance helps you get started, with clearer next steps when permissions are missing or app information cannot be fully read. Better original-app backups, failure recovery, and macOS 27 repair guidance are there to make the experience more reassuring, from your first move to everyday use. Thank you for telling us where things get frustrating—your feedback helps make AppPorts easier to use.

### Upgrade Notes

**Before upgrading to macOS 27, update and open AppPorts once.** Launching the new version updates any installed background re-signing script with a system-version check; downloading the update alone is not enough. Opening AppPorts after the macOS upgrade turns off “Auto Re-sign at Login” and stops and removes the old task. If cleanup cannot finish, Settings provides a retry option.

**If an app migrated with the old method no longer opens, start with the repair guide.** Connect the original external drive, fully quit the affected app, and click “Repair” beside an app marked “Signature replaced.” Restore container data migrated through old symbolic links first, then restore the original signature or reinstall from an official source. Keep existing data and backups, and do not re-sign the app again. See [Upgrading to macOS 27 and repairing affected apps](https://docs-appports.shimoko.com/en/macos-27.html).

Directories already using APFS mount migration do not need to be restored solely for signature repair. Updating AppPorts does not automatically convert older migrations or restore previously replaced signatures.

### New Features

**APFS container data migration** — Move app data under `Containers` and `Group Containers` to dedicated volumes on an external drive, mounted at the original directories without changing the app’s signature or data paths. Mount, unmount, and restore operations are available. This is the default method for container data; other directories continue to use their applicable migration methods.

**Container volume management and automatic reconnection** — New directory statuses include “Mounted,” “Pending Mount,” and “External drive not connected,” with the applicable mount, unmount, and restore actions. Successful migration installs a background task that attempts to reconnect volumes at login and when storage connects. It is removed after the final mount record is restored. The task runs without opening the main window; see the administrator-authorization limits for older systems below.

**New first-run guidance and readiness checks** — A step-by-step introduction checks Full Disk Access, App Management permission, and external storage. Missing permissions link to the corresponding System Settings page, and choosing a drive can wait until later. Completing the introduction is remembered. Readiness checks remain available in Settings.

**Identify the running copy of AppPorts** — Readiness checks show the current process’s app version, build, and actual path, with Show in Finder and Copy Path actions. Full Disk Access checks distinguish success, denial, and an unknown result, helping investigate permissions that may still refer to an older app copy. This checks the running process’s actual access; it cannot directly read and compare versions in the system’s authorization list.

**Zero-byte directory toggle** — Tool directories and app data hide confirmed empty local directories by default. “Show zero-byte directories” restores them and remembers the preference. Directories still being measured, incomplete reads, and linked, mounted, or pending-reconnection data remain visible. Parent context is retained when a child matches.

**Signature detection and repair panel** — AppPorts compares its original signing records with the real app’s current signature to identify replacements and provide an inline repair action. The panel shows the applicable steps for restoring container data, recovering the original signature, or reinstalling an official copy, with links to documentation and a way to check again.

**Complete original-app backups and restoration** — Before re-signing, AppPorts saves the complete original app so its signature, entitlements, and file metadata can be restored without the developer’s private key. Users with older signing records can supply a matching official app. If the current app does not match the backup, AppPorts explains the problem and preserves recovery materials.

### Interface and Directory Browsing

**A clearer directory tree** — The app list remains on the left, with data grouped by directory type on the right. Rows use system folder icons, while group icons and titles identify directory types. Refined row heights, indentation, typography, and spacing align names, sizes, statuses, and actions. Common migration and restoration actions appear directly on each row.

**One control for expanding and collapsing** — The toolbar switches between Expand All and Collapse All based on the current state. Groups, folders, and the full tree expand and collapse with transitions and rotating disclosure arrows, respecting the system’s Reduce Motion setting.

**Vertically resizable information panel** — Drag the handle below the directory list to give more space to either the list or its details. The panel can shrink to a compact path row while retaining Copy Path and Show in Finder. Expanding it reveals local and external paths and directory descriptions, with independent scrolling for longer content.

**Search and keyboard navigation** — Search directory names, paths, and descriptions alongside type, status, and priority filters. Results retain parent context and expand automatically. Arrow keys select, expand, and collapse directories, and the selected path can be copied. Mouse selection no longer forces a directory to the center of the list.

**Consistent styling across pages** — App migration retains its two-pane layout and workflow, with refined header, icon, and button proportions aligned to the lists below. Data directories, custom directory migration, and the top toolbar use more consistent backgrounds, corners, and spacing, with fewer dividers, heavy shadows, and abrupt white blocks. Subtle color distinguishes areas, selection, and hover states in light and dark appearances.

### Improvements

**More complete app data discovery** — Improved scanning for native apps moved to external storage, wrapped iOS apps, and apps restored to the Mac. AppPorts reads the real app’s identity to find associated directories while retaining existing name matching. This fix keeps migration, signing, and Dock workflows unchanged and requires no repeat migration, re-signing, or additional permission grants. Update and scan again to use it.

**Clear feedback when app information cannot be read** — Data found by name remains visible, with an inline warning that results may be incomplete. An identity lookup failure is no longer shown as an ordinary “No associated data directories found” result. If the real app path is unavailable, AppPorts suggests checking it; for apps on external storage, reconnect the drive and refresh to retry. Switching apps or starting a new scan clears the previous warning.

**More accurate reclaimable-space estimates** — Totals include only migratable local directories within the current filter, counting parent/child directories and duplicate paths once. Data already linked or mounted externally, including its descendants, is excluded from reclaimable local space. For apps such as WeChat, migratable children inside protected parent directories are still counted correctly.

**Explicit incomplete-read reporting** — If directory discovery or size measurement fails, available results are retained. Directory sizes show “At least…” or “Unable to read,” and the summary reports incomplete space statistics instead of presenting a partial result as complete or treating failed reads as empty directories. Permission denials provide an access-check entry point, and affected paths can be inspected.

**Fresh measurements when refreshing** — Refreshing measures directories again instead of reusing sizes from before an app wrote new data. Related caches account for mount-state changes and child-directory changes. Scanning remains active until size calculation finishes, using a fixed-size system progress indicator to avoid off-center rotation of the refresh icon.

**Clearer checks before migration** — Clicking “Migrate” checks the external storage connection, format, encryption status, and available space. You can choose or change storage and continue checking the selected directory. If the requirements are not met, AppPorts explains why and offers options to keep the current setup or read the preparation guide.

**Re-signing happens on a working copy first** — AppPorts validates the backup, signs a working copy, and verifies the result before replacing the real app. If the app changes during the operation, the backup is damaged, or replacement fails, the current app and recovery materials are retained. Signature restoration waits for old background re-signing tasks to stop so they cannot immediately overwrite the restored app.

**Backups follow verified app updates** — A verified official update or reinstall with the same developer identity creates a new recovery point while archiving the previous record and snapshot. This prevents an older backup from being used to overwrite a newer app. Official originals supplied for recovery are checked for matching app identity, version, and developer signature.

**More timely mounting at login and drive connection** — Adjusted how the background task starts and reduced repeated disk queries. Slow drives are given time to appear through connection events and bounded retries, without holding operation resources while waiting. Each mount is checked to ensure the volume reaches the original directory; volumes mounted elsewhere by macOS are relocated when possible.

**More reliable background-task paths** — Launching AppPorts after moving or updating it refreshes the background task’s executable path. Running from a DMG or a temporary App Translocation path prompts installation in Applications before setting up new mount migrations. Older systems can retry mounting through the system administrator password dialog.

**Less clutter from auxiliary data volumes** — Data volumes are hidden from Finder’s sidebar and desktop by default and marked to exclude them from Spotlight indexing. Restoration skips the volume’s index, event records, and other auxiliary files. Background runs with nothing to do produce less log output.

**Protecting the original directory while storage is offline** — Unmounted directories remain non-writable to reduce the risk of an app creating a second local data set. AppPorts checks that the mount point is empty before reconnecting a volume and stops if local files or another volume occupy it. Connect the drive and confirm mounting is complete before using the app.

**Clearer recovery after migration failures** — AppPorts checks external free space and retains a local safety copy before switching paths. Failed operations attempt to restore the original directory. If recovery cannot complete, available copies are retained and their paths and volume details are reported.

**Restoration and cleanup are handled separately** — AppPorts checks local free space and disables automatic remounting for the directory before switching back to local data. If the data is restored but cleanup fails, a separate pending-cleanup record supports retrying without copying or overwriting restored data again. An explicit option can remove only the cleanup record while preserving existing copies.

**Stronger checks on operation targets and records** — Mount, unmount, and restore operations verify volume identity and act only on managed targets. Unreadable migration records are preserved, and only empty mount points are deleted after unmounting. Background mounting, manual migration, and signing operations are coordinated to avoid changing the same data concurrently.

**App state is checked again after lengthy work** — After waiting for background work, acquiring operation access, or completing a signature backup, AppPorts checks whether the app is running and whether its launch entry still points to the same target. Relaunching an app during batch restoration stops subsequent directory operations. Classic-mode sandbox re-signing still requires separate approval for the current real app.

**Clearer confirmation dialogs** — Migration, restoration, and signing prompts use a consistent layout. Long explanations scroll while titles and action buttons remain visible. Cancel and Esc behave consistently, and operations requiring risk acknowledgment stay unavailable until it is checked. The current dialog closes before the next action to avoid unresponsive buttons or hidden follow-up prompts.

**Classic mode remains optional** — “Classic Data Migration Mode” is off by default and requires risk confirmation. Its Settings card now includes a link to the full documentation. Classic mode can still be enabled manually on macOS 27, but automatic re-signing at login remains disabled. Mount migration that preserves the original signature is recommended.

**Broader regression coverage** — Added tests for mounting and restoration, delayed drives, occupied directories, damaged backups, app updates, disabling background re-signing, and cleanup retries. Further coverage checks reclaimable-space deduplication, failed reads, zero-byte filtering, permissions for the running app, and online-first sponsor loading with offline fallbacks. The app data discovery fix adds another 48 regression tests covering migrated and restored apps, recovery after an external target becomes available, short-name mismatches, and invalid links. All 474 tests passed locally, and the relevant tests have been added to continuous integration.

### Fixes

- Fixed data scans for some externally migrated apps reading the local launch entry’s identity, which could miss associated containers or match unrelated directories ([#63](https://github.com/wzh4869/AppPorts/issues/63)).
- Fixed missing associated data for wrapped iOS apps, including after restoration to the Mac, by reading the inner app’s information. Existing short-name matching restrictions remain in place to avoid broader false matches.
- Fixed failed app identity lookups appearing as normal empty results without marking space estimates as incomplete. Refreshing reads the app information again when the external target becomes available.
- Fixed selecting a directory forcing it to the center of the list and interrupting browsing.
- Fixed inconsistent directory size calculations and cache updates that could show a parent directory as smaller than its children.
- Fixed reclaimable-space estimates for apps such as WeChat potentially including non-migratable parents, duplicate directories, or external data.
- Fixed failed directory reads being treated as empty directories or partial sizes appearing without a warning. Missing optional directories are no longer classified as read failures.
- Fixed permission checks failing to distinguish denial from an unknown result, avoiding a false denial when a probe file is unavailable.
- Fixed some repair and delete controls appearing overly prominent or misaligned with other controls on the row.
- Fixed the maximum log size displaying only `1` when `100 MB` was selected.
- Fixed generic terms such as `CN`, `mac`, and `desktop` in app names or Bundle IDs matching unrelated containers, including WPS data appearing in Trae CN’s repair steps.
- Fixed signature checks potentially inspecting the local launch entry instead of the real external app. Failed checks or inaccessible external apps now have a separate check-pending state, with recovery materials preserved.
- Fixed repair guidance requiring an external app to be moved back locally even when a complete original app backup was available. That step is now shown when needed for an official reinstall.
- Fixed restoration initiated from a local linked app mistaking its launch entry for the real external app and reporting that an existing local file could not be overwritten.
- Fixed some confirmation dialogs remaining open after an action, making buttons appear unresponsive or obscuring follow-up prompts.
- Fixed subdirectories potentially being missed when container paths use the `/private/var` form.
- Fixed missing sponsor names when no profile link was provided and fractional sponsorship amounts being rounded to whole numbers on the website.

### Migration Notes

- Container mount migration currently requires an **unencrypted APFS external drive** and Full Disk Access for AppPorts. Move AppPorts to Applications before using it. Other storage formats can still be used for supported app or ordinary-directory migrations, while container data can stay on the Mac. See [Mount Migration](https://docs-appports.shimoko.com/en/datamigrae/mount-migration.html).
- On the first launch after migration, allow Removable Volumes access if macOS asks. Connect the external drive before using the app, and quit the app and eject the drive normally before disconnecting it. Keep a separate backup of important data.
- On systems requiring administrator authorization for mounting, such as macOS 12, you may need to open AppPorts and enter the system password. The background login task cannot complete that authorization itself.

After confirming the download source, move AppPorts to the Applications folder and run:

```shell
xattr -rd com.apple.quarantine /Applications/AppPorts.app
```

**顶部工具栏重排** — 应用页和数据目录页的切换按钮改为更紧凑的图标 + 文本样式，减少按钮占用空间，整体视觉更轻量。

**数据目录页操作栏优化** — 「工具目录 / 应用数据」切换、迁移后重签名开关、恢复原始签名按钮和刷新按钮现在统一放在顶部工具栏中，不再在数据迁移页内单独占用一整行。

**应用状态徽章更新** — 应用列表新增「待迁出」状态徽章，方便区分本地版本高于外部旧副本、可以迁出替换的应用。

**数据目录迁移弹窗本地化** — 数据迁移重签名确认弹窗的标题、正文和按钮现在会跟随当前语言显示，不再出现部分内容回退中文的问题。

### 改进

**应用迁移安全策略增强** — 外部目标已存在时，AppPorts 不再仅凭同名或大小相近就自动删除目标。只有目标被明确识别为 AppPorts 管理的旧入口、旧迁移残留，或当前应用处于「待迁出」状态时，才会自动清理并继续迁移。

**数据目录恢复校验增强** — 数据目录迁移不再使用“目标目录大小接近源目录”的方式判断是否可自动恢复。现在必须完整匹配 AppPorts metadata，包括 `schemaVersion`、`managedBy`、`sourcePath`、`destinationPath` 和 `dataDirType`，才能自动接回或恢复。

**应用数据扫描更稳定** — 快速切换应用时，旧扫描任务的结果不会再覆盖当前选中应用的数据目录列表，避免出现上一个应用的数据误显示到当前应用中的情况。

**管理员命令和 AppleScript 转义增强** — 路径中包含引号、反斜杠、空格或中文时，Finder 删除和管理员修复权限命令现在会更安全地处理，降低特殊路径导致命令失败或误执行的风险。

**本地化完善** — 修复切换语言后部分帮助内容、提示弹窗和数据迁移确认内容仍显示中文或翻译不完整的问题，并补齐所有支持语言的相关翻译（[#43](https://github.com/wzh4869/AppPorts/issues/43)）。

**中国大陆更新体验优化** — 针对中国大陆网络环境适配更新接口，新增 AppPorts 官网更新源与「国内下载」入口；当 GitHub 访问不稳定时，仍可获取更新说明并通过国内镜像下载。

修复路径包含特殊字符时 AppleScript 或管理员命令可能构造错误的问题。

修复应用数据迁移流程中，后台迁移或迁移后重签名可能读取到已切换应用的问题。

修复「待迁出」状态未在应用列表中显示状态徽章的问题。

## English Release Notes

### New Features

**Pending Move Out status** — When a real local app is newer than the matching app on external storage, AppPorts now marks it as “Pending Move Out”. This means the newer local copy can safely replace the older external copy during migration.

**Re-sign confirmation for app container data migration** — Before migrating app container data, AppPorts now asks whether the related app should be automatically Ad-hoc re-signed after migration. Users can choose to re-sign after migration or migrate only, reducing the risk of app data recognition issues or launch problems after container data migration ([#44](https://github.com/wzh4869/AppPorts/issues/44)).

### UI Improvements

**Top toolbar refresh** — The Apps and Data Directories tab switcher now uses a more compact icon + text style, reducing oversized toolbar controls.

**Cleaner Data Directories toolbar** — The Tool Directories / App Data switcher, re-sign-after-migration toggle, restore original signature button, and refresh button are now consolidated into the top toolbar instead of taking a separate row inside the data migration page.

**Updated app status badge** — The app list now shows a new “Pending Move Out” badge for local apps that are newer than their matching external copies.

**Localized data migration dialog** — The re-sign confirmation dialog for data migration now follows the selected app language for its title, message, and buttons.

### Improvements

**Safer app migration conflict handling** — When an external target already exists, AppPorts no longer deletes it just because it has the same name or similar contents. Automatic cleanup is only allowed when the target is clearly identified as an AppPorts-managed legacy portal, old migration residue, or when the app is marked as “Pending Move Out”.

**Stricter data directory recovery checks** — Data directory migration no longer relies on size similarity to decide whether a target can be recovered. AppPorts now requires matching metadata, including `schemaVersion`, `managedBy`, `sourcePath`, `destinationPath`, and `dataDirType`.

**More stable app data scanning** — When switching apps quickly, stale scan results no longer overwrite the currently selected app’s data directory list.

**Safer AppleScript and administrator command escaping** — Paths containing quotes, backslashes, spaces, or non-ASCII characters are now handled more safely in Finder deletion and ownership repair commands.

**Localization updates** — Fixed cases where help content, prompts, and data migration confirmation dialogs could remain in Chinese or have incomplete translations after switching languages. Related translations have been completed for all supported languages ([#43](https://github.com/wzh4869/AppPorts/issues/43)).

**Improved update experience for users in mainland China**— Added an official AppPorts update feed and a China download entry, so release notes and domestic downloads remain available when GitHub access is unstable.

### Fixes

Fixed a case where data directory migration could mistake a real external directory for a recoverable AppPorts-managed target.

Fixed a case where app migration could accidentally delete a real external app with the same name.

Fixed detection and cleanup of legacy AppPorts portals and old migration residue.

Fixed AppleScript and administrator command generation for paths containing special characters.

Fixed migration and post-migration re-signing using the wrong selected app after the user switched apps.

Fixed the missing status badge for apps marked as “Pending Move Out”.

**Envoy AI Gateway v1.1.0 is the first minor release on the stable 1.x API. It adds token counting across providers, per-request upstream credentials, stream idle timeout with failover, MCP hostname routing and CEL backend selection, optional OpenTelemetry GenAI tracing, and HTTP CONNECT egress. Upgrading from v1.0 needs no CRD migrations; the only operator-facing change is Helm's restricted controller security context.**

## ✨ New Features

### Token Counting APIs

- **vLLM-compatible `/tokenize` across providers** — Count tokens for a prompt without generating a completion. Chat messages and completion prompts use the [vLLM tokenize](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/api/tokenization.html) request shape against vLLM, Vertex AI Gemini, GCP Anthropic, AWS Bedrock Converse, and AWS Anthropic. Native Anthropic clients can use `/anthropic/v1/messages/count_tokens`; Responses API clients can use `/v1/responses/input_tokens` (OpenAI and Azure OpenAI).
- **Anthropic-format `/anthropic/v1/models`** — Claude clients that call Anthropic's model list endpoint now get the gateway's configured catalog in Anthropic's response shape, scoped by hostname the same way `/v1/models` is.

### Per-Request Credentials & Egress

- **Per-request upstream credentials via `credentialOverride`** — A trusted filter can supply the backend credential per request instead of sharing one static key in `BackendSecurityPolicy`. Source from Envoy dynamic metadata (preferred) or a request header the gateway strips before the backend. API keys, Anthropic, Azure, GCP, and AWS SigV4 are supported.
- **HTTP CONNECT forward proxy** — `GatewayConfig.spec.forwardProxy` tunnels upstream LLM connections through an HTTP CONNECT proxy (`host:port`). Bedrock requests through PrivateLink now sign over the actual upstream host, so VPC endpoints no longer fail with a silent 403.

### Streaming Resilience

- **Stream idle timeout with failover** — `AIGatewayRouteRule.streamIdleTimeout` bounds how long Envoy waits without upstream bytes on a streaming response. If it fires before the first token, a retry policy can fail over to the next backend; mid-stream it returns 504. Pair with a `BackendTrafficPolicy` whose retry covers reset.

### MCP Gateway

- **Hostname routing and backend selection** — `MCPRoute.spec.hostnames` scopes an MCP endpoint to specific hosts. `backendSelector` restricts which backends a session fans out to via CEL rules evaluated at initialize (default Deny). Initialize now advertises merged backend capabilities, and the controller shares one Envoy Gateway `Backend` per namespace.

### Observability

- **OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions and Grafana dashboard** — Set `AI_GATEWAY_TRACING_SEMCONV=gen_ai` on the ext-proc to emit `gen_ai.*` span attributes. An example dashboard for `gen_ai_*` Prometheus metrics ships in `examples/monitoring/grafana-dashboard.json`. Controller and ext-proc logs accept `--logFormat=json`; MCP resource reads populate `mcp_resource_uri` in access-log metadata.

### Provider Translation & API Compatibility

- **Structured output for Claude on Vertex AI** — JSON-schema constrained decoding now works for Claude models on Vertex AI that advertise `output_config`. OpenAI `reasoning_effort` is forwarded to Bedrock as `reasoning_config`.
- **Responses API `tool_search`, unknown tools, and Codex inputs** — The Responses API accepts the built-in `tool_search` tool and `additional_tools`, preserves unknown tool types, and accepts Codex-style agent input items.

### Helm & Operations

- **Controller hardening and sharded config secrets** — The chart can emit a PDB, honour `topologySpreadConstraints`, and attach extra `podLabels`. Filter configuration is split across multiple Secrets so large Gateway configs no longer hit Kubernetes' 1 MiB Secret size limit.

## 🔗 API Updates

- **`AIGatewayRouteRule.name`** — Optional unique name copied onto the generated `HTTPRoute` rule. `route-not-found` is reserved.
- **`AIGatewayRouteRule.streamIdleTimeout`** — Optional Gateway API duration; unset means no per-try idle timeout.
- **`BackendSecurityPolicy.spec.credentialOverride`** — Optional per-request credential source. Exactly one of `fromRequestHeaders` or `fromDynamicMetadata`. `fallbackToConfigured` defaults to `true`.
- **`GatewayConfig.spec.forwardProxy`** — Optional HTTP CONNECT proxy. `address` is required (`host:port`).
- **`MCPRoute.spec.hostnames`** — Optional list of hostnames (max 16).
- **`MCPRoute.spec.backendSelector`** — Optional CEL selector evaluated at session initialize. `defaultAction` defaults to Deny.


## ⚠️ Breaking Changes

- **Helm controller security context defaults** — The Helm chart now sets a restricted `podSecurityContext` and container `securityContext` on the controller (non-root UID/GID 65532, all capabilities dropped, no privilege escalation, RuntimeDefault seccomp). Previously both were empty. If you run a custom controller image that cannot use UID 65532, override `controller.podSecurityContext` and `controller.securityContext` in your values.

## 📖 Upgrade Guidance

Upgrading from **v1.0** requires no CRD migrations. New fields are optional and backward compatible. Review the Helm security-context change if you override the controller image.

If the official controller image works for you, no action is needed. To restore empty security contexts:

```yaml
controller:
  podSecurityContext: {}
  securityContext: {}
```

JSON logs: set `controller.logFormat` and `extProc.logFormat` to `json`. Enable a PDB with `controller.podDisruptionBudget.enabled: true` when you run more than one replica.

# Envoy AI Gateway v1.0.0 — General Availability

Envoy AI Gateway v1.0.0 marks **General Availability**. With this release the core control-plane API — `AIGatewayRoute`, `AIServiceBackend`, `BackendSecurityPolicy`, `GatewayConfig`, and `MCPRoute`, all served at `v1beta1` — is declared **stable**: within the 1.x series we will not make breaking changes to it unless required by a critical security fix, and any such change will ship with a documented migration path. **Upgrading from v0.7 requires no changes to your resources.** 1.0 brings together everything built since the first release in February 2025: a single OpenAI-compatible API across 16 providers with cross-provider translation, a full Model Context Protocol gateway, multimodal and audio endpoints, enterprise-grade observability, and multi-tenant, quota-aware routing — all as an additive layer on CNCF Envoy Gateway.

## 🎉 What 1.0 Means

1.0 is a commitment, not just another feature release. From the first release we said the major version would arrive once we had a _first stable control-plane API_. That moment is here. General Availability means:

- **A stable API.** Your `v1beta1` resources will not break under you within the 1.x series.
- **Predictable upgrades.** Upgrading the controller will not break a valid, migrated configuration; any change requiring action ships with a documented path.
- **A complete platform.** Everything assembled since v0.1 is now production-ready on the proven Envoy Gateway foundation.

### Our API stability commitment

For **stable** releases, we will **never break the APIs unless there is a critical security issue**, and we will always provide a migration path in the release notes if we ever must. Following [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/), the `v1beta1` control-plane API remains backward compatible for the entire 1.x series — breaking changes would only ever land in a future 2.0. See the full [support policy](https://github.com/envoyproxy/ai-gateway/blob/main/RELEASES.md#support-policy).

## ✨ The 1.0 Feature Surface

These are the capabilities the stable 1.0 control plane brings together.

### A Stable, Versioned Control-Plane API

- **Core CRDs now covered by the stability guarantee** — The control-plane API you build on — `AIGatewayRoute`, `AIServiceBackend`, `BackendSecurityPolicy`, `GatewayConfig`, and `MCPRoute`, all served at `v1beta1` — is now a stable contract. Within the 1.x series these APIs will not change in a breaking way unless required by a critical security fix, and any such change will ship with a documented migration path.

### Universal LLM Access

- **One OpenAI-compatible API across 16 providers** — Reach OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Google Gemini, Google Vertex AI, AWS Bedrock, Anthropic, Mistral, Cohere, Groq, Together AI, DeepInfra, DeepSeek, Hunyuan, SambaNova, Grok, and the Tetrate Agent Router Service through a single endpoint. Switch or mix providers without changing client code.
- **Cross-provider request/response translation** — Translate between provider protocols transparently — Anthropic `/v1/messages` to OpenAI `/v1/chat/completions`, and Anthropic Messages to AWS Bedrock Converse and InvokeModel — including streaming, tool use, reasoning/thinking blocks, and images.
- **Model virtualization with `modelNameOverride`** — Expose stable, application-facing model names while the gateway maps them to provider-specific models, enabling A/B testing, gradual migrations, and multi-provider strategies without touching client code.

### Full Endpoint Coverage

- **Chat, completions, embeddings, and images** — `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/completions`, `/v1/embeddings`, and `/v1/images/generations` across compatible providers.
- **Audio: transcription, translation, and speech** — `/v1/audio/transcriptions`, `/v1/audio/translations`, and `/v1/audio/speech` bring speech-to-text and text-to-speech workloads through the gateway.
- **OpenAI Responses API and multimodal inputs** — `/v1/responses` is supported, including on Azure OpenAI backends, and chat requests accept image, `audio_url`, and `video_url` content parts for compatible backends.

### MCP Gateway

- **Aggregate and route Model Context Protocol servers** — Multiplex multiple MCP servers behind one endpoint with `MCPRoute`, including tool routing and include/exclude filtering.
- **Fine-grained, CEL-based authorization** — Enforce per-tool authorization. `tools/list` applies the same rules as `tools/call`, so callers only discover the tools they are allowed to invoke.
- **Per-backend header forwarding with JWT claim projection** — Forward selected request headers and project JWT claims to individual MCP backends.

### Traffic Management & Multi-Tenancy

- **Hostname-based multi-tenant routing** — Serve different model sets per hostname from a single Gateway with `AIGatewayRoute.spec.hostnames`; the `/v1/models` endpoint scopes its response to the matching host.
- **Token- and quota-aware rate limiting** — Rate limit on model tokens and per `QuotaPolicy`, with backend rate limit filter injection to enforce quota-based throttling.
- **Provider fallback and InferencePool support** — Automatic failover across providers, plus intelligent endpoint selection for self-hosted models via the Gateway API Inference Extension.

### Provider Authentication & Compliance

- **`BackendSecurityPolicy` for upstream authentication** — Centralize provider credentials with API key, AWS, Azure, and GCP cloud-native identity, including GKE Workload Identity via Application Default Credentials.
- **Request/response body redaction** — Redact sensitive request and response bodies to meet compliance requirements.

### Enterprise Observability

- **OpenTelemetry tracing with OpenInference** — Full request-lifecycle tracing, compatible with AI evaluation tools like Arize Phoenix.
- **GenAI token metrics and reasoning-token accounting** — Prometheus metrics for token usage, time-to-first-token, and inter-token latency, with separate accounting for reasoning tokens.

## 🔗 API Updates

- **The `v1beta1` API is now stable** — v1.0 does not change the API surface. Instead it elevates the existing `v1beta1` CRDs to a stable contract under our [support policy](https://github.com/envoyproxy/ai-gateway/blob/main/RELEASES.md#support-policy): no new apiVersion is introduced and no resource migration is required. New fields added during the 1.x series will remain backward compatible.

## ⚠️ Breaking Changes

**None.** v1.0 introduces no breaking changes. The `v1beta1` API is unchanged — 1.0 declares it stable rather than altering it — so there is no apiVersion bump and no resource migration. If you are running v0.7, your existing resources work as-is.

## 🛡️ Support & Compatibility Policy

With 1.0, the project's [support policy](https://github.com/envoyproxy/ai-gateway/blob/main/RELEASES.md#support-policy) applies in full:

- **API compatibility.** The `v1beta1` CRDs are stable for the 1.x series. New fields are added in a backward-compatible way; breaking changes are reserved for a future major version and would ship with a migration path.
- **Controller upgrades.** Upgrading the controller will not break a valid configuration. Upgrade at most two minor versions at a time, following any documented migration steps.
- **Envoy Gateway compatibility.** Each release is built on the latest stable Envoy Gateway (and therefore Envoy Proxy); keep Envoy Gateway up to date before upgrading Envoy AI Gateway.
- **End of life.** A release is supported until two releases after it, consistent with prior versions.

Upgrading from **v0.7** is a drop-in change — there are no API or resource changes:

1. Update the Helm chart / controller image to the v1.0.0 release.
2. Roll out as usual. Your existing `v1beta1` resources require no edits.

If you are on an older release, upgrade one or two minor versions at a time and follow the migration steps in each series' release notes (notably the v0.6 promotion of the core CRDs to `v1beta1`) before moving to 1.0.

# Envoy AI Gateway v0.7.0

Envoy AI Gateway v0.7.0 adds **hostname-based routing** to `AIGatewayRoute`, enabling multi-tenant deployments where different hostnames expose different model sets through a single Gateway. A new **Anthropic Messages → AWS Bedrock Converse** translator lets Anthropic-native clients reach Bedrock without switching protocols. OpenAI **audio transcription and translation** endpoints arrive alongside **Azure OpenAI Responses API** support. Quota-aware rate limiting takes its first step with **backend rate limit filter injection** for `QuotaPolicy`. **Claude Opus 4.7** gains full reasoning support including the `display` parameter and `xhigh` effort tier. Anthropic-to-OpenAI translation now handles **reasoning blocks and images** end-to-end. MCP `tools/list` responses **respect authorization rules**, and multimodal support grows with `audio_url` and `video_url` content types. Several SSE streaming and provider translation bugs are fixed.

## ✨ New Features

### Multi-Tenant Hostname Routing

- **Hostname-based model scoping on `AIGatewayRoute`** — Serve different model sets from a single Gateway by assigning hostnames to each `AIGatewayRoute`. The `/v1/models` endpoint automatically returns only the models declared by routes matching the request's `Host` header, so tenants on `teamA.ai.example.com` and `teamB.ai.example.com` each see their own catalog without separate Gateways. Wildcard hostnames (`*.ai.example.com`) are supported following the Gateway API hostname matching rules.

### Provider Translation

- **Anthropic `/v1/messages` → AWS Bedrock Converse API** — Send requests in Anthropic Messages format and have them translated to Bedrock's Converse and ConverseStream APIs automatically. Supports text, images, tool use, thinking blocks, and streaming — so Anthropic-native clients can reach any Bedrock model without changing their integration. Complements the existing OpenAI → Bedrock Converse and Anthropic → Bedrock InvokeModel paths.
- **Reasoning and image support for Anthropic-to-OpenAI translation** — The Anthropic `/v1/messages` → OpenAI `/v1/chat/completions` path now handles thinking/reasoning content and image blocks end-to-end. Thinking config (enabled/disabled/adaptive) passes through, thinking and redacted_thinking blocks are preserved in multi-turn conversations, and image blocks (base64 and URL) convert to OpenAI `image_url` format. Previously these were silently dropped.
- **Claude Opus 4.7 and Mythos Preview reasoning** — Full support for Claude Opus 4.7's reasoning features: the `display` parameter (`summarized`/`omitted`) controls thinking content visibility, and `xhigh` joins the reasoning effort tiers for long-horizon agentic and coding tasks. Both `claude-opus-4-7` and `claude-mythos-preview` models are recognized for effort-based thinking control.
- **Custom request paths for Anthropic backends via `prefix`** — The `prefix` field on `VersionedAPISchema` now works for Anthropic-schema backends, producing endpoints like `/{prefix}/messages` instead of the default `/v1/messages`. Useful for routing to Anthropic-compatible providers that use a non-standard path.
- **Anthropic `anthropic-beta` header forwarded to AWSAnthropic** — The `anthropic-beta` request header is now mapped into the `anthropic_beta` body field when routing to AWSAnthropic backends, so beta features like extended thinking and token counting work through the gateway without manual body rewriting.

### OpenAI API Compatibility

- **Audio transcription and translation endpoints** — Full data-plane support for OpenAI's `/v1/audio/transcriptions` (Whisper transcription) and `/v1/audio/translations` (Whisper translation) endpoints. These accept `multipart/form-data` requests containing audio files, enabling speech-to-text workloads to flow through the gateway with the same auth, rate limiting, and observability as other traffic.
- **Azure OpenAI Responses API** — The OpenAI-compatible `/v1/responses` endpoint now works with Azure OpenAI backends, routing requests to Azure's `/openai/responses?api-version=...` path while preserving existing request and response handling. Azure users get Responses API support without changing client code.
- **`audio_url` and `video_url` content types** — OpenAI chat completion requests can now include `audio_url` and `video_url` content parts, enabling multimodal audio and video inputs for compatible backends like vLLM with phi-4-mm and Qwen 3.5 models.

### Quota-Aware Routing

- **Backend quota rate limit filter injection** — First step toward quota-aware routing: the controller now injects a backend rate limit filter when a `QuotaPolicy` is attached to an `AIServiceBackend`. The QuotaPolicy controller reconciles the policy, builds rate limit descriptor trees, and configures the rate limit service. This enables per-backend request throttling based on upstream provider quotas.

### MCP Gateway

- **Authorization-filtered `tools/list` responses** — MCP `tools/list` now applies the same authorization rules used by `tools/call`, omitting tools the caller isn't authorized to invoke. Prevents unauthorized callers from discovering tool names and avoids wasted LLM turns on tools that would fail at call time.

### Observability

- **Smarter log redaction preserves developer-authored metadata** — Debug log redaction (`--enableRedaction`) no longer masks developer-authored schema metadata that was previously over-redacted: tool definition `description` and `parameters`, tool call `function.name`, `response_format.json_schema`, and `guided_json` are now visible in debug logs. User-provided content and AI-generated text remain redacted, making debug logs significantly more useful without compromising privacy.

## 🔗 API Updates

- **`AIGatewayRoute.spec.hostnames`** — New optional field accepting a list of hostnames for hostname-based request filtering. When specified, the generated `HTTPRoute` includes these hostnames, and the `/v1/models` endpoint scopes its response to models from matching routes. Follows Gateway API hostname semantics including wildcard support.
- **`AIGatewayRoute.spec.rules` capped at 15** — Maximum rules per `AIGatewayRoute` reduced from 128 to 15 to match the Gateway API `HTTPRoute` limit (one slot is reserved for a controller-injected catch-all rule). To configure more rules on the same Gateway, split them across multiple `AIGatewayRoute` resources.
- **`VersionedAPISchema.prefix` supported for Anthropic** — The `prefix` field now applies to Anthropic-schema backends in addition to OpenAI. The `version` field is ignored for Anthropic; use `prefix` for custom paths. Note: `prefix` is ignored for `AWSAnthropic` and `GCPAnthropic` as these override paths internally.
- **`QuotaPolicy` rate limit filter injection (runtime enforcement)** — The `QuotaPolicy` CRD (introduced as API-only in v0.6) now has its first runtime behavior: when attached to an `AIServiceBackend`, a backend rate limit filter is injected to enforce quota-based throttling. Full quota-aware routing across multiple backends is planned for future releases.

## 🐛 Bug Fixes

- **SSE parser handles fields without space after colon** — The SSE event parser now correctly handles fields formatted as `data:{json}` (no space after the colon), in addition to the standard `data: {json}`. Fixes silent field drops when proxying responses from providers that omit the optional space.
- **Responses API streaming SSE buffering** — OpenAI Responses API and speech streaming translators now buffer incomplete SSE events across response body chunks instead of treating each chunk as self-contained. Fixes dropped or mangled events when TCP segment boundaries split an SSE event mid-frame.
- **Responses API token usage from incomplete and failed streams** — Token usage is now captured from `response.incomplete` and `response.failed` SSE events, not just `response.completed`. Streams that hit `max_output_tokens` or encounter post-generation failures no longer report zero tokens.
- **Nil output guard in AWS Bedrock response translator** — Bedrock can return HTTP 200 with no `output` field (e.g. guardrail interventions or `UnknownOperationException`). Previously this caused a nil-pointer panic in the ext-proc; now it returns a clean error to the caller.
- **Comprehensive Gemini finish-reason mapping** — Gemini finish reasons like `SAFETY`, `BLOCKLIST`, `RECITATION`, `MALFORMED_FUNCTION_CALL`, and others now map to their correct OpenAI equivalents instead of all falling through to `content_filter`. Unknown reasons map to `error` rather than silently misreporting as a content filter event.
- **Empty delta in GCP Vertex AI streaming chunks** — Streaming response chunks from GCP Vertex AI that lack candidate content now emit an empty `delta` object instead of omitting the field, conforming to the OpenAI streaming contract and fixing parse errors in strict clients.
- **Typeless assistant output messages in Responses API** — Multi-turn Responses API inputs that include assistant messages without an explicit `type: "message"` field (e.g. from OpenCode) now parse correctly. Previously these were treated as easy-input messages, causing unmarshalling failures on `output_text` content blocks.

## 📖 Upgrade Guidance

### Using Hostname-Based Routing

To serve different model sets per hostname, add `hostnames` to your `AIGatewayRoute`:

```yaml
apiVersion: aigateway.envoyproxy.io/v1beta1
kind: AIGatewayRoute
metadata:
  name: team-a-route
spec:
  hostnames:
    - "team-a.ai.example.com"
  rules:
    - matches:
        - headers:
            - name: x-ai-eg-model
              value: gpt-4o
      backendRefs:
        - name: openai-backend
```

Routes without `hostnames` remain accessible on all hosts. When at least one route uses hostname scoping, the `/v1/models` endpoint automatically returns only the models for the matching host.

### Rules-Per-Route Limit

`AIGatewayRoute.spec.rules` is now capped at 15 (down from 128) to match the Gateway API HTTPRoute limit. If you have routes with more than 15 rules, split them across multiple `AIGatewayRoute` resources attached to the same Gateway.

### Using Anthropic Prefix

If you route Anthropic traffic to a provider with a non-standard path, use the `prefix` field:

```yaml
schema:
  name: Anthropic
  prefix: /custom/v2 # produces /custom/v2/messages
```

Note: `prefix` is ignored for `AWSAnthropic` and `GCPAnthropic` backends as they override paths internally.

### Adopting Claude Opus 4.7 Reasoning

If you use Claude Opus 4.7 or Mythos Preview models, note that `display` defaults to `omitted` (unlike earlier Claude models which default to `summarized`). To receive summarized thinking content, set `display: "summarized"` explicitly. The new `xhigh` reasoning effort tier is available for long-horizon agentic tasks.

# Envoy AI Gateway v0.6.0

Envoy AI Gateway v0.6.0 marks the first **production-ready API surface**:
* The core CRDs (`AIGatewayRoute`, `AIServiceBackend`, `BackendSecurityPolicy`, `GatewayConfig`, `MCPRoute`) are now served at `v1beta1`.
* AWS Bedrock gains a native `InvokeModel` path for Claude alongside Titan embeddings via the OpenAI `/v1/embeddings` contract.
* Gemini gets first-class embeddings and Anthropic-style prefix context caching.
* Cross-provider clients can hit Anthropic's `/v1/messages` endpoint on any OpenAI-compatible backend, and a single `reasoning_effort` knob now works across Anthropic, OpenAI, and Gemini.
* Operators get GKE Workload Identity via Application Default Credentials, configurable webhook host networking, request/response body redaction for compliance, and the Go 1.26.2 + Envoy 1.37 + Envoy Gateway 1.7 baseline.

**Two breaking changes land in v0.6** — `AIGatewayRoute.spec.filterConfig` is removed (move to `GatewayConfig`), and the deprecated `version`-as-prefix behavior on `VersionedAPISchema` is removed (use `prefix`). See Upgrade Guidance below.

📖 **[Full documentation](https://aigateway.envoyproxy.io/docs/0.6/)**

## ⚠️ Breaking Changes

- **`AIGatewayRoute.spec.filterConfig` removed.** The `filterConfig` field on `AIGatewayRoute` has been removed. Move external-processor configuration (resources, env vars, image overrides) to a `GatewayConfig` resource referenced from the `Gateway` via the `aigateway.envoyproxy.io/gateway-config` annotation. v0.5 deprecated the `resources` subfield with a pointer to `GatewayConfig`; v0.6 removes the entire `filterConfig` struct, so anything still set there must move now. See the upgrade guidance below.
- **`VersionedAPISchema.version` no longer acts as an endpoint prefix for OpenAI-schema backends.** The legacy behavior deprecated in v0.5 is gone. Use the `prefix` field instead (e.g. `prefix: /v1beta/openai` for Gemini's OpenAI-compatible API, `prefix: /compatibility/v1` for Cohere). See the upgrade guidance below.

## ✨ New Features

### AWS Bedrock

- **Native `InvokeModel` API for Claude** — Send requests to Claude models on Bedrock through Bedrock's native `InvokeModel` endpoint, complementing the existing Converse API path. Useful when applications already speak the Anthropic Messages format and want a thin translation layer.
- **OpenAI → Bedrock Titan embeddings translation** — Call Amazon Titan embedding models on Bedrock through the standard OpenAI `/v1/embeddings` contract. Switch embedding providers without changing client code. Cohere and other Bedrock embedding models are not yet covered and will follow in a later release.

### Anthropic and Cross-Provider Translation

- **Anthropic `/v1/messages` endpoint on OpenAI backends** — Expose any OpenAI-compatible backend through Anthropic's Messages API. Lets Claude-style clients reach OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, or any other OpenAI-compatible provider behind the gateway without rewriting requests.
- **Structured output for Claude models** — Pass JSON schema constraints through to Claude so responses conform to your declared shape. Available on Anthropic and AWS Bedrock Claude backends today; GCP Vertex AI Claude is excluded pending upstream provider support.
- **Cleaner handling when `max_tokens` is omitted on Anthropic requests** — Requests without an explicit `max_tokens` no longer crash the translator; they're forwarded so the provider returns a normal validation error. Removes a long-standing footgun when forwarding OpenAI-shaped requests through the Anthropic path.
- **Adaptive thinking for `claude-opus-4.6`** — Translate Claude's new adaptive thinking mode end-to-end. Adaptive lets the model decide thinking depth per request rather than committing to a fixed budget, so callers can opt in without bespoke provider code.
- **Unified `reasoning_effort` across Anthropic, OpenAI, and Gemini** — A single OpenAI-style `reasoning_effort` value (`low`/`medium`/`high`/`xhigh`) now maps onto Anthropic's thinking budgets and Gemini 3's thinking controls. One client knob, three providers.

### Gemini Provider

- **Gemini embeddings translation** — Use Gemini embedding models through the OpenAI `/v1/embeddings` contract, completing Gemini coverage alongside chat completions and Responses.
- **Gemini context caching with prefix-style API** — Activate Gemini's context caching using the same Anthropic-style `cache_control` prefix surface already supported elsewhere. Cut input token costs on long, repeated system prompts without a Gemini-specific code path.
- **Gemini reasoning surfaced as thinking blocks** — Non-streaming Gemini reasoning is now exposed as both string content and structured `thinking_blocks`, matching the shape clients already use for Anthropic responses. Streaming responses still surface reasoning as string content only.

### OpenAI API Compatibility

- **Responses API — context management and richer streaming** — Second wave of Responses API work fills in context management and improved streaming so the `/v1/responses` path is closer to parity with `/v1/chat/completions`. If you held off on `/v1/responses` due to missing features, retest now.
- **Compatibility with open-source Responses API implementations** — Improved compatibility with non-OpenAI implementations of the Responses API (e.g. open-source inference servers that expose a `/v1/responses` endpoint), broadening which Responses-aware clients can sit in front of the gateway.
- **Text-to-speech endpoint `/v1/audio/speech`** — Route OpenAI text-to-speech requests through the gateway, so audio workloads benefit from the same auth, rate limiting, and observability as chat traffic.

### MCP Gateway

- **Per-backend header forwarding with rename** — `MCPRouteBackendRef.forwardHeaders` accepts a list of inbound headers to forward to each backend, optionally renaming them on the way out. Each MCP backend can receive its own set of headers (e.g. trace context, tenant identifiers, per-user auth) without a single route-wide rule.
- **JWT claim forwarding to MCP backends** — Project verified JWT claims into outbound headers via `MCPRouteOAuth.claimToHeaders`, enabling identity-aware tool execution at backend MCP servers without re-authenticating downstream.
- **Exclude / `excludeRegex` on tool selectors** — `MCPToolFilter` now supports deny patterns (literal `exclude` and regex `excludeRegex`) alongside the existing include rules. Useful when a backend exposes more capabilities than a given route should surface.
- **Tool name in access logs and response metadata** — Tool invocations now carry the tool name in dynamic metadata (key `mcp_tool_name`), so per-tool debugging, dashboards, and access-log fields are straightforward to wire up.
- **Per-backend capability tracking** — The gateway tracks which MCP server feature flags (`tools`, `prompts`, `resources`, `logging`, `completions`) each backend supports and merges them across a route. Capability negotiation now reflects what's actually reachable, so clients don't get told a feature is available when no reachable backend implements it.

### Authentication and Identity

- **GKE Workload Identity via Application Default Credentials** — GCP backends now authenticate using the standard ADC chain when neither `credentialsFile` nor `workloadIdentityFederationConfig` is set in the `BackendSecurityPolicy`. Workloads running on GKE pick up Workload Identity automatically — no static service account JSON secret needed.

### Security and Privacy

- **Request and response body redaction** — Strip or mask sensitive fields in request and response bodies before they hit logs, traces, or metrics. Lets you keep observability on while meeting privacy and compliance constraints.

### Observability

- **OTLP access logging auto-configured by `aigw`** — Standalone `aigw` wires up OTLP access logging out of the box when an OTLP endpoint is configured (via `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT`), removing a manual step from local-dev and demo paths.
- **Default `agent-session-id` → `session.id` header mapping** — Spans and logs now correlate by `session.id` automatically when clients send the `agent-session-id` header, so agent frameworks like Goose get session correlation with zero config. Override or disable via `OTEL_AIGW_REQUEST_HEADER_ATTRIBUTES`. Metrics never default to session IDs (high cardinality).
- **`ReasoningToken` cost type** — `LLMRequestCostType` now includes `ReasoningToken`, so you can budget and bill against thinking tokens separately from input, output, and cache cost types.
- **Response model metadata** — Responses now carry the resolved upstream model in metadata, which clients and downstream tools can read to confirm exactly which model served a request (useful when routes use model aliasing or fallback).
- **OTEL attribute count cap removed for large contexts** — Removed the OTEL span attribute count limit so long-context requests no longer have parts of their trace silently dropped.

### Operations and Extensibility

- **Custom webhook port and host network** — The conversion webhook can now bind to a configurable port (`controller.mutatingWebhook.port`) and run on the host network (`controller.hostNetwork`), smoothing installs in clusters with restrictive admission webhook networking such as GKE private clusters.
- **Lua filter slot after the AI ExtProc stage** — Lua filters can now be attached after the AI ExtProc stage in the standard filter chain, so you can do last-mile request shaping (header rewrites, body tweaks) without writing a custom `EnvoyExtensionPolicy`.
- **Route-scoped LLM request costs with global defaults** — Set `GatewayConfig.spec.globalLLMRequestCosts` for fleet-wide defaults and override per-route at `AIGatewayRoute.spec.llmRequestCosts`. Makes per-tenant or per-backend cost tracking straightforward without per-route boilerplate.

## 🔗 API Updates

- **Core CRDs promoted to `aigateway.envoyproxy.io/v1beta1`** — `AIGatewayRoute`, `AIServiceBackend`, `BackendSecurityPolicy`, `GatewayConfig`, and `MCPRoute` are now served at v1beta1, signaling that the core API and MCP routing surface are stable enough for production use. v1alpha1 versions remain registered with deprecation warnings so existing manifests continue to apply during the upgrade window.
- **`MCPRouteBackendRef.forwardHeaders`** — New per-backend list of headers to forward, with optional rename. Replaces the need for a single route-wide header forwarding rule when backends expect different headers.
- **`MCPRouteOAuth.claimToHeaders`** — Configure which verified JWT claims should be projected into outbound headers to MCP backends.
- **`MCPToolFilter.exclude` / `excludeRegex`** — Tool selectors now support exclusion alongside inclusion, with both literal and regex forms.
- **`LLMRequestCostType.ReasoningToken`** — New cost type for thinking-token usage, complementing the existing input, output, and cache cost types.
- **`GatewayConfig.spec.globalLLMRequestCosts`** — Fleet-wide cost defaults that individual `AIGatewayRoute.spec.llmRequestCosts` entries can override.
- **Preview: `QuotaPolicy` API (v1alpha1, no runtime enforcement yet)** — New CRD surface for declaring upstream-provider quota policies, laying the groundwork for quota-aware routing. Currently API-only — no controller reconciliation or enforcement is wired up. Track it for future releases; do not rely on it as a working feature today.

## 🐛 Bug Fixes

- **Webhook cache race during extProc injection** — Fixes a race where freshly applied AIGatewayRoute resources could miss extProc injection on first reconcile because the conversion webhook read from a stale cache. Scripted apply-then-curl tests should see fewer flakes.
- **Field ownership preserved on updates** — Controllers no longer claim ownership of fields they don't manage during updates. If you co-deploy the AI Gateway controller alongside other operators that touch adjacent fields (e.g. service mesh injectors, policy controllers), expect fewer reconcile churn loops on shared resources.
- **Orphan cleanup for MCPRoute backendrefs** — Resources tied to MCPRoute backend references are now cleaned up when the route or reference is removed, fixing a leak that could leave stale config in the cluster.
- **Standalone Envoy startup failures surfaced by `aigw`** — `aigw` now reports standalone Envoy startup failures cleanly instead of hanging or printing an unhelpful trace, making local dev and CI loops much faster to diagnose.
- **Bedrock Titan embeddings dataplane route** — Restored the Envoy route for Titan embeddings in dataplane tests so Titan workloads exercise the full pipeline.
- **Hardened bearer token parsing** — Malformed `Authorization: Bearer` headers used to panic the MCP subject extractor; they now return a clean auth failure and the request falls through to the standard auth failure path.
- **Request context propagation in `PostTranslateModify`** — Kubernetes client calls inside `PostTranslateModify` now honor request cancellation and deadlines, reducing stuck reconciles when the parent request is canceled.
- **Case-sensitive JSON marshalling and unmarshalling** — JSON encoding now consistently honors case, fixing subtle mismatches when round-tripping fields whose names differ only in case (visible previously as occasional 400s on certain provider payloads).
- **Secret rotation propagates to MCPRoute** — Updates to a Secret referenced by an `MCPBackendRef` are now reflected in the live configuration, matching how `BackendSecurityPolicy` already handled secret updates. Operators rotating MCP backend credentials no longer need to bounce the route.
- **MCP proxy handles compressed `Accept-Encoding` from upstreams** — The MCP proxy now correctly handles compressed `Accept-Encoding` values from upstream requests, fixing failures when MCP backends advertise gzip or other compression schemes.
- **`aigw` standalone accepts IP addresses for endpoints** — In standalone mode, `aigw` previously assumed endpoints were hostnames; you can now point OpenAI and MCP env config at IP addresses (e.g. `127.0.0.1`), making local dev against loopback addresses work.

# Envoy AI Gateway v0.5.0

Multi-gateway configuration, prompt caching cost savings, fine-grained MCP authorization, OpenAI Responses API, and Google Search grounding for Gemini.

Envoy AI Gateway v0.5.0 makes multi-gateway deployments easier with the new GatewayConfig CRD, cuts costs with prompt caching for AWS Bedrock and GCP Claude, and unlocks fine-grained access control with CEL-based MCP authorization. Developers gain OpenAI Responses API support, Google Search grounding for Gemini, and the ability to mutate request bodies per-route. Under the hood, the switch to sonic JSON processing reduces latency across all requests.

### MCP Gateway Enhancements

- **Fine-grained authorization with CEL, JWT claims, and external auth** — Write expressive CEL rules using request attributes (HTTP method, headers, JWT claims, tool names, call arguments), enforce access based on JWT claim values, or delegate to external gRPC/HTTP authorization services.
