# World of ClaudeCraft v0.40.1 Release Notes

**Release:** v0.40.1
**Date:** 2026-08-27
**Previous release:** v0.40.0

Version 0.40.1 is the patch release that carried the $WOC Exchange from a switched-off
feature to a live marketplace. It ships the operator and security surface the launch
checklist demanded: a settlement review ruling endpoint for operators, re-authorization
before a linked payout wallet can be changed or removed, the revised marketplace Terms
on the live pages, and a wallet status card at the top of the Exchange. Around the
launch, guild pledges become durable (a pledge now survives logout, and accepting an
offline pledger seats them into the guild), and two server performance defects
introduced in v0.40.0 are fixed: the account wealth sweep and the Exchange's mail
parcels both stopped round-tripping the entire realm mail book, removing multi-hundred
millisecond world-loop stalls that grew with mailbox size. The release takes seven pull
requests, 22 commits across 235 files.

The Exchange itself launched to production from this release line on August 26, ahead
of the tag: the operator arm, the Terms revision, and the wallet re-authorization gate
were already live for launch day and appear here as the versioned record.

## The $WOC Exchange

- **Operators can rule a parked settlement.** The overdue sweep parks a payment it
  cannot prove in review; a new dashboard-secret endpoint rules it paid (the delivery
  claim sweep resumes on its own) or unpaid (the settlement fails with a review
  provenance stamp and the refund path takes over). The ruling drives the same
  settlement state machine as the sweeps, distinguishes a lost operator race from a
  missing row, and stays available under a trading pause for incident work (#3642).
- **Changing your payout wallet now demands proof it is you.** Marketplace proceeds
  pay to the linked Solana wallet, so relinking to a different address or removing the
  link now requires the CURRENT wallet's co-signature, or the account password plus
  the second factor when one is enrolled, and every change sends a wallet-changed
  email. First links and same-wallet re-verifies stay prompt-free, and passwordless
  accounts are pointed at Set-a-Password instead of a dead end (#3651).
- **The Exchange shows your wallet standing up front.** The Claudium panel's Solana
  wallet card now sits above the Browse filters with the same per-state text and the
  same Connect, Verify and link, Reconnect, or Manage button, so a disconnected wallet
  is fixable without leaving for the store (#3664).
- **The marketplace Terms revision is live.** The revised Terms of Service and the
  marketplace risk disclosures are published to the live legal pages the client links
  to (#3646).

## Guilds

- **Pledges persist over logout, and accepting an offline pledger works.** Accepting a
  pledge used to delete the request and then attempt an online-only invite, so an
  offline pledger's request simply vanished. A pledge is now the player's standing
  request: it survives logout, accepting an offline pledger seats them directly into
  the guild (they find themselves in it on next login), an online accept keeps the
  familiar invite handshake with the pledge standing until the join, and declining the
  guild's invite withdraws the pledge. An officer's reject now also cancels any
  still-pending invite from an earlier accept, and the offline seat consumes the
  pledge in the same transaction, so a withdraw or decline racing the accept can never
  seat a player who just said no. Founding a guild clears the founder's standing
  pledge (#3656).

## Performance

- **The account wealth sweep no longer parses the mail book in Node.** The admin
  economy dashboard's per-account wealth totals refresh every 60 seconds; the escrow
  half used to ship every realm's whole mail and market blob into the server process
  and fold them there, a main-thread block of roughly 400 ms per minute against the
  production 89 MB mail row that the world loop paid as a stall. The totals are now
  aggregated inside Postgres under a bounded per-statement memory allowance, so the
  sweep's cost on the game process stays flat as the book grows, and the SQL is pinned
  byte-identical to the retired fold by a real-Postgres parity suite (#3661).
- **Booking an Exchange parcel costs the parcel, not the mail book.** Every delivered
  item, returned listing, and sold notice used to re-serialize and rewrite the entire
  realm mail blob, roughly 250 ms of main-thread time per parcel at production book
  size. A booked parcel now writes one durable row, still before its settlement
  advances; the parcel reaches the blob on the next scheduled book write, which
  removes the row in the same transaction, and a crash replays surviving rows through
  the existing book-once dedupe at boot. A persisted accounting watermark makes the
  replay provably safe across restarts and rollbacks, and residue is visible on the
  market ops readout and swept nightly (#3663).

## Under the hood

- The escrow aggregate's copper casts are CASE-armored against SQL qualifier
  reordering, so no stored blob value can abort the sweep whatever the planner does
  (#3661).
- The custody replay's rollback guard was upgraded from a timestamp comparison to a
  persisted per-realm watermark that only advances inside a committed book write and
  only after a completed boot merge, closing the last theoretical re-book window
  (#3663).
- The version bump moves package.json, a hashed leaf of the Fenbridge source
  fingerprint, so that GLB family was re-stamped in place (no visual change) with its
  dependent pins re-minted, the same recipe as previous hotfixes.

# World of ClaudeCraft v0.40.0 Release Notes

**Release:** v0.40.0
**Date:** 2026-08-25
**Previous release:** v0.39.3

Version 0.40.0 is an economy, community, and input release. The $WOC Exchange arrives: a
full player-to-player marketplace with auctions, buy-now listings, directed offers, bid
bonds, and mount and chroma trading, shipping in this build behind a launch switch that
stays off until the launch checklist completes. Around it, every town signpost becomes the
realm guild board with a new pledge system for finding a guild, controller support is
rebuilt around an FFXIV-style cross hotbar, the touch HUD is redesigned around thumb
reach, and a new GPU scheduler cuts the worst in-game freeze from 5.6 s to under half a
second. Warlocks become raid-viable, leveling-zone loot returns to classic rates, the
rogue stealth kit gets its long-owed pass, and the tutorial island learns to teach
controller players. The release takes 26 direct pull requests plus a 45-strong OSSBrain
community batch (#3524) into the release line, 1,158 commits across 2,456 files, and ships
fully localized across all 21 locales.

Hotfix content already shipped to production in v0.39.1 through v0.39.3 (the desktop
KTX2 texture policy fix and the Double Honor Weekend with its 12-hour early open) appears
in this version's history but is not new to this release.

## Highlights

- **The $WOC Exchange arrives.** A marketplace window for listing eligible items in $WOC:
  standard auctions with an optional hidden reserve, fixed-price buy-now listings, or
  both attached, plus direct player-to-player offers from the trade window. Every
  completed sale takes a 10% seller fee, split 90% to the seller, 3% burned, and 7% to
  the treasury. It ships in this build switched off, pending the launch checklist
  (#3606).
- **Every town signpost is now the realm guild board.** Interacting with any town
  noticeboard opens the Guild Signpost: guilds ranked by lifetime XP with recruiting
  status and the Guild Master's note, a click-through public roster, and a pledge system
  so an unguilded player can raise their hand to any recruiting guild (#3607).
- **Controller support, rebuilt.** Holding a trigger arms 8 cells and the right bumper
  swaps between two standing sets, 16 actions total with no accidental presses;
  auto-targeting, in-game layout arranging, and full d-pad window navigation come with it
  (#3501).
- **The touch HUD is redesigned around thumb reach.** The radial ring packs 4 buttons
  times 5 actions across 2 pages, consumables move into reach, a ten-item Quick Actions
  strip replaces the old button row, and a dedicated bar editor ends mid-combat
  rearrange accidents (#3554).
- **Freezes are dramatically shorter.** One GPU scheduler now paces every shader compile
  and texture upload: the worst single freeze in a measured production session drops
  from 5.6 s to 0.47 s, teleport landings go from 2.2 to 2.6 s of freeze down to 0.25 s
  or less, and teleport loading screens shrink by up to two thirds (#3519).
- **World entry is faster.** A representative populated entry drops from 23.7 s to
  16.0 s of loading with the initial GPU prewarm cut from 14.1 s to 3.7 s, and loading
  screens now rotate through 11 backdrops instead of one static image (#3582, #3232).
- **Warlocks are raid-viable.** All three specs land near the 200 DPS heroic contract
  (204.8 affliction, 207.0 destruction, 190.1 demonology, up from live parse tops of
  169.5, 132.8, and 131.3), while Enhancement and fire converge back onto the same
  contract from above (#3605, #3581, #3600).
- **Leveling loot returns to classic rates.** Fourteen normal mobs that dropped greens
  at 10 to 30% and blues at 4 to 8% per kill now sit at 2% and 0.2%, leaving rares,
  elites, bosses, and quest drops untouched (#3533).
- **The rogue stealth kit gets its pass.** Duskveil runs full speed under Skulduggery,
  Sap gets its own diminishing-returns ladder and no longer starts the fight, two new
  poisons land, pets are blind to stealth, and Vanish truly drops every attacker
  (#3323, #3609).
- **The 1-to-2-hour rift slowdown is fixed, and a wipe no longer costs the loot.**
  Server tick time on a busy rift realm drops from 5.80 ms to 4.53 ms mean, client GPU
  leaks are closed, and a won rift's portal now stays open for a 15-minute recovery
  window (#3557, #3569).
- **Fully localized.** The release fill closes all 9,825 pending rows across the 21
  locales, including the new sim emit strings, deed pages, and 22 reworded English lines
  whose translations had silently gone stale.

## The $WOC Exchange

- **Auctions, buy-now, or both.** Listings run 12, 24, or 48 hours, a bid inside the
  final two minutes extends the auction by two minutes up to a 30-minute cap, and a
  bought-out auction records the actual sale price (#3606).
- **Mounts and mech chromas are tradeable.** All eight rideable mounts and all fifteen
  mech chroma plates can be listed at every rarity through a rail that bypasses the
  equipment rarity floor (#3606).
- **Directed offers.** A seller can propose a $WOC sale to one named player from the
  trade window; the item only enters escrow once that player accepts (#3606).
- **Bid bonds and a strike ladder.** A bid posts a refundable bond (default 5%); a
  winner who fails to settle forfeits it and takes a strike, with progressively longer
  bidding suspensions for repeat non-payment (#3606).
- **Browse properly.** Weapon and armor category filters, an uncommon-to-rare quality
  range on top of the epic default, and a click-through seller history (#3606).
- **No two-factor prompt to bid or buy.** Both already require the buyer's own wallet
  signature, so the redundant TOTP step-up is gone; account login 2FA is unchanged
  (#3606).
- **Built custody-first.** Escrow is a currency-blind sim primitive with explicit
  soulbound and quest-item refusals, settlement and mail delivery share one database
  transaction so delivery is exactly-once across every crash point, and anything the
  system cannot prove is parked for operators instead of guessed at (#3606).
- **Admin economy oversight ships ahead of the launch.** Account search by character
  name, a materialized wealth total (purse plus mail and market escrow) behind a Top
  Holders board, and a persisted suspicion-flag workflow with a full audit trail
  (#3511).

## Guilds and community

- **Pledge to a guild without joining one.** A pledge renders on nameplates as "Pledge
  of {guild}", guild names colour by a five-step lifetime-XP tier ladder, and a
  five-minute per-character cooldown plus a day, week, forever rejection ladder keeps
  the system honest; any real invite from the guild wipes its rejections (#3607).
- **Officers get a Pledges tab.** A live pledge count in the social window, accept and
  decline per pledge, a recruitment settings editor, and a chat notification to online
  officers on every new pledge (#3607).
- **Board notes are filtered.** A Guild Master's note is refused at write time if it
  hits the chat filter's hard list and soft-masked like any other player text (#3607).
- **Moderation keeps up.** Bot-detector suspicion flags now write from the detector's
  actual decisions instead of a five-minute poll that over-counted occurrences by up to
  288x a day, and the admin wealth pane degrades gracefully instead of failing when a
  read times out (#3622, community contribution).

## New player experience

- **The tutorial island teaches controller players.** Controller glyph layouts are
  detected (or overridden), prompts render from live remaps, and the coach now teaches
  target selection, attacks, abilities, inventory, and death actions on gamepad (#3607).
- **The mobile coach speaks in buttons.** Coach steps are tappable, the whole path to
  an objective glows instead of one element, a stuck mobile veil is freed, and
  graduation no longer tears down the entire HUD on the way out (#3607).
- **The ferry lands properly.** Graduating the island lands the ferry at the harbor
  town with the loading screen held across the crossing, and "Welcome to Adventure"
  takes over as the island's music cue (#3607).

## Classes and combat

- **Warlock viability floors.** Affliction spell damage +7%, destruction +10%,
  demonology +10% plus pet damage +15%, with the Hex of Violence and Pyre Colossus
  tooltips updated to the new numbers (#3605).
- **The Warspirit convergence, tuned twice.** The first round brought Enhancement's top
  parses (up to 316 DPS, with 22 of 57 ranked parses over cap) down onto the 200 DPS
  contract and trimmed fire's Ignition mastery from 40% to 30% of crit damage; a
  follow-up softening then lifted Enhancement from 202.0 to 212.7 DPS after
  re-measurement showed it had landed below combat rogue and fire (#3581, #3600).
- **The Bonewrought mail set is shaman-legal.** The four tier-2 Strength mail pieces
  were mistakenly warrior and paladin only (#3581).
- **Courser's Guise has a real drawback.** Taking damage while it is active now dazes
  the hunter, halving movement speed for 4 seconds, closing the Pack Rally loophole in
  the same pass (#3608).
- **Beast Mastery pets deal their promised damage.** Unleashed Frenzy's +25% now
  reaches auto-attacks, bolts, cleave, and Fang Chorus, and pets inherit the owner's
  melee haste 1:1 (measured 154.975 to 157.6 DPS from the damage fix alone) (#3540).
- **Channeled damage no longer double-bursts on interruption.** A pushback-shortened
  channel deals proportionately less damage instead of force-firing every remaining
  tick at once; in the measured repro a clipped Consume dropped from 21 damage to the
  correct 7 (#3595).
- **Feared players stop grinding into walls.** A wall guard probes 2 yards ahead and
  steers to the most open direction; feared mobs keep their classic behavior (#3612).
- **The pet bar survives Graveguard's death**, falling back to a living Necromancy
  summon so Attack and Mode keep commanding them (#3515), and Improved Abyssal Gag's

- **Cheap Trick's Gut Punch button matches what it does**, reading the talent-resolved
  ability for both the bar slot and the tooltip (#3325).

## PvP and duels

- **Battleground enemies are targetable, and casting engages.** Enemy players and their
  pets no longer read as friendly on the client in Thornhollow Fields, and a hostile
  cast at a battleground enemy now starts auto-attack like it already did in duels and
  arenas (#3564, #3559).
- **Duels stop killing the winner's opponent after the bell.** A set proc, weapon proc,
  or riding dot can no longer land after the duel-ending blow and kill the 1-hp loser
  for real (#3601).
- **Battleground Unstuck keeps you in the match.** If no safe in-battleground spot
  exists it now fails cleanly instead of teleporting the player out to an overworld
  graveyard (#3524).

## Performance

- **One scheduler for all GPU preparation.** Main-thread time blocked by shader
  compiles in a 5-minute session falls from 1,104 ms across 47 programs to at most
  504 ms across 6, frames of 50 ms or more per minute of play fall from 28.6 to 4.2,
  and unattributable long frames drop from 407 of 520 to 12 of 514 (#3519).
- **Crowd stutter, cut.** Shared character materials stop rebuilding program parameters
  on alternating draws (430.9 down to 11.6 rebuilds per frame on a 20-player crowd),
  the worst weapon-skin freeze drops from 534.7 ms to 43.9 ms, and portrait capture
  moves off the main thread (#3531).
- **Entry does less before first paint.** Hidden catalog compilation, scenery texture
  uploads, and non-essential passes defer onto bounded post-entry lanes, and GPU upload
  volume during entry shrinks from 1,365.84 MiB to 954.94 MiB on the same capture
  (#3582).
- **Long rift sessions stay smooth.** Rift collision goes from a full scan to a cell
  index (resolvePosition 566 ns to 187 ns per op), prop teardown frees materials as
  well as geometry, and dead-instance corpses stop costing frames (#3557).
- **A file descriptor leak on aborted downloads is fixed**, about 95 leaked descriptors
  per hour in production before the fix (#3568).
- **Distant mobs stop sliding around frozen**, and trees with colliders stay rendered
  at every graphics tier instead of becoming invisible walls on Low (#3594, #3526).

## Controller, touch, and input

- **The cross hotbar in detail.** Auto-targeting picks the nearest attackable enemy
  under the same faction and opt-in rules the client already enforces, layouts arrange
  in place or straight from the spellbook, pad layouts are namespaced per character,

- **Touch accessibility.** The new Tap Menus setting makes every radial and strip

- **Space and Enter stop replaying your last click.** Three related focus bugs are

- **Drags no longer jam.** A bag rebuild mid-drag (loot, a vendor buy, a gather tick)

- **A build switch keeps your freed attack slot.** The ability on the freed first slot

# World of ClaudeCraft v0.39.3 Release Notes

**Release:** v0.39.3

Version 0.39.3 opens the Double Honor Weekend 12 hours earlier. The window
shipped in v0.39.2 opened at the Saturday 3 AM reset in realm time (US
Eastern), which is Saturday evening for players west of the date line: their
Saturday was nearly over before the event began. The window now opens Friday
3 PM realm time, Saturday 7 AM in New Zealand, so the event covers the entire
weekend on both sides of the date line.

## Changed

- **Double Honor now runs Friday 3 PM to Monday 3 AM realm time.** The open
  moved 12 hours earlier and the close is unchanged, so US players keep their
  Sunday evening and players across the date line gain their whole Saturday.
  Every Thornhollow Fields honor award (match results, kills, assists, and
  the first-win bonus) pays double for the full window, and a played-out loss
  or draw still pays the win base while it is open (#3558).

## Under the hood

- The sim stays clock-free: the hosts feed a second calendar key, the realm
  reset day probed 12 hours ahead, and the event opens when either key reads
  a weekend day. Daily rollovers (the first-win bonus, honor diminishing
  returns, the delve daily) are untouched, and headless, replay, and parity
  runs remain byte-identical.
- The server world loop memoizes its day-key derivation per minute, since it
  now derives two calendar keys per tick.

# World of ClaudeCraft v0.39.1 Release Notes

**Release:** v0.39.1
**Date:** 2026-08-20
**Previous release:** v0.39.0

Version 0.39.1 is a hotfix for the v0.39.0 desktop (Electron) build, which hung at
world entry. The desktop shell's Content Security Policy blocked the Zstandard
texture decoder's WASM bootstrap, so every zstd-supercompressed KTX2 model was
refused and world entry died. Web and native mobile builds were unaffected because
the desktop shell is the only host that ships a CSP.

## Fixes

- **Desktop world entry no longer hangs.** Three's ZSTDDecoder (the KTX2 Zstandard
  path taken by every UASTC normal and occlusion map) boots its WASM with a fetch of
  a data: URI, which is a connect-src request. The desktop CSP listed connect-src
  'self' blob: but not data:, so all 170 shipped GLBs carrying zstd-supercompressed
  textures (179 KTX2 images) were refused at ZSTDDecoder.init. The connect-src
  directive now allows data:, a self-contained inline scheme that opens no
  exfiltration path; img-src already listed it for the same embedded-texture reason
  (#3520).

## Under the hood

- Two CI guards make this class of break unshippable again: a decoder-contract test
  welds buildContentSecurityPolicy() to the vendored three decoder sources (every
  URL scheme the GLB decoder stack fetches must be allowed by connect-src, WASM
  stays instantiable without unsafe-eval, and data: stays off the executable
  directives), and a real-browser shell smoke drives offline world entry under the
  real packaged CSP and fails on any first-party violation (#3520).
- The version bump moves package.json, a hashed leaf of the Fenbridge source
  fingerprint, so that GLB family was re-stamped in place (byte sizes unchanged,
  no visual change) and the dependent test, evidence, and media manifest pins
  re-minted, the same recipe as the v0.38.x hotfixes.

# World of ClaudeCraft v0.38.4 Release Notes

**Release:** v0.38.4
**Date:** 2026-08-17
**Previous release:** v0.38.3

Version 0.38.4 is a hotfix for the delve wedge reported on production: under the
Restless Graves affix a run could become permanently uncompletable, and the broken
claim then followed the player through every relog because delve runs are keyed to
the durable character id.

## Fixes

- **Restless Graves risen can no longer break a delve run.** The affix raises a
  Bonewalker 3 seconds after each trash death, but killing the room's LAST trash
  opened and latched the exit portal inside that window, so the risen appeared
  behind an already-open portal. Worse, a spawn queued in one room survived the
  advance into the next: it rose in the old room but joined the new room's kill
  list, sealing that room's exit with an enemy the player could not reach. The
  portal now counts pending spawns as living trash (it opens normally once the
  risen are down), and a room's pending spawns are dropped when the party moves
  on, so neither half of the trap can occur (#3475, from #3471).
- **Wedged delve claims free themselves again.** An abandoned run is meant to
  free five minutes after everyone leaves, but the empty-run check watched a
  symmetric band around the run's origin that reached deep into the NEIGHBORING
  slot's rooms, so on a busy realm other groups running the same delve kept a
  wedged run claimed indefinitely (the reported character waited 20 minutes for
  nothing). The band now matches the real room footprint, so the five-minute
  clock runs whenever the run itself is empty, regardless of how busy the delve
  is (#3475, from #3471).

## Under the hood

- None of the three fixes adds or moves an rng draw, so loot draw order and the
  parity goldens are untouched; the new tests pin the portal race, the
  cross-room spawn drop, and the occupancy band from both sides of its margin.
- The version bump moves package.json, a hashed leaf of the Fenbridge source
  fingerprint, so that GLB family was re-stamped in place (byte sizes unchanged,
  no visual change) and the dependent test, evidence, and media manifest pins
  re-minted, the same recipe as v0.38.2 and v0.38.3.

Version 0.38.3 is a hotfix-scale release with three player-facing changes: it closes the

## Fixes

- **Resurrection can no longer bypass raid and heroic lockouts.** Lockouts are enforced at
  the dungeon door, but an accepted resurrection teleports the dead player to the caster,
  and the mass resurrections (Collective Reversal, Ancestors' Return, and the Sunmender's

  a caster standing inside a locked instance could raise a member dead anywhere in the
  world and pull them past the gate. Every player-cast resurrection now requires the dead
  ally's body to be within the casting spell's range (its authored range where one exists,
  a 40 yard ceiling for the mass sweeps; the Sunmender rite sweeps at its own 30) and in
  the caster's line of sight, checked when the cast starts, while it channels, and when it
  completes. Accepting an offer only delivers you to the caster while they are still
  within that reach of your body; otherwise you rise where the spell was cast, so a caster
  who zones into a locked instance during the offer window no longer ferries anyone in.
  The spell tooltips now state the limits (#3455).
- **The local character stays smooth through long render frames online.** Around every
  long frame the browser applies the snapshots queued during the block only afterwards, so
  the predictor's authoritative anchor froze and then swept several ticks at once: the
  display stalled for a frame or two, then rushed at up to twice run speed, sometimes
  stepping backward. An isolated long frame now opens a block episode in which the leash
  lends the ground the frozen anchor could not cover and the divergence servo sits out the
  burst sweep; steady low fps keeps its existing behaviour (#3453).

## Balance

- **Dungeon gold: farm nerfs and heroic finale bases.** Korzul the Gravewyrm's guaranteed
  gold base made the Sanctum a repeatable farm; it drops from 50000c to 15000c, and Zulgar

  nominal and the heroic Nythraxis raid finale pays 20g, rewarding the daily-lockout clear
  rather than the repeatable route. The Dungeon Finder preview now advertises the heroic
  base on heroic finales instead of understating it by 6.7x to 40x (#3454).

## Under the hood

- The heroic finale gold substitutes its raised base on the same single rng draw the
  normal roll uses, so loot draw order and the parity goldens are untouched (#3454).
- The accepted-resurrection arrival rule is now one shared function, used by both the
  live accept and the Nythraxis transition-stun prediction, so the encounter can never
  predict a landing the accept will not honor (#3455).
- The version bump moves package.json, a hashed leaf of the Fenbridge source
  fingerprint, so that GLB family was re-stamped in place (byte sizes unchanged, no

# World of ClaudeCraft v0.38.2 Release Notes

**Release:** v0.38.2
**Date:** 2026-08-16
**Previous release:** v0.38.1

Version 0.38.2 is a hotfix for two player-facing breaks: the Nythraxis arena wardstones
have been invisible to most raiders since v0.38.0, which made the Deathless Rage channel
impossible to counter and wiped the raid, and the composer high and ultra graphics tiers
rendered a fully black frame on ANGLE's OpenGL backend (Linux + NVIDIA + Chrome) after
the Three.js r185 upgrade.

## Fixes

- **The Nythraxis arena wardstones are visible to every raider again.** The v0.38.0
  quest-collectable display gate hides a collectable whose quest is not active on the
  viewer's log, and the three arena wardstones reuse the Sunken Bastion quest item
  (`bastion_ward_stone`, a collect objective of the zone 2 quest), so any raider who had
  finished, or never taken, that quest lost all three: no model, no minimap mark, no
  interact target, and Deathless Rage could not be channeled against. Only a player
  mid-way through the Bastion quest still saw them, which is why it survived a quick
  check. A dungeon can now declare a placed object an interact-only encounter mechanic
  (`interactOnly`), and the gate reads that off the instance the object stands in, so
  the raid keeps its wards while the overworld pickup keeps its collectable behaviour
  and the crypt relics stay quest-gated (#3433).
- **The composer high and ultra tiers no longer black out on ANGLE's OpenGL backend**
  (Linux + NVIDIA + Chrome, a r165 to r185 regression). Two arms. On grass tufts and
  grazing building edges the interpolated vertex normal underflows to zero, so the
  engine's stock `normalize(vNormal)` emits NaN, which poisons both cube_uv IBL inputs;
  the engine patch resets a degenerate normal to a valid unit vector, a no-op for every
  finite normal. And the output grade pass now scrubs NaN from both of its beauty reads
  before the tonemap, because the bloom blur smeared a single NaN pixel frame-wide and
  tonemapped the whole frame to black; the UNSIGNED_BYTE low and medium tiers clamp it
  away, which is why only high and ultra went dark (#3426).

## Under the hood

- The engine fix lands in `patches/three@0.185.1.patch`, which moves `pnpm-lock.yaml`, a
  hashed leaf in the source fingerprint of the Eastbrook-era GLB families. A re-export is
  not viable (those assets ship KTX2), so the embedded fingerprint was swapped in place

- New coverage pins the arena wardstones as interact-only in the dungeon content, the

- No balance, content-tuning, schema, or data-migration changes. No strings moved.

## Upgrade notes

Standard server plus client deploy, no migrations. The wardstone fix needs both sides on

# World of ClaudeCraft v0.38.1 Release Notes

**Release:** v0.38.1
**Date:** 2026-08-15
**Previous release:** v0.38.0

Version 0.38.1 is a hotfix for two things the Three.js r185 upgrade and the CI sharding work
left behind in v0.38.0: the chase camera aimed from a stale pose while you turned, and the
Docker image could not build at all, which made v0.38.0 undeployable to every environment.

## Fixes

- **The camera aims where you are, not where you were.** r185 gates a node's own
  `matrixWorld` compose on `matrixWorldAutoUpdate` (r165 composed unconditionally) while still
  clearing the dirty bit, and `Object3D.lookAt` reads its eye position out of `matrixWorld`
  rather than `.position`. The renderer freezes the camera, so setting the position and then
  calling a bare `lookAt` aimed from the pose the previous refresh had baked. Standing still
  that was invisible, but a turn orbited the camera every frame, so v0.38.0 shipped the avatar
  sitting off screen centre for the whole turn, by one frame of turn (about 3 degrees at 60 fps
  at the PI rad/s turn speed, and proportionally worse as the frame rate drops). Both aim sites
  now hold the flag across the aim so the new position composes first (#3420).
- **The Docker image builds again.** `vite.config.ts` imports the vitest sharding sequencer at
  module scope, but `.dockerignore` excludes `scripts/*` behind a hand-maintained allowlist that
  the sequencer never joined, so every image build died loading its own config with
  `[UNRESOLVED_IMPORT] Could not resolve './scripts/ci_balanced_sequencer.mjs'`. The sequencer
  and the two files it pulls in, the shard partitioner and the measured-weights JSON, are now in
  the build context (#3419).

## Under the hood

- The image-context break was the second of its kind in a week (#3353 was the same failure for
  `build_bundle_pregen.mjs`), because CI builds with the whole repo present and never exercises
  the `.dockerignore` filter, and the existing coverage is per-file string pins that a newly
  added import has no reason to acquire. A new guard walks `vite.config.ts`'s own transitive
  relative imports and fails naming any the filter would drop, so the class fails at review
  instead of at deploy (#3419).
- New coverage pins the frozen-camera aim contract directly, so a future engine bump that
  changes matrix-compose semantics fails a test rather than shipping an off-centre avatar
  (#3420).
- No balance, content, or data-migration changes. Full parity across all 21 locales; no strings
  moved.

## Upgrade notes

v0.38.0 cannot build a deployable image. Deploy 0.38.1 rather than 0.38.0, on every environment.

# World of ClaudeCraft v0.38.0 Release Notes

**Release:** v0.38.0
**Date:** 2026-08-15
**Previous release:** v0.37.1

Version 0.38.0 is a tanking, tooling, and desktop release. Every tank spec was re-tuned
against measured threat and survivability parses until all four sit within 17% of each
other, Bruin Form gets its missing heal and its first area taunt, and Wolf Form finally
swings on the classic beat. The desktop client is rebuilt on the Three.js r185 train with
real window memory, Discord Rich Presence, native notifications, and a GPU rescue hatch.
Operators get the Cheater mark, a power-neutral public sanction that burns played time
rather than wall-clock time. Around that, the World Market gets a redesign and a
lowest-price view, the map draws real instance floor plans, nights become readable, and a
long run of GPU hitch work takes a 950 ms stall down to 13 ms. The release spans 603
commits and 48 pull requests across 1,696 files, and ships fully localized across all 21
locales.

## Highlights

- **All four tanks within 17% of each other.** Faithwarden paladins were generating 2.6x
  every other tank's threat on live 0.37.1 parses (447 TPS against warrior 173, Wildfang
  bear 101, Warspirit Stonebound 171). A full re-tune lands the paladin at 292 TPS with
  the field closed up (#3405).
- **Bruin Form is a real tank kit again.** Savage Mending, an in-form heal that was built
  but never granted by any talent row, is live, and Baleful Roar gives the form its first
  area taunt (#3411).
- **Wolf Form swings on the classic beat.** Feral autos move from the rogue's borrowed
  1.8 sec cadence to a fixed 1.0 sec paw speed, with the weapon roll rescaled so white
  damage tracks the weapon's authored DPS at any speed (#3414).
- **The desktop client, rebuilt.** Three.js r185, window and display memory, Discord Rich
  Presence, native OS notifications, a borderless or windowed display mode, and a
  dedicated-GPU toggle with a no-boot escape hatch (#3406).
- **The Cheater mark.** A public, undispellable, power-neutral sanction that burns a
  budget of played seconds, so it cannot be waited out logged off or escaped on an alt
  (#3322, #3348, #3349, #3350).
- **A 950 ms stall, gone.** A budgeted light inside a group whose visibility toggled each
  frame was forcing a synchronous relink of every material on screen. Measured over 90 s
  with 20 geared players: live stall cost 950 ms to 13 ms, and world entry 44.6 s to
  27.2 s (#3368).
- **Readable nights.** Moonlight and sky-bounce ambient are tuned separately so terrain
  stays legible off the lit roads, moon phase drives brightness, and the full cycle runs
  45 minutes instead of 20 (#3373).
- **The map draws the actual room.** Rift and Delve maps render the authored floor plan
  from the same generator that builds the instance, and every marker family got curated
  art with real states (#3369).
- **A smarter World Market.** A Browse toggle collapses to the lowest price per item
  server-side, and the Sell tab shows the going rate before you list (#3376, #3315,
  #3333).
- **Ranked arena losers finally earn something.** A loss, and both sides of a draw, now
  pay a third of the win award on the same daily taper (#3408).
- **Fully localized.** All 21 locales ship with zero pending rows across 12,805 keys.

## Combat, classes, and content

- **Tank threat brought into line.** The warrior and bear signatures moved from flat
  threat adds to multiplicative threat with flat floors, the paladin's triple threat stack
  was trimmed (Burning Oath 1.6 to 1.3, per-ability multipliers cut across the Protection
  kit, Oathward mastery 50% to 40%), and Ironguard's Recompense mastery threat rose 30% to
  80% to compensate (#3405).
- **Bear Form reclaims the classic big-pool identity.** Max health rises 15% to 30%,
  funded by trimming the form's armor multiplier from 2.3x to 2.1x, so Wildfang stays
  tanky through raw HP rather than pure armor (#3405).
- **Stonebound gets a real health budget.** The Warspirit shaman's tank posture gained a
  20% Stamina buff it never had, armor rose 30% to 40%, damage reduction 10% to 15%, and
  its threat multiplier rose 2x to 2.5x. Its effective-health ceiling against a protection
  warrior moved from 0.8x to 0.9x, an explicit owner call, letting it tank heroic
  Nythraxis without one-shotting (#3405).
- **Savage Mending and Baleful Roar.** Savage Mending heals 180 health over 10 sec on a
  60 sec cooldown. Baleful Roar forces every enemy within 10 yards to attack the druid for
  3 sec, mirroring the warrior's Defiant Bellow, on a 60 sec cooldown for 10 rage (#3411).
- **Wolf Form damage neutrality.** A single 1.22x constant keeps the bench within about 2%
  of pre-change numbers across the cadence change, specials included (#3414).
- **Ranked arena loss Honor.** 1v1 and 2v2 losses, and draws, pay 8 and 17 Honor
  respectively, a third of the win award, on the same per-opponent daily taper, so trading
  wins back and forth still caps at one win plus one loss per pairing per day (#3408).
- **Pets can crit committed tanks in PvP again.** Tank crit immunity was enforced on the
  shared mob-swing path that player pets also use, so a hostile player's pet could never
  critically strike a committed protection warrior, Faithwarden paladin, or Wildfang bear.
  The rule is now keyed on the attacker as well as the target (#3382).
- **Grix the Tunnelking is no longer a three-hour ghost.** The Zone 1 miniboss now
  respawns 15 to 30 minutes after each kill, re-derived from Zone 1's own rare ladder (4x
  for Mogger and Old Greyjaw up to 432x for Wraithbinder Maldrec) rather than asserted. He
  stays rarer than the plain rares, while a zone visit now sees him two to four times
  (#3361).
- **Delve bonus Marks stop outrunning the shop.** The premium lockpick chest (+2 Marks)
  and Drowned Litany rite (+4) used to pay on every clear all day, past the 6 to 8 Marks
  per day the shop is priced against. Both now only ride a clear inside the existing
  first-three-clears daily window, and pay only the party members that clear actually
  credited. The copper bonus and loot tier are untouched (#3397).
- **A death mid-channel no longer poisons your next cast.** Dying during a channel, most
  visibly the Nythraxis wardstone force-channel, left the channeling flag stuck true on
  the corpse, so the next hard cast after resurrecting ran the channel-tick branch every
  sim tick for the whole cast bar, spiking damage 4 to 9k on the opener (#3404).
- **Combat rogue re-banded.** Thuggery was parsing roughly 240 DPS on the heroic Nythraxis
  check against Knifework's 189 and Skulduggery's 179. Trimming its attack-power and
  melee-damage baselines (apPct 0.55 to 0.20, meleeDmgPct 0.36 to 0.16) lands it at about
  200 DPS, the top of the shared 150 to 200 band, leaving the other two untouched (#3352).
- **Chronomancy gets its capped healing back.** The mage healer spec was missing its level
  20 healing ranks entirely. Temporal Mend gains a rank 4 (218 to 258 healing for 110
  mana) and Temporal Barrier a rank 4 (232 absorb for 120 mana), landing Chronomancy's HPS
  at about 175, beside Heal and Holy Light at level 20. A follow-up pinned Aether Surge's
  mana cost at the derived 14 across every rank, after a prior merge silently reverted it
  to 16 above level 10 (#2786).
- **Cheap Trick actually frees Gut Punch.** The rogue talent that lifts Gut Punch's stealth
  requirement was honored by the sim's cast gate but not by the action bar or tooltip,
  which kept painting the button unusable and printing "Requires stealth" even though the
  cast went through. Both surfaces now read the resolved ability, and a companion sim fix
  carries the cleared requirement through ability-replacement swaps so it cannot silently
  reattach (#3358).
- **The training dummy stays put.** Beyond the paladin's Oath Chain, warlock pet
  Gloomshade's Abyssal Chain and the Abyssal Rift pull could still drag the Highwatch
  training dummy off its marker. All three relocation sites now share one eligibility
  check (#3338).

## Moderation

- **The Cheater mark is a played-time sanction, not a wall-clock one.** An operator can
  brand an account with a public Cheater tag that burns down a budget of played seconds,
  up to 100 hours, so it cannot be waited out by staying logged off. It is account-scoped,
  so every character wears it and rolling an alt does not escape it (#3322, #3348).
- **Power-neutral by construction.** The mark rides a mechanically inert aura kind with
  value 0 and no arm in the stat fold. It changes no stat, cooldown, or combat outcome,
  and a whole-entity-minus-auras test pins that a marked and an unmarked character resolve
  identically (#3322).
- **It cannot be shed.** Two independent guards keep it on the wearer: the aura is
  undispellable, and it carries the physical school, which the dispel check refuses
  outright regardless of that flag. Only the countdown reaching zero, or an operator lift,
  clears it (#3322).
- **Survives everything a player controls, but pauses while dead.** Death, every respawn
  path, arena entry, and a Fiesta down all preserve the mark, even though arena and Fiesta
  otherwise strip every other aura for a clean competitive slate. The budget only burns
  while the character is alive in world, so a parked corpse serves no sanction time
  (#3322).
- **Off party and raid frames on purpose.** Those frames cap how many auras they draw, so
  showing the tag there could push a real, dispellable debuff off a marked player's healer.
  That is an information handicap the power-neutral rule forbids, so the tag renders on the
  nameplate, the target frame, and the personal debuff bar only (#3322, #3349).
- **Rendering is player-gated.** If the flag ever ended up on a mob it brands nothing, so a
  moderation verdict can never land somewhere no operator could lift it (#3349).
- **A coded admin API with explicit refusals.** Apply, re-length, and lift all require an
  audited reason and return stable `cheater_mark.*` codes instead of prose: a blank reason
  (`reason_required`), a non-positive or invalid budget (`invalid_duration`), lifting an
  unmarked account (`not_marked`), a mistyped or purged account id (`no_account`), and
  marking an operator's own account (`admin_target`), which is refused outright (#3348).
- **Re-lengthening a live mark is one action, not two.** Correcting a mistaken duration
  used to require a lift plus a re-apply, which wrote two audit rows and briefly dropped
  the public tag. It is now a single audited action and the tag never flickers off (#3350).
- **The account moderation panel.** A dedicated section on the account detail view shows
  the live reason, remaining played time, and when it was applied, behind the shared
  confirm-and-reason prompt. It is hidden outright for admin accounts, matching the
  server-side refusal (#3350).
- **Fully localized, operators included.** Every mark label, dialog, and error string is a
  translated key, down to a post-ship fix for an inconsistent Danish compound term after an
  independent language review (#3348, #3350).

## Desktop client and the r185 render train

- **Three.js r185.** The renderer moves from three 0.165.0 to 0.185.1, postprocessing to
  6.39.4, and n8ao to 2.0.0. Real behavior changes came with it and were fixed in the same
  pass: r185 gates a node's own matrix compose on `matrixWorldAutoUpdate` where the flag
  previously only affected children, which had silently frozen the chase camera, editor
  free-cam, screen shake, and screenshot camera at their construction pose; a deprecated
  GLSL alias used by the night sky's light-splat shader was swapped for its canonical
  replacement; and the shader-compile prewarm cache was re-keyed to r185's new program
  parameters (#3406).
- **Discord Rich Presence.** A new in-house IPC client shows your zone and game identity as
  your Discord activity, on by default now that the official application id ships baked
  into the build. It connects lazily after the window opens, retries with jittered backoff
  up to 60 seconds, and clears your activity when you go idle or turn it off. The Options
  note discloses that your zone and elapsed session time are shown, and that anyone who can
  see your Discord profile can see both (#3406).
- **Display mode.** A new Options row offers Borderless or Windowed instead of the old
  browser-style fullscreen toggle, which fought the shell's own window mode. Borderless is
  the default (#3406).
- **Window memory.** The client remembers size, position, maximized state, and which
  display you were on, and restores it on the next launch with no flash of an unpainted or
  wrong-sized frame. A saved display that is gone or off-screen falls back to centered
  (#3406).
- **GPU controls, with a rescue path.** Windows and Linux players on hybrid-GPU laptops get
  an opt-out for the forced discrete-GPU preference (Options, "Use the Dedicated Gaming
  GPU", on by default). If a machine cannot boot at all because of it, launching with
  `WOC_DISABLE_GPU_FORCE=1` skips both GPU levers for that one launch without touching the
  saved setting, so you can get far enough in to flip the toggle off for good (#3406).
- **A GPU status toast.** Running on software rendering, or with your discrete GPU
  inactive, now surfaces a one-time toast naming the problem, remembered per verdict so it
  will not re-nag once dismissed but reappears if a new issue shows up (#3406).
- **Native OS notifications.** Real OS-level toasts, rate-limited to one per kind per 10
  seconds and capped at 50 per session, with a click focusing the window. Linux
  notification text is escaped so a hostile string cannot inject markup into KDE, dunst, or
  xfce4-notifyd (#3406).
- **Stay-awake during controller play.** Gamepad-only sessions no longer let the display
  sleep, since controller input does not reset the OS idle timer (#3406).
- **Faster, quieter startup.** The window stays hidden until first paint, with a 4-second
  safety fallback so a stuck renderer cannot leave you windowless. A second launch focuses
  the existing window instead of appearing to do nothing, the application menu is stripped
  before the first window paints on Windows and Linux, and Chromium persists compiled
  bytecode for the bundled scripts across launches to cut cold-start time (#3406).
- **Hardened local storage.** The preferences file is written atomically through an
  exclusive temp file and fsynced before the rename, a hand-edited file with a stray BOM or
  garbage in an unrelated field still loads, and the loader refuses to treat a symlink,
  FIFO, or device node at the prefs path as a real file (#3406).
- **The mobile OTA overlay lost its cancel action.** Downloading an update now blocks play
  rather than letting you skip ahead onto a bundle version headed for a compatibility dead
  end (#3377).
- **The update-ready card links to what changed.** The toast shown after a new build
  finishes downloading now opens these release notes in your system browser (#3406).
- **The desktop download version cannot drift again.** The download page's version is
  derived from the package version at build time instead of being hand-bumped, so a release
  can no longer ship links pointing at a stale installer (#3406).

## Client performance

- **A budgeted light can no longer freeze a scene-wide relink.** Three bakes light counts
  into every material's program cache key, so a light that becomes visible before the
  budget has ranked it forces a synchronous relink of every material drawn that frame. The
  jail moderator gate was the live case. Adoption is now one seam that hides the light and
  dirties the rank together. Measured over 90 s with 20 geared players: live stall cost 950
  ms to 13 ms, cover-phase cost 17.2 s to 0.52 s, world entry 44.6 s to 27.2 s, with the
  visible count constant across 5,504 consecutive frames (#3368).
- **No more first-cast freeze in the Nythraxis arena.** Soul Rend's shader variants are
  prewarmed off-screen at arena entry. Measured with six geared players, the mark used to
  link 32 programs and stall the GPU driver submit for 571 ms inside a single frame.
  Warming ahead of time takes that to zero links, and a follow-up closed the last gap so
  shapeshifted bodies inherit the warmed variant too (#3407).
- **Fewer background stutters while shaders compile.** Shader-readiness polling used to
  re-query the GPU once per material even when several materials shared one in-flight
  program. Deduping to one check per program per pass measured 18% fewer queries and 27%
  less distributed poll cost per login in a live production A/B (#3345).
- **Compile pressure paces itself.** An adaptive controller is now the shipping default: it
  admits shader-compile work against a window sized on observed link times, growing after
  fast settlements and backing off after slow ones or failures, in place of fixed
  submission (#3368).
- **The Store stopped taxing every login.** Pre-warming the Armory preview catalog cost
  about 2.1 to 2.6 seconds of live-frame hitches every online session, for a window only
  some players open, and its own reporting understated that by a factor of 20 to 50. It now
  builds when you inspect a card instead. A warm-on-store-open alternative was tried and
  measured negligible (530.9 ms against 522.8 ms on a cold open) before being dropped
  (#3401).
- **Minimizing the desktop client stops burning GPU.** A hidden or minimized window fully
  skips GL submission, HUD paint, and perf sampling, and the zone-warm background lane
  pauses too. The sim tick and network keep running, so refocusing resumes with no backlog
  freeze (#3406).
- **Auto-scaling quality no longer sticks degraded.** After a demanding fight forced render
  resolution and world-dressing density down to protect frame rate, they could stay low
  once things calmed. Recovery now restores baseline resolution and density before quality
  is allowed to climb again (#3406).
- **The Low preset is finally lighter than Medium.** Plain Low had been rendering more than
  Medium on five axes at once, and a town scene measured 4.52 million triangles at Low
  against Medium's 3.55 million. Low is now derived from Medium by monotone scaling so it
  can only shed further, and the extra grass-card density is gated to genuinely weak or
  software-rendered GPUs. This is cosmetic density only: no gameplay information moves
  between tiers (#3406).

## Visuals and the world

- **Readable moon-lit nights, and a longer cycle.** Wilderness night used to read as a
  near-black cutout because one light drove both the sky-bounce ambient and the moon's key
  light off the same floor. The two are tuned separately now, so terrain and silhouettes
  stay legible off the lit roads while night still feels genuinely dark, with real contrast
  and long moon shadows. Moon phase drives that brightness, a full moon lifting it and a
  new moon settling toward the darkest still-navigable night, and the full cycle runs 45
  minutes instead of 20 (#3373). A follow-up kept distant snow caps and rim rock from
  glowing under the brighter ambient floor.
- **Grix and the Deeprock Diggers stopped freezing mid-hit.** Both were sharing a goblin
  rig's hit-reaction clip that bound to zero bones on their own skeletons, freezing them
  mid-pose like a statue on every hit taken. Grix's hit reaction is empty until one is
  authored for his rig, the Diggers keep their native reaction, Grix's swing now lands its
  hit near the moment your health bar moves instead of well after, and both mobs' feet
  plant on the ground instead of floating (#3379).
- **Quest collectables only appear once you are on the quest.** Sparkle crates, sigils,
  ledger pages and similar pickups used to sit in the world for everyone, so a player
  without the quest could walk up to a glowing item the game would then refuse to hand
  over. They now appear only while their quest is active or ready to turn in, and clear on
  turn-in or abandon. Interact-only scenery like huts and monuments is unaffected (#3359).
- **Heal glow no longer misfires on allies stepping back into view.** A heal landing on a
  target with nothing on screen was still starting the shared glow throttle, which could
  silently swallow the next heal glow once that ally came back into sight.
- **The r185 upgrade is meant to be invisible.** Post-processing (bloom, ambient occlusion,
  tone mapping) was rebuilt against the new three.js and n8ao to reproduce the old output
  rather than adopt the libraries' new defaults (#3406).

## Map and interface

- **Every marker family got real art and real states.** Gathering nodes, dungeon and delve
  entrances and exits, crafting stations, mailboxes, noticeboards, quest markers, and Rift
  and Delve rewards now render from curated, reviewed art instead of generic dots, with
  ready, cooldown, and tool-locked states baked into the icon, and reward markers carrying
  locked, active, opened, jammed, or bountiful (#3369).
- **Rift and Delve maps stop lying about the room.** Both the minimap and the full map for
  instanced content draw the actual authored floor plan, walls, pillars, tombs, platforms
  and ramps, pulled from the same generator that builds the real instance (#3369).
- **The map talks back to screen readers.** A hidden marker summary describes what is
  visible by kind, direction, and distance, groups crowded clusters instead of reading
  every marker, and re-localizes if you switch languages mid-session (#3369).
- **Mobile map layout.** On a wide landscape phone the map and quest log sit side by side
  instead of the quest sheet squeezing the map down, and every map control keeps a 40px
  touch floor at any UI scale (#3369).
- **Marker priority is well defined.** Quest glyphs win over navigation, station, service,
  and gather markers on overlap, and touch taps use a wider hit radius than a mouse hover
  (#3369).
- **Your look is a shareable code.** The character creator gained a Share tab: every
  customizable feature serializes into one versioned code you can copy or paste back in. A
  bad paste reports which field failed instead of silently misreading it, and importing a
  code never touches your current body proportions (#3381).
- **Tooltip and notification corrections.** The Temporal Echo tooltip's group-heal
  percentage now reads the same constant the sim uses instead of a stale hardcoded number,
  and the Japanese party-invite toast once again names who sent the invite instead of
  reading as an ambiguous ellipsis.

## World Market, server, and data

**World Market and economy**

- **Listing redesign.** Browse rows are denser and calmer: armor class shows as small
  weight pips on the item icon instead of a text pill, heroic items get a gold corner star,
  item name and seller sit on one compact line, and prices read gold-first with a copper
  trim. Buy, Reclaim, List, and Collect All move to the shared forged-button treatment, and
  rare and epic name colors were retuned after the originals failed WCAG AA on the panel
  (#3376).
- **Find the cheapest listing.** A Browse toggle collapses the list to the lowest price per
  item, tie-broken by the older listing. The collapse runs server-side so it narrows the
  whole market rather than one page, and your own listings always show in full regardless
  of the toggle (#3315).
- **Check the going rate before you sell.** The Sell tab shows the current lowest active
  listing for the item in hand, or states plainly that none exist. A follow-up aligned its
  rounding on indivisible stacks with what Browse shows (#3333).

**Server, networking, and data**

- **Signup captures ad-click attribution, with an explicit opt-in.** The client stores the
  first ad click's context (Facebook click id, UTM tags, landing URL, referrer) plus a
  visitor id and chosen language, and sends it with registration. The register form on both
  entry points adds a marketing-communications opt-in checkbox that is never pre-ticked
  (#3374).
- **Attribution is persisted server-side.** A new `account_attribution` table stores one
  first-touch row per account, merging the client-sent data with the Meta `_fbp` and `_fbc`
  cookies the server already read at signup, and stamps locale, country from a trusted edge
  geo header, and the marketing opt-in choice. The row is deleted if the account is later
  deactivated (#3374).
- **New onboarding event logs.** `level_up_events` mirrors every level-up; `ftue_events`
  mirrors quest accepts, turn-ins, and player deaths (with level, zone, and killer) for
  characters between level 1 and 10. Both are append-only and pruned nightly, level-up
  events after 365 days by default and FTUE events after 90 (#3374).
- **Conversion events sent to Meta.** The server reports a faster `ReachedLevel2`
  conversion alongside the existing `ReachedLevel5`, plus a one-time `D7Retained` fired on
  an account's first session in its seventh day. Conversions carry the signup email as a
  SHA-256 hash for match quality. All of it stays inert unless a Meta CAPI access token is
  configured (#3374).
- **Ad-spend ledger.** Admins can hand-enter daily spend and delivery counts per campaign,
  in integer cents, so cost per install, cost per level 5, and cost per retained player
  become computable. Reads ride the existing `analytics.read` permission; writes require a
  stricter `analytics.manage`, so viewer-tier staff can see spend but never edit it. A
  follow-up mounted these routes on the shared admin auth gate after they had briefly built
  their own (#3374).
- **Hardening on the new instrumentation.** Follow-ups bound every client-drivable event
  path with per-character death caps and depth-limited queues, gate all Meta CAPI work
  behind the enabled check so an unconfigured deployment cannot burn the once-per-account
  D7 guard, cap and strip the Meta cookies before storage, and add the new attribution and
  event data to the account data-export tool (#3374).
- **Rift forge exploit rollback.** A one-off server migration reverses the rift forge wire
  exploit closed in v0.37.0: it resets upgrade level, enchants, and gems on every forged
  item across inventory, bank, buyback, and both equipment slots, refunds the essence the
  forge ladder consumed, and returns socketed gems as items. It is one-off by contract, a
  completion marker refuses a second run, and a follow-up hardened it to serialize on one
  database client, reject scoped writes, require a drained maintenance window, and
  compare-and-swap character state before applying (#3354).
- **Steadier play on congested or shared connections.** Input sends are shed once the local
  WebSocket buffer backs up instead of queuing without bound, which previously delayed the
  keepalive pong and caused rubber-banding and reconnect loops when two players shared one

## Build, CI, and quality

- **Sharding by measured weight.** PR test shards pack by real per-file duration through a
  balanced LPT sequencer instead of vitest's sha1-contiguous slice, which had let shard 4
  dominate every sampled selective run. Measured against a 2,720-file harvest, weighted
  packing lands a 9.79 minute worst shard with 0.06 minutes of spread against 10.49 minutes
  contiguous (#3396).
- **One collection instead of two.** The selective gate's floor and related legs merged
  into a single vitest invocation (#3378), then split by platform behind a pure leg
  planner: POSIX runs one merged run, Windows keeps the classic split because vitest
  4.1.10 does not slash-normalize related seeds there (#3394).
- **Blobless sparse checkout.** `docs/screenshots` was 794 MB of committed PR evidence, and
  a measured lane had spent 11m21s fetching before an 8m25s test step. The five sparse test
  jobs now check out everything except screenshot directories, with the re-include list
  scraped from the git index rather than hand-curated, skipping about 380 MB per job
  (#3380).
- **CI bounds re-derived from measured, mode-labeled walls.** pr-gate dropped from 40 to 37
  minutes off a measured selective worst of 16.55 minutes, the long-sims lanes moved 30 to
  28, and release-gate 35 to 36. The merge queue's required critical path is now welded to
  the bounds table by an executable pin proving it stays under the 90 minute queue ceiling
  (#3384).
- **Worker count held at half cores.** A measured 3-worker trial on the 4-vCPU PR runners
  bought at most about a minute of wall time but blew default timeouts on three unrelated
  suites under contention, so the half-cores default stands, now behind a validated
  `WOC_TEST_WORKERS` resolver (#3383).
- **Freshness-guarding the SFX, guide, and media manifests.** These three committed,
  generated manifests were the last regeneration surface forcing full-mode CI through the
  unclassified catch-all. Each regenerates in well under a second, so they join the i18n
  arm's freshness-guarded family and feed `vitest related` as graph nodes, selecting 248
  consumer suites instead of the whole tree (#3386).
- **A duration-budget ratchet against silent lane drift.** Declared vitest timeout growth
  is now a red diff at review time: the owned-class balance harness had reached 788 to 842
  seconds as one file and the warlock sustain suite had drifted to 359 seconds with nothing
  flagging it (#3375).
- **Check-context rename, with a real merge hazard.** All fourteen required check names
  moved to a clean scheme (`Classify changes`, `PR tests (1)` through `(8)`, `PR long sims
  A` and `B`, `PR checks`, `Lint (changed files)`, `Browser tests`, and the release lanes).
  Because branch protection matches exact context strings, the ruleset must swap old names
  for new at the same moment this lands, and any PR opened before the flip needs a base
  update to report under contexts that will otherwise never appear again (#3387).
- **One-command release mint.** The merge-queue ruleset's include stayed pinned to
  `release/v0.35.0` from the v0.36.0 mint until 2026-08-14, quietly leaving the queue with
  nothing to queue against for three consecutive releases. `scripts/release_mint.mjs` now
  does the swap as one audited local command: it dumps before and after state, refuses to
  narrow the required-checks glob, and rewrites the merge-queue include to exactly `main`
  plus the new release ref (#3388).
- **Local gate concurrency lock.** `npm run gate` serializes the full-suite vitest step
  across concurrent local gate runs via an advisory lock (closes #2808). A review then
  caught a double-reclaim race where two waiters could both act on the same stale lock; the
  fix re-reads the lock file immediately before unlinking, and ownership moved to a
  kernel-owned loopback listener for atomic ownership and crash recovery.
- **The pre-merge gate now actually starts on Windows.** `gate_select`, `gate_shadow`, and
  `ci:changed` all routed their `git rev-parse ref^{commit}` base probes through `cmd.exe`,
  which eats the caret, so every base candidate failed and the documented gate had never
  been runnable on Windows at all (issue #3225). All three now spawn git shell-free, with
  launch failures surfaced instead of misreported as "no base resolves".
- **The portrait manifest stopped false-failing release CI.** Its `--check` byte-compared
  the whole renderer fingerprint, which moves on any source change anywhere in the render
  import graph even when zero portrait pixels changed, and had driven 8 manifest rewrites
  in two weeks and roughly 250 re-pin and re-bless commits in the same window, 40 of them
  in one day. A bookkeeping-only-drift classifier now tolerates fingerprint and
  bundle-digest movement while still failing on any real change (#3307).
- **Repo hygiene.** The shared comment-stripping test helper had a block-first flattener
  hole that silently voided negative source-text pins across large spans of `main.ts` and
  six other files; a follow-up closed a related block-terminator-adjacent gap. Separately, a
  repo-wide dead-code sweep removed 328 orphaned files and about 105 unused exports and
  types, cross-checked against this repo's known false-positive classes and reviewed by
  four fresh domain agents before landing.

# World of ClaudeCraft v0.37.1 Release Notes

**Release:** v0.37.1
**Date:** 2026-08-13
**Previous release:** v0.37.0

Version 0.37.1 is a hotfix for the battleground queue. Since the v0.36.0 deploy, queue
pops fired their cue and chat line but never showed the Accept/Decline prompt for some
players; silence counted as a decline, so pops churned and no battleground match could
seat. The prompt is restored, and the dungeon finder's "group found" prompt — which
carried the identical flaw with a wider window — gets the same fix.

## Fixes

- **Battleground queue pops prompt again.** Online, the queue-pop event arrives one
  message ahead of the snapshot that carries the offer state. When a frame boundary
  landed between the two, the popup read the gap as an already-resolved offer and closed
  for good. The popup now arms on the event (cue plays immediately) and opens on the
  first frame that can actually read the offer, with a bounded ~5-second grace window
  (#3363).
- **Dungeon finder "group found" prompt** hardened against the same arrival-order race,
  which had a wider window on its slower snapshot cadence (#3363).

## Under the hood

- New regression suites pin both popups' pending-arrival contract and the server's
  events-before-snapshot wire ordering, so a change to either half of the ordering is a
  conscious one.
- No markup, style, or balance changes; no data migration. Full parity across all 21
  locales (the prompt's strings are unchanged).

# World of ClaudeCraft v0.37.0 Release Notes

**Release:** v0.37.0
**Date:** 2026-08-13
**Previous release:** v0.36.0

Version 0.37.0 is a client performance and platform delivery release. The loading and
hitch-elimination campaign that started in v0.36.0 closes out its worst remaining
offenders, the native mobile shells gain real differential over-the-air updates behind a
visible update gate, the Android build finally fits under the Play Store size cap, and
the texture pipeline moves terrain to standalone KTX2. Around the platform work, players
get a bag item lock, a smarter World Market, backward Tab targeting, and authored bodies
for zone 1's kobolds. One security fix is included: the Rift forge's wire commands are
now gated off by default. The release spans 384 commits and roughly 43 pull requests
across 677 files, and ships fully localized across all 21 locales.

## Highlights

- **Login and preview hitches, bounded.** The hitch-login-storm pass (#3328) takes the
  worst measured armory preview stall from 754ms to 42ms and preview queue-sync from
  10.2s to 1.6s, and holds first reveals until shaders finish linking off-thread.
- **Real over-the-air updates.** The native shells download only the files that changed
  (content-addressed by SHA-256), show progress in a visible update gate, and fall back
  to the full bundle on any irregularity (#3317).
- **Under the Play Store cap.** An install-time asset pack moves media and audio out of
  the Android base module, cutting it from 555 MB to 68 MB compressed (#3317).
- **The iOS crash-reload loop is fixed.** Far-away zone geometry is now evicted under
  memory pressure, ending the WebKit kill-and-reload cycle on long sessions (#3318).
- **Terrain in KTX2.** The 38 runtime terrain and structure textures ship as standalone
  KTX2, cutting their resident memory from about 212 MB to 41 MB (#3291 line).
- **Rift forge wire commands closed.** The three forge commands were dispatchable by
  wire-literate players despite the UI never shipping; they now sit behind a
  default-off realm flag (#3329).
- **Lock your treasures.** A player-controlled item lock blocks selling, salvaging, and
  crafting away anything you mark (#3326).
- **General chat gets guard rails.** Bounded per-account send quotas with localized
  feedback and a full admin dashboard (#3335).
- **Quality of life.** Shift+Tab cycles targets backward, the World Market sorts by
  price and badges armor classes, and battleground Unstuck actually unsticks.
- **Fully localized.** All 21 locales ship with zero pending rows across 12,640 keys,
  including a 485-row fill for the new chat-quota surfaces.

## Combat, classes, and balance

- The proportional fear diminishing-returns ladder is restored after a refactor
  regression had silently flattened it to absolute durations — a 4s Psychic Scream no
  longer becomes a flat 8s on first PvP application.
- Bonelord Xarreth's Soul Grave and Death Sentence death-zone cast times are raised to
  match the rest of the rift boss roster: at S-rank tempo they left about half a second
  of real reaction time versus over a full second for peers. A roster-wide,
  rank-wide regression guard keeps single-boss fixes from drifting again (#3342).
- Training dummies are excluded from Sentence's sub-20% Condemnation execute, which was
  reporting the dummy's ~999,999 remaining health as a single hit and corrupting DPS
  meters (#3320).
- Pets detect stealthed players at their real 18-yard aggressive-engagement range
  instead of their 50-yard assist-scan range.
- Pet stat auras now respect the aura's apply/remove direction instead of always

  "competitive": living fighters recover to their team graveyard (chosen over the

## Rendering and client performance

- The hitch-login-storm pass (#3328) bounds three classes of production hitching:
  - The shader-readiness poll is a round-robin pass under a 2ms budget instead of a
    synchronous scan measured at 10.2s on link-backlogged GPUs.
  - Character texture uploads prewarm in 8ms slices ahead of first draw instead of
    costing 140-870ms synchronously; player portraits prewarm through an async staged
    core instead of paying 150-248ms shader links on first view.
  - The armory preview lane is staged into budgeted slices with a held warmup buffer:
    the worst measured preview unit drops from 754ms to 42ms.
  - First-reveal compile gates hold a far cell's near-representation and a town's first
    fog-cull reveal until their programs link off-thread (632-681ms submit stalls

  per-biome sky HDR stores with distance eviction (previously ~17 MB per biome for the
  session across 19 biomes), pooled contact blob shadows for characters on shadowless
  tiers, and correct material cloning that restores dyed armor colors and the arena
  walls' stone-detail layer. Review rounds fixed an instance buffer re-uploading every
  frame, let half-loaded biomes self-repair, and made teleports into evicted realms
  recover behind the loading curtain.
- Terrain and surface-detail textures ship as standalone KTX2: resident texture memory
  drops from about 212 MB to 41 MB, and download size by about a third. Six splat color
  layers deliberately stay JPG after KTX2 crashed the low-tier world builder, with a
  drawability guard that degrades instead of crashing.
- Far-away zones' terrain and water geometry evict under constrained memory, fixing the
  iOS WebKit crash-reload on long sessions — a live iOS test freed 141 of 261 resident

- Shadow work (#3299): the sun shadow camera snaps to whole texels, ending "shadow
  swimming"; shadow maps drop to half rate under sustained render pressure with
  hysteresis; and the "Insane" 8192x8192 (~256 MB) shadow rung is retired, with stored

  spell school — a fire boss's windup no longer rings up arcane violet — with lightness

- The surface-detail shader's program cache no longer collides dyed and undyed
  materials of the same family onto one compiled shader.

# World of ClaudeCraft v0.32.4 Release Notes

**Release:** v0.32.4
**Date:** 2026-08-01
**Previous release:** v0.32.3

Version 0.32.4 is an emergency hotfix for the desktop apps. Since v0.32.2 shipped every
GLB's textures as KTX2 (the iOS world-entry memory fix), the Windows, macOS, and Linux
desktop clients froze at the "Loading world" screen: the KTX2 transcoder runs inside a
worker that inherits the desktop shell's Content Security Policy, the transcoder's
generated glue compiled code at startup, the CSP (correctly) refuses that, and every
model load then waited forever with no error shown. The web client was never affected,
and this release changes nothing about how the game plays.

## Highlights

- **Desktop loading works again.** The shipped Basis/KTX2 transcoder is rebuilt without
  any dynamic code generation (the same shapes Emscripten emits under its
  no-dynamic-execution mode), so it initializes under the desktop shell's strict CSP.
  The shell's security policy is unchanged: the fix removes the transcoder's need for
  eval rather than weakening the policy.
- **iOS keeps its memory fix.** KTX2 textures are untouched and the patched transcoder
  produces byte-identical output everywhere the old one already worked, verified across
  every mip level of shipped textures.
- **Guarded against recurrence.** The transcoder is now a generated artifact with a
  committed patcher, structural no-dynamic-code pins, and a functional transcode parity
  test, so a future three.js re-vendor cannot silently reintroduce the freeze.

## Desktop players

Installed apps update automatically: the updater still runs while the loading screen is
stuck, so affected 0.32.2 and 0.32.3 installs pick up 0.32.4 within their normal check
window (15 seconds after launch, then every 4 hours). Restarting the app forces the
check. Fresh installers for all three platforms are on the download page.

## Under the hood

- `public/basis/basis_transcoder.js` is regenerated by `scripts/patch_basis_transcoder.mjs`
  from three's vendored copy, replacing the four embind code-generation sites with their
  eval-free equivalents. The wasm is untouched and stays byte-pinned to three.
- `tests/basis_transcoder_csp.test.ts` pins the no-dynamic-code invariant, the patcher's
  failure arms, and byte parity of a real KTX2 transcode against the pristine transcoder.
- `tests/glb_texture_compression.test.ts` now pins shipped === patch(vendored), so a
  three.js bump goes red until the patcher is deliberately re-run.

# World of ClaudeCraft v0.32.1 Release Notes

**Release:** v0.32.1
**Date:** 2026-07-30
**Previous release:** v0.32.0

Version 0.32.1 is the first patch on the 0.32 line, and it is mostly about honoring what 0.32.0
promised. The headline is that `/unstuck` no longer kills you: it moves you to the nearest
graveyard under a new, shorter sickness instead of routing you through the Pale Keeper. Around it,
the four escort quests become completable for the first time, the ten new realms' world mobs
finally drop loot, normal Wildheart Basin gets a real tuning pass, rift portals move from three
world-wide to one per zone every hour with WoW-style instance binding, world entry stops dying on
4 GB iPhones, and the mobile apps gain self-hosted over-the-air updates so fixes like these reach
phones without waiting on a store review.

## Highlights

- **Unstuck stops killing you.** After the same 10-second stationary countdown, `/unstuck` moves
  you to the nearest graveyard, revives you if you were down, and charges the new Unstuck Sickness
  instead of a death and the Pale Keeper walk.
- **All four escort quests are completable.** No shipped client could actually start an escort
  run; now the Interact key and right-click both work, the quest text points the right way, and
  the townsfolk you walk home no longer render as the bandits you protect them from.
- **Rifts: a portal in every zone, every hour.** Availability moves from at most three portals
  world-wide to one open portal per eligible zone (all eleven) on an hourly rotation, the instance
  pool grows from 8 to 64 slots, and progressed runs bind their members raid-style.
- **Normal Wildheart Basin hits like a dungeon.** It shipped running raw base templates at roughly
  a quarter of the intended pressure; it is now calibrated to the Gravewyrm Sanctum model, and
  pulling the boss early sends the whole living route at you.
- **The v0.32.0 realms drop loot.** 54 world mobs that dropped nothing (or only quest items) now
  carry the standard copper curve and family junk drops.
- **4 GB iPhones survive world entry**, with a tight-memory graphics rung, deferred cosmetic skin
  atlases, and an armed entry crash probe that engages the recovery ladder instead of bouncing you
  back to the launcher.
- **Self-hosted OTA updates for the mobile shells.** JS and content fixes can ship to the
  published iOS and Android apps from our own update host, with a dry-run-default publish
  workflow, a world-layout compatibility preflight, and automatic rollback of a broken bundle.

## Unstuck

- A living invoker is moved to the nearest graveyard, still alive, pools intact. A dead or
  released invoker is pulled there and raised at a fifth of their pools. Neither outcome leaves a
  corpse, and dying mid-countdown still cancels, so a pre-started `/unstuck` can never be a
  discount on the ordinary death loop.
- The price is **Unstuck Sickness**: the same 75 percent whole-attribute drain as The Keeper's
  Toll, level-scaled the same way (nothing below level 10), but capped at 5 minutes instead of 10,
  which is exactly the `/unstuck` success cooldown, so the debuff expires as the command comes
  back. It persists across a relog, and it never stacks with The Keeper's Toll: whichever sickness
  lands most recently displaces the other.
- Inside a dungeon, delve, or rift, the destination is the overworld graveyard nearest the door,
  and the teleport lands settled, so a stale jump arc can never deal fall damage on arrival.
- Cross-version safety for the new OTA world: a 0.32.1 client shows the correct message even when
  a not-yet-updated server resolves the old kill-and-release outcome.

## Rifts

- Every eligible zone keeps one open rift portal on an hourly rotation. A zone's next portal opens
  one cycle after the previous one opened, so an expired portal is replaced immediately while a
  freshly cleared zone waits for its boundary rather than being instantly refarmable.
- The instance pool grows from 8 to 64 slots, with a per-event cap of 32 so one hyped portal can
  never drain the global pool. The community-test density profile is retired: the dense population
  is now the one policy on every host.
- **Binding:** the first mob kill or plundered cache marks a run progressed. A progressed run
  binds its members raid-style: they always re-enter their own run, never a sibling instance,
  whatever their party does. Unspoiled leftovers recycle when players who entered independently
  regroup, so a party shares one run instead of being split across instances.
- **The race is fair to the losers:** another group's first clear no longer ejects you mid-run.
  Losing runs play to their own finish, but pay no completion loot: an egress only, no clear-time
  gear ladder, no sealed cache. Everything a loser walks out with came off the mobs or a mid-run
  chest, and the first-clear extras stay winner-exclusive.

## Quests

- All four escort quests ("Seeing Wren Home" and the Mosley, Suli, and Bram escorts) were
  uncompletable from every shipped client: both interaction ladders only routed talkable entities
  of NPC kind, and an escortee is mob-kind, so nothing could start the run. Escort starts now work
