## Dungeons

- **Normal Wildheart Basin** shipped with no normal tuning record, so it ran raw base templates:
  on the reference level-20 protection warrior its trash swung 26 to 32 and Zulgar the Basin
  Tyrant 35, against normal Gravewyrm Sanctum's 103 to 112 and 200 to 301. It is now ported to the
  Sanctum calibration: doubled health, trash floored at 100 damage, the rare ccImmune beastmaster
  packs at 150, the boss at 200, and a new per-mob ranged multiplier so the half of the roster
  that casts from range (stalkers and hexcallers) scales with everything else instead of idling at

- **Premature boss pulls are punished:** aggroing Zulgar while any of the route is still alive

combat meters became windows you can move, resize, and pull apart.

## Highlights

- **Rifts: procedural infinite dungeons** on a C to S rank ladder, generated purely from
  `seed + baseLevel + floorIndex` so the server and every client rebuild byte-identical content from
  a descriptor. Closed out across nine playtest map and collision rounds (#1584, #2575 to #2584).
- **Eleven new realms**: The Veiled Hollow, The Drakelands, The Frostveil Reach, The Amberfall, The
  Willowfen, The Nightbloom, The Wraithwood, The Galecrest, The Palmreach, The Evergarden, and The
  Farshore, carrying 105 new quests and 48 new NPCs between them, plus a new five-man dungeon, the
  Wildheart Basin, hidden behind the Sunken Idol in Palmreach.
- **Mounts became items.** Reins are used from a bag or an action bar slot, the mount picker and the
  persisted "selected mount" concept are gone, dismount is instant, and the rarity ladder was
  rotated so the tiers match their speed.
- **The rift loot economy was rebuilt on real rates.** Rank pools now derive from the tables their
  tier already uses, the legendary chase dropped from 4 percent to 0.3 percent per item, and the
  mount ladder pays the exact rates those mounts already pay in heroic five-mans.
- **Voice-over for the new realms.** 72 new NPC voices and 334 new clips take the catalog from 18
  voices and 191 clips to 90 voices and 525 voiced lines. No greeting NPC is silent.
- **The world streams.** Chunk streaming replaces all-at-once residency, lifting the view distance
  off the client's memory ceiling (#2570), with the unowned world-gap chunks filled in (#2535).
- **An interactive continent overview** joins the world map (#2495).
- **The combat meters are real windows**, movable, resizable, and separable from the tabbed panel,
  with hover detail on the damage meter (#2592, #2588).

## Rifts

- A Rift is fully procedural. Geometry, spawns, hazards, and the floor's puzzle or gate are
  generated from `seed + baseLevel + floorIndex`, so nothing but that descriptor crosses the wire
  and every host regenerates the same dungeon.
- You find them as overworld portals, from level 20. At most three portals are open world-wide at
  once, each lives an hour before collapsing unused, and a new one spawns two to four hours after a
  slot frees.
- A run is three to six generated floors, each with its own room shape, theme, and one headline
  mechanic, ending on a floor boss. Killing the last boss opens the exit and seals the portal, so a
  cleared rift cannot be re-farmed.
- Fifteen percent of C-rank seeds open the hand-authored two-floor Infernal Citadel instead of a
  generated layout. It is deliberately C-only content.
- Every portal is a race. One rift event is shared by everyone who finds it, each group gets its own
  instance, and they compete for a single first-clear claim.
- Eight environment themes (Frostbound, Emberforge, Venomweald, Boneyard, Warcamp, Voidscar,
  Stormspire, Sunken) with their own giga-bosses at up to 3.3x normal scale.
- Floor mechanics are mutually exclusive so only one thing reads at a time: rune pylons, an ice
  slide, a boulder push, a rune sequence, or a switch-gated portcullis.

### The rank ladder

- Ranks set the portal's base level: C at 20, B at 22, A at 25, S at 28. C ramps its mob level per
  floor up to 22; B and A hold flat at 22; S holds flat at 23.
- Scaling is a multiplier on the template, calibrated against real normal and heroic dungeon output.
  C uses normal-dungeon tuning and stays kiteable. B is heroic parity, A is heroic times 1.2, and S
  is heroic times 1.33, each also raising add damage, armor, and a mob move-speed floor.
- Bosses spend a mechanic budget by rank: one live headline mechanic at C, two at B, three at A,
  four at S, drawn in the boss's authored order.
- Death rules harden with rank. Lava and blackwater burn 6 or 12 percent of max health per second up
  to A, and are a guaranteed kill at S. A rolling boulder chips about 7 percent at C and is a
  guaranteed kill at B and above. Boss death zones always kill anyone still standing in them when
  the fuse ends, and at S they cast and recycle faster.
- Non-dodgeable boss mechanics are capped at 90 percent of your max health, so they threaten hard
  but can never one-shot you from full. Only the dodgeable hazards are exempt from that cap, on
  purpose.
- Dying in a rift is an ordinary death. Re-entry while dead is limited to a run you already belong
  to, and only once that run is out of combat.

## Loot and rewards

- Rank pools derive from the content tables their tier already uses rather than a bespoke list. C
  pays from every equippable rare or epic that a normal level-20 five-man drops; B, A and S pay from
  every epic the heroic five-man bosses drop, plus four rift-signature epics. The heroic raid is
  explicitly excluded so a rift can never back-door into raid loot.
- The practical effect is far wider variety. The C pool went from 10 items to 33 and the heroic pool
  from 4 to 32, with every class covered rather than a handful.
- Clear rewards by rank: C pays a guaranteed item and 10,000 coin. B pays a guaranteed epic and
  10,000. A pays a guaranteed epic and 35,000. S pays a guaranteed epic, a 35 percent chance of a
  second epic, and 55,000.
- Two rift-exclusive legendaries each roll independently at 0.3 percent on an S clear: Heart of the

- Voidsong is deliberately a poor melee weapon. Its damage line is priced at rare-dagger tier so a
  melee class has no reason to take it from a caster, and it carries no class lock, which leaves the
  healer paladin and shaman cases open on purpose.
- The mount ladder rolls once per B, A or S clear and never inherits from a lower tier. B pays 0.5

# World of ClaudeCraft v0.31.0 Release Notes

**Release:** v0.31.0
**Date:** 2026-07-27
**Previous release:** v0.30.0

Version 0.31.0 makes the world physical. One deterministic character-physics engine now runs in
the offline sim, on the authoritative server, and in the client's self-extrapolator, so every model
you can see collides exactly as it is drawn, and a real traversal ladder sits on top of it: stride
over the low things, vault the waist-high things, and pull yourself up onto the things above your
head. Alongside it the release hardens the corpse-harvest pipeline against every malformed request
it could previously be handed, gives bags their own World Market browse category, makes a
destructive enchant replacement look destructive, draws world-map labels and minimap glyphs from
bounded sprite caches, and rolls back the vertical nameplate stacking that did not survive contact
with a crowd.

## Highlights

- The parkour physics engine lands: continuous swept collision, multi-pass sliding,
  depenetration, and step-up, with a pinned traversal ladder that leaves no unreachable gap
  between striding, vaulting, and climbing (#2527).
- Props collide as they are drawn. Measured colliders now exist for market stalls, the composed
  chapel and its standable hall roof, dock huts and rowboats, camp crates, ruin stumps, headstones,
  town and station furniture, field rocks, gather nodes, the banker's strongbox, the Ravenpost
  mailbox, dungeon door jambs, delve portal slabs, and the town wall as a vaultable parapet
  (#2527).
- Ledge climb is a real pull-up, a sim-owned movement mode with netted progress, posed from the
  rigs' baked clips and cross-faded at the pull's midpoint. Low objects keep the vault (#2527).
- Corpse harvest is hardened end to end: it now refuses a pick that can never yield anything,
  ignores a component tag the corpse does not carry, collapses a repeated tag, grants the full
  rolled quantity on a signed yield, and stops offering a harvest whose every family is unmapped
  (#2472, #2496, #2503, #2508, #2515, #2533).
- Bags are findable on the World Market for the first time. They were the only items in the game
  reachable from nothing but "All", and they now have their own category with capacity subtypes
  derived from the catalog rather than hardcoded (#2464).
- A World Market enchant row that will destroy an existing enchant now looks destructive, with a
  danger tint and a leading rule that survive forced-colors mode (#2465).
- Vertical nameplate stacking is reverted. It read well with a few plates but churned badly in a
  crowd, lifting far plates off their owners and compressing them against the top of the viewport
  (#2520).

## Movement and the physical world

- One character-physics engine, shared by all three hosts. Continuous swept collision, multi-pass
  sliding, depenetration, and step-up resolve identically offline, on the server, and in the client
  self-extrapolator, so what your client predicts is what the server agrees happened (#2527).
- The traversal ladder is defined by obstacle height: stride under 0.9, silent vault through the
  jump arc plus mantle reach, ledge climb for lips above your head, and wall above that. An
  invariant test proves the bands leave no gap you can neither cross nor climb (#2527).
- Dungeon interiors join the ladder. Per-dungeon furniture colliders come from the shared layouts,
  coffin lids and cargo tiers are standable, and the raised boss dais is real floor rather than
  decoration (#2527).
- Grounded presentation on the render side: step smoothing, ground tilt, and landing dust (#2527).
- Deliberate pass-through exceptions are documented rather than accidental: herb clusters, marsh
  reeds, well monuments, and notice boards stay walkable, and the list lives in
  `docs/design/physics-asset-audit.md` (#2527).
- Existing gameplay contracts were pinned rather than assumed. Station anchors, service routes, NPC
  reachability, mob pathing, and town containment all hold, and grounded movers without a jump see
  the same walls they saw before (#2527).

## Professions and gathering

- The Apply Enchant picker states what a replacement keeps and flags the row that destroys. The
  "Replaces {enchant}" flag previously rendered in the same muted style as the purely informational
  "Worn ({slot})" tag, so a destructive row carried no more visual weight than a harmless one. The
  tint stays redundant with the wording in both palettes and is never shed by a graphics tier,
  because a destroy warning is actionable information (#2465).
- The enchant picker's mixed-holding flag now counts the worn family, so the warning matches what
  you actually hold (#2465).
- Corpse harvest has its own result event rather than borrowing another system's (#2472).
- A signed corpse-harvest yield grants the full rolled quantity (#2496, #2391).
- A corpse-harvest request carrying a duplicate component tag collapses to one, and a tag the
  corpse does not carry is ignored rather than accepted (#2503, #2508).
- A harvest whose pick can never yield anything is refused, and a corpse whose every family is
  unmapped no longer offers a harvest at all (#2515, #2533).
- Profession grants print exactly one chat line each, instead of one per underlying grant site
  (#2452).
- The loot cue stands down on an unbind stack peel, so peeling one item off a stack no longer fires
  the full loot presentation (#2483).
- Disenchant now resolves the inventory slot you actually clicked. Previously it resolved by item
  id through a preference scan that consumed the least special copy, so with duplicates the copy
  destroyed could be one you did not select.

## The World Market and economy

- Bags get a World Market browse category, with capacity subtypes computed from the distinct
  `bagSlots` values the content ships. Authoring a bag with a new capacity adds its option
  automatically, in ascending order, with no code and no locale change (#2464).
- Merchant house stock and player listing ids now occupy separate id bands, so a house listing can
  no longer collide with a player's (#2470).
- The Claudium WOC discount is read from the economy service's authoritative native price response
  and rendered dynamically, instead of bundling a fixed percentage. It fails closed when the
  discount data is missing, malformed, stale-mixed, or inconsistent across SKUs (#2501).
- The vendor sell-quantity dialog caps the clicked slot rather than the total you hold (#2353).
- Vendor buyback preserves masterwork and signer data, so buying back a piece returns the piece you
  sold (#2398).

## Interface and controls

- World-map labels draw from a bounded sprite cache rather than being laid out per frame (#2484).

- Vertical nameplate stacking is fully reverted to the cluster-mean declutter that preceded it,

- The Town Focus panel repaints only when its signature changes, and keeps keyboard focus across

- A resized window's body follows the new height instead of keeping its old one (#2477).
- Every chat-link encode site routes through the parser's own id charset guard, so an id the parser
  would reject can no longer be encoded into a link (#2462).
- Parry displays as a percent, matching Dodge and Crit Chance (#2386).
- Gamepad look-pitch direction matches mouse and touch (#2401).

- A shared kill credits the whole eligible party toward deeds, not just the killing blow (#2392).
- A master-loot assignment carrying the same player id twice collapses to one, so a duplicated

**Date:** 2026-07-26
**Previous release:** v0.29.1

Version 0.30.0 turns enchanting into a system you can actually live with: enchants apply to the
gear you are wearing and can be replaced later, and the enchanting screens now explain what every
choice does. Alongside it, the release adds a second ranked arena map, rebalances critical strike
and haste onto the classic stat ladder, retunes normal Gravewyrm Sanctum for freshly capped
groups, replaces the procedural item and HUD icons with painted art, rebuilds Eastbrook Vale's town
center with hand-crafted models, gives professions and consumables real recorded sound, and fixes
a server input limit that had been silently discarding movement from high refresh rate displays.

## Highlights

- Enchanting is finished as a loop: apply an enchant directly to equipped gear, replace an
  existing enchant behind an explicit confirmation, and read exactly what each enchant does before
  you commit (#2404, #2405, #2418).
- Critical strike and haste now cost 20 rating per 1%, up from 10. Existing gear was not touched,
  so every piece you own grants half the crit or haste percentage it did before (#2358).
- The Drowned Court is a second ranked arena map, and the Ashen Coliseum pit was rebuilt with new
  cover and larger bounds. Ranked 1v1 and 2v2 now rotate between the two (#2406, #2407).
- Roughly 259 item icons and 18 HUD launcher icons are now hand-painted art instead of procedural
  glyphs, and Eastbrook Vale's town center is rebuilt with new models (#2301, #2356, #2383).
- Gathering, crafting, enchanting, eating, and drinking now play real recorded sound: 47 new
  recordings, where most of these actions were previously silent (#2134, #2274).
- Normal Gravewyrm Sanctum is clearable by a freshly capped group in quest gear, and Korzul's
  Grave Inferno now actually fires during a normal kill instead of only on a 30 second timer
  (#2378, #2419).
- The server's inbound message limit rises from 40 to 120 messages per second. The old ceiling sat
  below what a 120 Hz display legitimately sends while turning, so real movement input was being
  discarded (#2372).

## Enchanting and professions

- Applying an enchant no longer requires unequipping the item first. Point Apply Enchant at a worn
  ring, weapon, or armor piece and it enchants in place. Because rings and dual wielded weapons can
  hold identical copies in two slots, you choose the exact slot rather than just the item (#2405).
- You can now replace an enchant that is already on a piece of gear. Choosing a different enchant
  for an enchanted item raises a confirmation that names the enchant you are about to destroy, the
  reagent cost, and a warning that the old enchant's materials are not refunded and the action
  cannot be undone. Re-applying the identical enchant you already have is refused, since it would
  consume materials for no change (#2418).
- The enchanting surfaces now explain themselves. The Apply Enchant list states each enchant's stat
  bonus inline and groups choices into Base, Runed, and Greater. Item tooltips replace the vague
  "Enchanted" badge with per-line attribution, so you can see which stats come from the enchant and
  which come from the masterwork bonus. The disenchant confirmation previews the materials you will
  receive, enchanting materials explain what they are for and which gear drops them, and bagged
  items get distinct corner marks for enchanted, signed, and bind-on-trade instead of one
  ambiguous wedge (#2404).
- Disenchanting an item whose only copy is already enchanted no longer fails with a misleading
  "you do not have that item" message. Disenchant still consumes a plain copy first when you have
  one, and only falls back to an enchanted copy, destroying that enchant with it, as a last resort
  (#2349).
- Every gathering node and cast now requires a matching tool, including the starting tier that
  previously needed none: mining, logging, and herbalism check for a pick, axe, or sickle, and
  casting a line requires a pole or rod. Gathering tools are now hotbar placeable, and using one
  walks you to the nearest matching node in range and begins harvesting. Node tooltips, the minimap
  lock icon, and the denial message all state the tool requirement, and each tool's tooltip lists
  what it unlocks along with its speed or catch bonus (#2357).
- Crafting, salvaging, disenchanting, and unbinding now confirm the result will fit in your bags
  before completing, accounting for the space the consumed materials free up, and refuse with a
  clear reason when it will not (#2352).
- Crafting grants character experience scaled to the crafting skill you actually gained from that
  craft. A recipe that teaches you nothing, because the craft is at its 125 cap or the recipe has
  gone gray, now grants no character experience (#2361).
- The character sheet shows your true floored gathering proficiency. Previously a raw value between
  99.5 and 99.99 displayed as 100 while the deed and catch tier thresholds, which read the real
  value, stayed locked (#2348).
- The Kilnscale Mantle's vendor sell-back value drops from 470 to 280 copper. A crafter using
  discounted material counts could produce it for as little as 300 copper and vendor it at a
  guaranteed profit, printing copper at no risk.
- Clicking Learn at a trainer now shows immediate feedback on that recipe and disables the row
  while the request is in flight, which also prevents a fast double click from producing an error
  (#2359).
- The crafting window updates the moment your bags change, so buying, looting, or trading for the
  last reagent you need enables the Craft button without closing and reopening the window (#2377).

## Classes and combat

- Critical strike and haste rating now convert at 20 rating per 1%, up from 10. Hit rating is
  unchanged at 10 per 1%. Item and set rating values were deliberately not adjusted, so a set bonus
  that read "+2% critical strike" or "+15% attack and casting speed" now delivers 1% and 7.5%. Crit
  and haste remain single shared stats: crit raises attack and spell critical chance together, and
  haste speeds melee swings, ranged autoattacks, and casting together, so healers take the same
  reduction to cast speed and heal crit that a damage dealer takes to attack speed and damage crit.
  Hit is now clearly the cheapest secondary stat, matching the classic era ladder (#2358).
- Fire mage burst is reined in. A live raid report had a fire mage at 363 DPS over a 27 second
  Nythraxis kill, roughly 2.3 times a comparably geared player. Two causes were corrected: Ignite
  was re-extending its entire banked burn on every refresh instead of carrying only the unpaid
  remainder forward, paying out about double its stated 40% over 6 seconds; and Cinderfall's three
  charges each recharged in 8 seconds, letting fire dump nine guaranteed crits every 24 seconds.
  Cinderfall keeps three charges and still empties its bank inside Phoenix Trance, which now also
  instantly completes whichever charge is recharging so a Trance window always opens with one
  ready, but each charge now recharges in 30 seconds. On best-in-slot gear, fire's burst window
  lands around 1.5 times a comparable frost mage, and sustained damage over a full fight sits close
  to frost rather than 2 to 3 times above it (#2360).
- Only one elixir can be active at a time. All four elixirs in the game buff Stamina (Elixir of the
  Boar at +6, Vipersear Elixir at +9, Elixir of the Bear at +12, and Elixir of the Serpent at +12),
  and each previously tracked as a separate buff, so drinking all four stacked to +39. They now
  share a single slot and the most recently drunk one replaces whatever was active, even if it is
  weaker, matching the classic single elixir rule. A replaced buff now also reports its fade
  properly, so the icon and combat log stay honest. Class buffs such as Mark of the Wild's Stamina
  bonus and enemy Stamina debuffs are unaffected and still stack (#2408).
- Ground area abilities and Heroic Leap now scale with your damage modifiers. Consecration,
  Earthquake, Blizzard, Meteor's ground zone, and a warrior's Heroic Leap landing hit were ignoring
  every damage-percent modifier in the game, which meant the Fiesta augments Bloodhunter,
  Overdrive, Apex Predator, Archmage, and Avatar granted no benefit to those abilities despite
  their tooltips promising it. Rune of Power's ground pulse is an ally damage buff rather than a
  damage roll and is deliberately unchanged (#2396).

## Dungeons and the raid

- Normal Gravewyrm Sanctum is retuned for freshly capped groups across two passes this release. The
  first pass corrected damage floors that were close to unsurvivable for a fresh group, where a
  balance bench recorded a tank death in 89 of 96 runs even with a healer; the second pass found
  that correction had overshot soft and raised the pressure back. The shipped floors are roughly
  103 on trash, 301 on Korgath the Bound, 280 on Korzul the Gravewyrm, and 200 on Grand Necromancer
  Velkhar, which is about 20 to 31 percent of a freshly geared tank's health per hit. Velkhar is
  unchanged from the first pass because he was already the dungeon's peak fight, layering summoned
  bonewalker waves on top of his own swings. Every mob keeps its doubled health, and the summoned
  bonewalkers keep their 50 floor (#2378, #2419; the #2419 figures are the shipped ones).
- Korzul's Grave Inferno now happens. The channel previously armed only on a 30 second timer, so a
  normal group killing him in his typical 15 to 26 seconds never saw it. It now also arms when he
  drops to 50% health, comfortably above his 30% enrage, so every kill meets the mechanic. Standing
  in the full four pulse channel deals roughly 1050 to 1350 raw damage, which is lethal to a fresh
  character, so stepping out is a real check rather than a mechanic most groups outlived (#2419).
- Heroic boss-summoned adds hit 40% softer. Across The Hollow Crypt, The Sunken Bastion, Gravewyrm
  Sanctum, and The Drowned Temple, a boss's summoned adds now floor at 150 damage on a reference
  tank instead of 250. Boss, trash, health, and armor values in those dungeons, and everything in
  the Nythraxis raid, are unchanged (#2378).

- A target selected during the prep countdown now survives into the fight instead of being cleared

## Server, performance, and reliability

- The inbound message limit rises from 40 messages per second (burst 60) to 120 per second (burst
  180), with a byte budget of 64 KB per second (burst 128 KB). The old ceiling was below what real
  play produces: a player holding a turn on a 120 Hz or faster display can legitimately send about
  80 messages per second, so once the burst allowance drained the server silently discarded roughly
  a third to a half of those updates, which could read as stutter or rubber-banding while turning.
  Ordinary play uses at most about 83 messages per second and around 10 KB per second, both well
  under the new limits (#2372).
- A connection that genuinely floods the server is disconnected, but only on a sustained pattern:
  at least 5 separate seconds within a rolling 10 second window in which more than 30 of that
  connection's messages were rejected. A single lag spike, or a network stall followed by the client
  flushing its backlog in one burst, can mark at most one or two seconds as abusive by design, well
  short of the 5 required (#2372).
- A flood disconnect now gives a specific message, "You were disconnected for sending actions too
  quickly. Please wait a moment and log back in," instead of a generic error. The anti-bot
  disconnect keeps its own deliberately vaguer message (#2372).
- Inbound traffic is split into reserved per-class budgets after parsing (movement at 90 per second
  with a burst of 120, commands at 30 with a burst of 60, chat at 4 with a burst of 8 in front of
  the existing chat cooldown), so a movement flood cannot starve casts and commands, or the reverse
  (#2372).
- A one-time performance tip can now appear if your recent frames have been rough, under about 45
  fps or noticeably uneven, and the game can identify a likely cause on your machine. It shows once
  per install per cause and names the fix: either that the game is running without GPU acceleration,
  or that a laptop is rendering on its integrated power-saving GPU rather than a dedicated one
  (#2372).
- On High and Ultra graphics settings, reported draw-call and triangle counts are now real
  accumulated per-frame values. A renderer quirk reset them on every render pass, so those clients
  always reported a fixed low number. This was a telemetry-only defect; the adaptive resolution
  governor's own input was unaffected and is bit-for-bit unchanged on every tier.
- Client network and memory telemetry (snapshot parse and apply cost, arrival gaps, snapshots per
  frame, and 1 Hz heap sampling) is now always on and rides the existing performance beacon,
  closing a blind spot where this cost was invisible in production.
- The ignore and block list commands are now rate limited well above any normal usage pattern.

## Operator notes

- Three new Prometheus counters on the existing bearer-gated `/metrics` endpoint:
  `woc_ws_messages_dropped_total` (labeled by cause: rate limit, byte budget, or one of the three
  inbound classes), `woc_ws_rate_kicks_total`, and `woc_input_frames_missed_total`. Every cause
  series is pre-registered at zero, so a quiet cause reads as zero rather than as a missing series.
- No new environment variables. Every gate, class budget, and abuse-window value in the inbound
  redesign is a compile-time constant, not operator tunable.
- After deploying, watch `woc_ws_rate_kicks_total` and `woc_ws_messages_dropped_total` to confirm no
  unexpected increase from real mobile or high-latency traffic. The inbound ceiling is now roughly
  three times looser than before, and the old 200-consecutive-violation kick counter is removed, so
  the windowed abuse score and the per-class budgets are the replacement defense.
- `client_perf_reports` gains six additive columns under report schema version 2 (a zone or
  scenario id, a crowd size bucket with raw entity and view counts, a worst 10 second p95 frame
  time, and perf-doctor suggestion ids), plus an index on
  `(worst_10s_frame_p95_ms DESC, created_at DESC)` built through the existing concurrent-index path
  rather than boot DDL. The admin perf summary API returns a crowd breakdown, the worst 10 second
  p95 figure, and suggestion counts. The TickPerf dashboard page does not yet visualize the new
  fields; they are available through the API and database only.
- `guilds` gains `motd` and `motd_set_by`, both `TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ''`, for the guild
  billboard.
- All new database objects are additive and idempotent and apply at boot; no manual migration step
  is required. Confirm the concurrent index build completes on a large `client_perf_reports` table
  before relying on the new query performance.

## Compatibility and upgrade notes

- **Critical strike and haste on your existing gear are worth half what they were.** Nothing needs
  to be replaced or re-gemmed, but every item and set bonus granting crit or haste rating now
  converts to half the percentage it did before. Builds that lean on crit chance or haste rather
  than flat or guaranteed effects feel this most; frost mage's Shatter kit and its haste-heavy set
  bonus are the clearest example (#2358).
- **Gathering now requires a tool at every tier, including tier 1.** Bare hands previously worked
  throughout Zone 1 and for any tier-1 node elsewhere, so a character who has been gathering
  without a tool will be denied until they buy one. Starter tools (Copper Mining Pick, Handaxe,
  Gathering Sickle, Simple Fishing Pole) cost 20 copper each from the same Zone 1 vendors as
  before, with tier 2 at 60 and tier 3 at 150 copper from the Zone 2 and Zone 3 hub vendors.
  Harvesting materials from a corpse is unaffected and still needs no tool (#2357).
- **Only the last elixir you drink applies.** If your pull routine was quaffing all four Stamina
  elixirs for a combined +39, only the most recent one now counts, up to +12. The rest are wasted
  (#2408).
- **Fire mage Cinderfall cadence drops sharply.** A rotation built on chaining three Cinderfall
  presses every 8 seconds now recharges one charge every 30 seconds. This is an intentional cut to
  burst frequency, not a bug (#2360).
- **Crafting no longer grants character experience at the skill cap.** Repeatedly crafting a recipe
  your profession has mastered, or that has gone gray, now grants no character experience (#2361).
- **Two automatic one-time fixes apply at your next login, with no action needed.** If a gathering
  proficiency displayed as 100 or 200 while the matching deed (for example Old Salt) never
  unlocked, the deed is granted retroactively (#2348). And if you last logged out inside Eastbrook
  Vale, you may be moved slightly so you do not spawn inside the rebuilt town's new geometry;
  instance and delve exits are untouched.
- **Enchant replacement can destroy an enchant permanently.** Overwriting an existing enchant is a
  new option, and confirming it consumes the old enchant with no refund of its materials.
  Previously the game simply refused the action (#2418).
- **The Kilnscale Mantle now vendors for 280 copper instead of 470.** If you hold one to sell, it
  is worth less than before.
- **Two interface behaviors moved.** The target-of-target frame is now beside your target frame
  rather than below it (#2334), and Reset to Defaults resets only the open settings tab rather than
  every category, so a full reset means visiting each tab (#2365).
- **The decorative critters are gone.** Rabbits, squirrels, and songbirds no longer spawn in the
  world (#2331).
- **The flood disconnect message changed.** Support and community channels should expect the new
  "sending actions too quickly" wording; the anti-bot disconnect message is unchanged (#2372).
- All new and changed text is localized across the full 22 locale set.
- No Android or iOS project files changed in this release. The desktop and mobile shells pick up
  these changes through the ordinary web bundle, though the release version surfaces still advance
  as usual.

# World of ClaudeCraft v0.29.0 Release Notes

**Release:** v0.29.0
**Date:** 2026-07-23
**Previous release:** v0.28.0

Version 0.29.0 finalizes Professions 2.0 as a complete, balanced crafting economy. Every
character's profession skills are reset to 0 one time with this release so progression starts on
the finished mastery curve. The release also retunes dungeon and raid difficulty, fills
long-standing class loot gaps, refreshes a large part of the interface, streams a remastered
soundtrack, adds an AAA camera feel pass, and lands substantial server reliability and security
work.

## Highlights

- Professions 2.0 is finished: the mastery curve and skill caps, gathering casts, the fishing
  minigame, commission crafting with the Maker's Bond, enchanting, attunement quests, profession
  deeds, and a commissioned art set complete the system.
- **All profession skills reset to 0 once with this release. Check your in-game mail:** a
  letter from The Guildhall explains the reset. Your items, recipes, tools, materials, bank,
  gold, attunements, titles, deeds, renown, and quests are all kept. The professions guide on
  the game wiki has explicit instructions on how the finished system works:
  https://worldofclaudecraft.com/wiki/professions
- Every dungeon and the Nythraxis raid received a difficulty and economy retune, including a new
  heroic-only Onrush charge mechanic and crowd-control immunity for bosses (#2315).
- The crafting window is rebuilt as a tabbed showcase book, alongside redesigns of the character
  sheet, World Market, Quest Log, and vendor windows.
- Zone and battle music now streams as a remastered soundtrack, and a new chase-camera feel
  stack adds weight to jumps, landings, and zone entries (#2261, #2305).
- Authentication token scopes are now strictly enforced at the WebSocket and admin boundaries,
  and a nightly retention sweep keeps the database bounded (#2282).

## Professions 2.0

- The one-time skill reset: at each character's first login on v0.29.0, every craft skill and
  gathering proficiency is zeroed so all players start the finished progression curve together.
  Nothing else is touched: your items, known recipes, tools, materials, bank, gold, attunements,
  archetype history, titles, deeds, renown, and quests are all preserved. Check your in-game
  mail: every affected character receives a letter from The Guildhall explaining exactly what
  was reset and what was kept.
- The professions guide at https://worldofclaudecraft.com/wiki/professions was rewritten as
  per-skill pages (eight crafts, four gathering skills, an economy page, and an FAQ) with exact
  numbers for training fees, recipe gain rates, node tiers, cast times, catch odds, and enchant
  values, all generated from the live simulation constants (#2303).
- Crafting gain now follows a four-state mastery curve (full, half, quarter, and zero gain by
  recipe difficulty), so cheap recipes no longer grant full skill forever, and per-profession
  caps are enforced: 100 for mining, logging, and herbalism, 125 for the crafts and enchanting,
  and 200 for fishing (#2242).
- Harvesting a node now starts a timed cast, with tool tier and proficiency reducing the cast

# World of ClaudeCraft v0.27.2 Release Notes

**Release:** v0.27.2
**Date:** 2026-07-19
**Previous release:** v0.27.0

v0.27.2 rolls up everything shipped since v0.27.0: the warrior balance round deployed as the v0.27.1 hotfix (never tagged; documented here), the iOS world-entry crash fix this release is named for, two gameplay fixes, two server snapshot performance improvements, and a renderer dependency revert.

## What changed

### iOS world-entry crash fix ([#2138](https://github.com/levy-street/world-of-claudecraft/pull/2138))

Entering the world on an iPhone at any graphics preset above Low could exceed the WebView memory budget, killing the process and dumping the player back to the start screen in a reload loop with no reachable graphics control. v0.27.2 attacks it on three fronts, all client-side:

- **A constrained-memory graphics profile** trims the world-entry GPU allocation spike on phone-class browsers (iOS and Android alike): smaller shadow maps (1536 on Medium, 2048 on High and Ultra), composer MSAA off on High and Ultra, a 1.48 pixel-ratio cap on every tier, sky backdrop mip chains disabled (roughly 44MB of estimated GPU memory), and only the initial biome's environment map prefiltered at entry, with the other two deferred to 30 and 40 seconds after scene build.
- **A watchdog-safe prewarm** on constrained devices: 5 seconds total budget (desktop keeps 12), a 2.5 second shader-compile budget, at most 12 nearby character views built synchronously at entry (the rest stream in during play), and event-loop yields between stages. Desktop budgets, manifest, and ordering are unchanged.
- **A world-entry crash guard** detects that the previous entry attempt crashed (a probe stamped right before scene build and cleared 20 seconds after a stable entry). On iOS and the native apps it steps the graphics preset down exactly one tier, pins the Auto default away from the crashed tier, and lands the next boot on the start screen instead of auto-reentering the world into the same crash. Players see a dismissable "Graphics lowered" banner explaining what happened, localized across all 20 non-English locales.

Also fixed in the same pass: the startup Ultra/Advanced-to-High clamp now covers iOS Safari, not just the native app, and opening the More tray at Medium no longer kills the process (the CSS effects tier is re-stamped at world entry with the real renderer tier, which strips the tray's backdrop blur on phone WebKit). All trims shed cosmetic sharpness only (shadow texels, MSAA, pixel ratio, backdrop mips, IBL timing); no tier hides or delays information a player acts on, keeping the graphics-settings fairness rule. Every stage logs entry-guard diagnostics so any future on-device kill can be isolated from a Web Inspector session.

### Warrior balance: the fury overpower hotfix ([#2112](https://github.com/levy-street/world-of-claudecraft/pull/2112))

The balance round deployed to production as v0.27.1, ending the fury overpower incident. Fury damage came from several compounding sources, and each is addressed at its root:

- **Two-handers re-budgeted game-wide.** The two-hand stat budget drops from 2.0x to 1.3x the one-hand line, deliberately below the 1.75x a mainhand plus offhand pair carries, and in exchange two-handers now carry a codified 15% weapon DPS premium. This affects every class that uses two-handers, not just warriors. Four epic two-handers are re-statted in place with the same item ids, so existing copies update automatically: Deathless Greatblade (46 to 30 stat points, weapon damage raised to 52 to 78), Wyrmfang Greatblade (36 to 23, damage raised to 33 to 53), Bonewrought Greatsword (40 to 26), and Direfang Greatblade (40 to 26). Heroic variants re-derive with the same premium.
- **Titan's Grip has a real cost.** While dual-wielding with a two-handed weapon in either hand, all physical damage the warrior deals is reduced by 12%. Spells and non-physical damage are unaffected, and solo two-hander and dual one-hander loadouts are untouched. The Bloodrush spec description now states the penalty.
- **Fury rage income is cut on four axes.** Warrior auto-attack rage returns to the shared classic scale (a hidden warrior-only bonus multiplier is deleted); Twinstrike generates 4 rage, down from 8; Bladed Gyre no longer generates rage at all (it stays free to cast and keeps Bladed Echo); and Anger Management is trimmed to +10% auto-attack rage and +5% ability rage, from +25% and +15%. Red Harvest itself is unchanged; the income funding it is what shrank.
- **Colossal Might is capped.** The capstone's cooldown refund is capped at up to 10 seconds of reduction every 30 seconds, with the accumulator shown as a visible aura the player can watch tick down. Uncapped, sustained Red Harvest spam collapsed the 180 second Recklessness and Avatar cooldowns to an effective 78 seconds.

Two cross-cutting mechanics fixes shipped in the same round:

- **Melee haste now stacks additively**, mirroring how spell haste has always worked: Bloodlust 30% plus Wildfang Rally 5% plus Enrage 25% now yields 1.6x attack speed instead of the old compounding 1.71x. Any single haste source is numerically identical to before, and slows keep their own multiplicative axis.
- **Wildfang Rally no longer stacks with itself.** A second hunter's cast replaces the first copy instead of doubling the buff on every ally, and a new guard test enforces that every current and future group attack buff is either exhaustion-gated or deduplicated.

All changed tooltips, talent row descriptions, and the fury spec text ship localized across every locale in the same change. Anger Management and Colossal Might keep their row ids, so saved talent picks survive.

### Nature's Fury stops re-announcing itself ([#2110](https://github.com/levy-street/world-of-claudecraft/pull/2110))

The druid Nature's Fury aura is maintained by a once-per-second refresh pulse, and every pulse re-fired the buff-gained announcement: the apply sound, the buff swirl, and a combat log line, every second, for the druid and each buffed party member. The announcement now fires exactly once, on the real first application, for both the self-buff and party members. Buff uptime, the crit value, the 30 yard radius, and expiry behavior are unchanged; this is purely a cue fix.

### Ghosts can corpse-run back into the Abandoned Crypt ([#2105](https://github.com/levy-street/world-of-claudecraft/pull/2105))

Players who died in the Abandoned Crypt (the 10-player Nythraxis raid) and released their spirit could never re-enter the instance: a ghost re-enters only by walking within the door's 2 yard proximity trigger, and the crypt entrance's rock-mound collider bled about 1.6 yards past the portal, stopping every collision-resolved approach just outside the trigger. Mine props now support per-entry collider tuning, and the crypt entrance's collider is pulled back to hug the visible rock pile. Only this entrance changed, there is no visual change, and clicking the door while dead is still refused by design; the walk-in path is the fix. Covered by an end-to-end ghost corpse-run test.

### Server snapshot performance ([#2136](https://github.com/levy-street/world-of-claudecraft/pull/2136), [#2141](https://github.com/levy-street/world-of-claudecraft/pull/2141))

Two changes cut per-tick server cost on the snapshot broadcast path:

- **Party and raid frames are built once per group, not once per viewer.** Each member's frame row (HP, resource, auras, absorbs, role, aggro, incoming heals) is now projected once per broadcast and shared across recipients, turning quadratic per-viewer work linear: a 10-player raid drops from 100 member projections per broadcast to 10. All frame semantics (Temporal Echo visibility, aura priority order, the 8-aura cap, spectator anchoring) are preserved and pinned by tests.
- **A stable snapshot timer wire (v2) removes per-tick timer re-serialization.** Clients on this build negotiate a wire where aura, cooldown, and charge timers are sent as absolute deadlines, cached server-side, and aged locally by the client from the authoritative snapshot clock, so an ordinary tick where timers merely count down re-serializes nothing. In the timer-heavy regression fixture, aura serialization rebuilds drop from more than 150 to 1 and the aggregate payload lands under 35% of the legacy wire (fixture numbers, not a production bandwidth claim). Legacy clients keep byte-compatible snapshots, so rolling deploys are safe, and the server's perf heartbeat gains serialization counters for operators.

### three.js reverted to 0.165 ([#2147](https://github.com/levy-street/world-of-claudecraft/pull/2147))

The renderer library returns from 0.185.1 (picked up in a mid-July dependency bump) to 0.165.0, the version the game ran from launch through v0.26. postprocessing is pinned to exactly 6.36.0 to keep peer dependencies resolvable; that package is not imported by any game code (the post chain uses three's bundled composer plus N8AO), so the pin is inert at runtime, and n8ao itself is unchanged. A full compatibility audit found no code depending on any newer three API, so rendering is intended to be identical. Only package.json and the lockfile changed.

## Version surfaces

All release surfaces are synchronized to v0.27.2:

- Electron website and Steam builds inherit v0.27.2 from package.json, including installer artifact names and app.getVersion().
- Android: versionName 0.27.2, versionCode 25.
- iOS: MARKETING_VERSION 0.27.2, CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION 28.
- Desktop download links, web version labels, and README badges across all 21 locales are v0.27.2.

## Validation

- CI is green on the tagged head (2edc3ac17): the full PR gate, Biome changed-file checks, Chromium browser regressions, and the screenshot jobs.
- The three.js revert ran the full local gate before merge: 16,184 tests passed (the only 2 failures are the known macOS-only deploy watchdog environment flakes, green on Ubuntu CI), plus a dedicated API-compatibility audit across the renderer, the untyped asset scripts, and the tests.
- The release_version, version_sync, and app_version suites (33 tests) report every version surface synchronized to 0.27.2.

## Upgrade notes

This is a patch release. Deploy server and clients from the same v0.27.2 build. The stable timer wire activates only between a v0.27.2 server and client; older clients stay on the unchanged legacy wire automatically, so rolling deploys are safe. The v0.27.2 tag starts the desktop publishing workflow for the signed macOS, Windows, and Linux artifacts and their update feeds.

See [#2138](https://github.com/levy-street/world-of-claudecraft/pull/2138), [#2112](https://github.com/levy-street/world-of-claudecraft/pull/2112), [#2110](https://github.com/levy-street/world-of-claudecraft/pull/2110), [#2105](https://github.com/levy-street/world-of-claudecraft/pull/2105), [#2136](https://github.com/levy-street/world-of-claudecraft/pull/2136), [#2141](https://github.com/levy-street/world-of-claudecraft/pull/2141), and [#2147](https://github.com/levy-street/world-of-claudecraft/pull/2147) for the implementation and verification records.

## Classes and Talents 2.0

### Warrior redesign

- **Three specializations:** Battlecraft (Arms, two-handed DPS, Master Armorer mastery: +10% damage while wielding a two-hander), Bloodrush (Fury, dual-wield berserker, Bloodletter mastery: +5% crit and +10 attack power), and Ironguard (Protection, shield tank, Recompense mastery: +30% threat, +10% armor, +40% Stamina, armor equal to 70% of Strength). Mastery scales linearly from level 1 to 20.
- **Stances:** Battle Stance (Arms/Protection default, +10% rage generation), Berserker Stance (Fury only, +3% crit and +3% crit damage), and Guarded Stance (Arms/Protection, +30% threat, -10% damage dealt and taken). Warriors are never stanceless; stances auto-apply on spawn and spec change. The stance bar returns to the HUD between the pet bar and action bars; stance abilities are removed from the main action bar.
- **Shared base kit:** Onrush (Charge, 8 to 25 yards, 1-second stun, generates 9 rage), Jawcrack (Pummel, free interrupt with rage on stop), Hobbling Cut (Hamstring), Iron Bellow (party AP shout, 30-minute buff, tooltip corrected from the old "2 min" text), Valor Roar (Rallying Cry, +20% max HP for party for 10 seconds at level 18), Heroic Leap (leap and AoE on landing), Early Grave (Execute, below 20% HP), and Intimidating Shout (AoE fear, 8 yards, 8 seconds, 5 targets, 120-second cooldown) join the warrior's class-wide kit.
- **Arms exclusive kit:** Maiming Strike (Mortal Strike, 50% healing reduction), Brute Swing (free rage builder with 4-second cooldown), Gaping Wounds (bleed from Maiming Strike), Reaping Arc (frontal AoE cleave), Widening Strikes (next single-target attack also strikes 1 nearby enemy for full damage), and Die by the Sword (30% damage reduction plus dodge for 8 seconds, 120-second cooldown) are Arms exclusives.
- **Fury exclusive kit:** Bloodletting (Bloodthirst, 50% weapon + 30 damage, heals 3% max HP, 30% chance to Enrage), Twinstrike (two 40% weapon hits, 2 charges), Mayhem passive (while Enraged: +7% damage, +25% attack speed, +10% movement speed), Red Harvest (costs 80 rage for a triple strike, always Enrages), Bladed Gyre (AoE whirlwind), and Furious Mending (120-second defensive that also makes Bloodletting heal 20% max HP).
- **Protection exclusive kit:** Shieldcrack (Shield Slam, massive threat, generates 15 rage), Armor Shear (Sunder Armor, max 5 stacks, -25 armor per stack), Quaking Blow (Thunder Clap with attack-speed slow), Revenge (free after dodge or parry), Raised Guard (50% physical damage reduction for 6 seconds, 2 charges), Iron Resolve (absorbs 4 damage per rage spent, up to 160 at 40 rage), Faultline (3-second frontal stun), Direhowl (all nearby enemies -20% damage for 20 seconds), and Defiant Bellow (AoE taunt, 10 yards, 3 seconds).
- **Six-tier choice-row tree:** Tier 1 mobility (Double Charge, Pursuit, Crushing Charge), Tier 2 survival (Second Wind at 1.5% max HP per second below 35%, Die by the Sword, Victory Rush), Tier 3 control (Piercing Howl, Storm Bolt, Lingering Dread), Tier 4 resource (Anger Management, Combat Mastery, Battle Rhythm), Tier 5 offensive cooldown (Recklessness, Avatar, Bloodbath), and Tier 6 capstone (Colossal Might, Bladestorm, Sanguine Aura). All 18 options are live.
- **Warrior parry and block:** Strength-scaled parry (base 5% plus 0.05% per Strength point, front-arc only) and shield block (Protection only, requires shield) are now applied to the warrior melee hit table.
- **Cleaving Blows timer bug fixed:** The refunded Twinstrike charge left an orphaned per-charge recharge timer that froze on a full pool and caused abnormally early recharge on the next spend. Fixed by popping the newest timer and re-deriving the active timer from the earliest surviving one.

### Talent engine (all classes)

- **Parallel per-charge recharge timers (all classes):** Two-charge abilities (such as Twin Gavels) now run one recharge timer per spent charge in parallel; the previous behavior queued the second charge behind the first, adding a full extra cooldown cycle.
- **Proc guardrails (G1 to G3):** A cast consuming a proc empower no longer advances castNth counters, stopping relay chains. castNth and spellCrit triggers accept an optional internal cooldown. All talent empowerNext responses must be ability-scoped; unscoped empowers are blocked.
- **Chance-gated proc triggers (G4):** castNth, spellCrit, and meleeSwingWhile triggers accept an optional chance field; the RNG roll fires only when the trigger would otherwise fire. Used in Rogue Venom Dividend.
- **PvP stun DR exemption:** Player-applied stuns (Storm Bolt, Twin Gavels) are exempt from the PvP diminishing-returns ladder. Short flat durations behind real cooldowns previously felt broken; fear, root, and lockout effects keep their DR ladders.
- **Max-health-scaled defensives (seven classes):** Seven choice-row panic-shield options that used flat absorb amounts (rotting as player health scaled) are reworked to scale with max HP: Hunter Deathless Will (ward 20% max HP), Priest Wounded Halo (15% max HP ward), Shaman Ancestral Mending (instant heal 12% max HP), Warlock Fiendward (heal 15% max HP if wearer falls below 35%), Warlock Deep Hunger (+50% Drain Life damage/healing), Druid Ironhide Reflex (absorb scales to 15% max HP, also restores 20 rage in Bruin Form).
- **Ability-scoped crit modifier (G8):** A new critPct field in the talent ability modifier system feeds both weapon-strike and direct-damage crit roll paths, used by the Rogue Knifework mastery.
- **Talent-loadout bar validation:** Switching talent loadouts no longer leaves spec-specific abilities from the wrong spec on the action bar; the check now resolves the ability set the target loadout actually grants before deciding which entries to keep ([#2003](https://github.com/levy-street/world-of-claudecraft/pull/2003)).
- **Spell crit now uses the shared crit bonus:** Melee crit correctly incorporated crit rating, talent crit, and set crit bonuses, but spell crit silently ignored them since the rating system launched. A new `Entity.sharedCritBonus` field is read by both the melee and spell hit tables. Crit rating from gear, talent crit bonuses (such as Nighttalon 3-piece), and flat crit auras now work for casters. Pinned by `tests/spell_crit_shared_core.test.ts`.
- **Damage-scaled fear breaks:** The full fear family (Intimidating Shout, Harrow, Dread Chorus, Morrowlash, Terror Canticle, and the shared aoeFear branch) no longer insta-breaks on any damage hit. Each damage event breaks the fear with probability min(1, damage / (0.1 times target max HP)), matching the classic rule (G5) that makes DoT-then-fear a workable warlock opener. Plain incapacitates keep break-on-any-damage behavior.

### Mage rework (all three specs)

- **Chronomancy (Arcane healer):** The Arcane spec is now a full healer. Temporal Echo marks an ally and converts 35% of the caster's single-target Arcane damage to healing on that ally (15% for AoE). Aether Surge stacks up to 4 Arcane Charges, scaling damage and cost geometrically at full stack; a 25% chance arms an Aether Rush proc (free, 2x faster cast). Aether Darts (formerly Arcane Missiles) consumes all charges on the first missile and fires 5 missiles at full charge. Temporal Cascade places group echo marks on up to 5 allies. Perfect Moment (120-second cooldown) grants 4 charges and opens a 10-second window where Aether Darts does not consume them. Temporal Acceleration shares the Bloodlust sated debuff with the Shaman's Storm Chorus. Temporal Reversal is a combat resurrection (600-second cooldown). Collective Reversal mass-resurrects all dead group members out of combat (7-second cast). Hourglass of Suspension (50-second cooldown) suspends an enemy for 60 seconds (10 in PvP), grants stasis to a group ally with 30% max HP recovery and 2x cooldown tick rate, or waits as a persistent ground trap.
- **Cryomancy (Frost) rework:** Fingers of Frost (15% per Rimelance impact, max 2 stacks) allows the next Ice Lance to treat the target as frozen. Brain Freeze (20% per Rimelance impact) makes the next Winterlash (formerly Flurry) instant and 30% stronger. Winter's Recall (formerly Cold Snap) finishes cooldowns on Flickerstep, Frostveil, and Greater Invisibility.
- **Pyromancy (Fire) rework:** Ignition mastery banks a stackable burn for 40% of each crit's damage, ticking every 2 seconds. Hot Streak arms a free instant Pyrelance or Flamestrike after two consecutive crits. Phoenix Trance (formerly Combustion, 120-second cooldown) guarantees crits for 10 seconds; builder crits outside it shave 1 second off its cooldown. Cauterize passive turns a killing blow into 25% max HP and a 5-second burn (5% per second) on a 5-minute cooldown. Dragon's Breath is a hold-to-charge frontal cone (guaranteed crit at full charge, counts toward Hot Streak). Cinderfall (formerly Fire Blast) is instant, off-GCD, always crits, 3 charges. Scald (formerly Scorch) is castable while moving and always crits below 30% enemy HP. Ember Form is a toggle travel form granting 40% movement speed with a custom visual (recast to return to normal form).
- **Shared base changes:** Flickerstep (Blink) moved from level 10 to level 5. Ice Block added to all three specs' base kits (Frost gets a second charge). Four ability names renamed to clear the IP denylist: Winterlash (formerly Flurry), Brittle Ruin (formerly Shatter), Phoenix Trance (formerly Combustion), and Winter's Recall (formerly Cold Snap). All four are filled across 20 release locales.

## Professions 2.0 and crafting

- **Archetype quest live:** "A Craft to Call Your Own" is now a real quest from Smith Haldren in Eastbrook (not the old stub giver). Completing it requires harvesting 3 ore veins and choosing a pair from a dropdown. The selected pair becomes the player's two majors (empowered past rare); the opposite of each major auto-assigns as the hobby (empowered to rare).
- **Pair-based archetype titles:** Ten archetype titles replace per-craft practitioner titles: Smith (Weaponcrafting + Armorcrafting), Bladewright (Jewelcrafting + Weaponcrafting), Arcanist (Inscription + Enchanting), and seven others covering the full craft ring.
- **Deterministic craft quality:** The five-way quality roll is retired. Every successful craft yields its declared output quality (common, uncommon, or rare). The only remaining randomness is the masterwork proc.
- **Masterwork proc:** A single draw at craft time can yield a copy with bonus primary stats equivalent to one tier higher, baked from the item budget, with the crafter's maker's mark. Base chance is 3% at tier, plus 1% per tier above requirement, plus 2% for a signed reagent (any player's signature counts), plus 3% at the 75-skill specialization threshold, hard-capped at 15%.
- **Combo recipe gating fixed online:** Combo recipes now require the exact active pair. The ClientWorld stub that kept the online Craft button always disabled is replaced by a shared `combo_eligibility.ts` module mirrored via the new `cprof` snapshot delta key.
- **Enchanting overhaul:** The enchanting table now offers two tiers: a base tier with per-build-archetype options on every slot (agility weapon, caster/healer/melee slot options, Reinforcement for tank helmets and chests) and a Greater tier on the five highest-impact slots: two weapon options (Might, Spellpower) plus helmet Fortitude, chest Stamina, legs Stamina, and gloves Agility. Greater enchants are the only consumer of Arcane Shards, giving disenchanting epics and legendaries a meaningful output ([#1950](https://github.com/levy-street/world-of-claudecraft/pull/1950)).
- **New caster-stat crafted gear:** Six new craftable items fill previously empty caster slots: Eastbrook Ritual Vestments (cloth chest, Tailoring), Eastbrook Druid's Hide (leather chest, Leatherworking), Eastbrook Warded Leggings (mail legs, Armorcrafting) at uncommon tier, and Wardweave Cowl (cloth helmet), Duskhide Wraps (leather gloves), and Sootscale Mantle (mail shoulders) as hub-tier rares at item level 23 ([#1965](https://github.com/levy-street/world-of-claudecraft/pull/1965)).
- **Crafting material quality fixed:** Three crafting reagents (Twitching Spider Leg, Bone Fragments, Linen Scrap) were quality "poor" and auto-vendored by "Sell All Junk." All recipe reagents are now quality "common." A guard test (`tests/crafting_materials_quality.test.ts`) ensures no future reagent is assigned quality "poor."
- **Traded items preserve enchants and craft quality:** Items with an instance payload (enchants, maker's mark, masterwork flag) no longer lose that data when traded between players ([#2045](https://github.com/levy-street/world-of-claudecraft/pull/2045)).
- **Crafted items now show item level and item score** in their tooltips; the item level calculation system was not registering crafted outputs from recipes.

# World of ClaudeCraft v0.26.0 Release Notes

**Release:** v0.26.0
**Date:** 2026-07-15
**Previous release:** v0.25.0

v0.26.0 is a dungeon finder, itemization, combat, social, and production hardening release, with 131 commits since v0.25.0. It adds the Dungeon Finder with auto-queue and premade boards, a Hit Rating stat with a complete heroic itemization pass, three tank defensive cooldowns, a signed Windows desktop installer, node harvesting you can actually click, weapon sheathing, production stability hardening with realm admission caps and lease takeover, and 11 GLB prop replacements across the Drowned Litany and related zones.

## Highlights

- **Dungeon Finder:** a new Shift+I window with activity catalogue, Quick Match role queue, and Premade Board covers all four dungeons, their heroic variants, and the Nythraxis raid in both difficulties. Matches form automatically via deterministic FIFO and never touch the sim's RNG ([#1789](https://github.com/levy-street/world-of-claudecraft/pull/1789)).
- **Hit Rating and heroic itemization:** a new Hit Rating stat (10 rating = 1% hit) caps the above-level miss/resist penalty at roughly 26%/25% for Heroic (+3 level), down from roughly 44%/43%. Every ilvl-31 heroic boss-set piece and every Nythraxis raid piece gains one or two combat ratings, and Heroic Quartermaster rings and amulets each carry 2.5% in one combat rating chosen by archetype. PvP gear is rebalanced so it is no longer a PvE stat upgrade over same-tier dungeon gear ([#1860](https://github.com/levy-street/world-of-claudecraft/pull/1860)).
- **Tank defensive cooldowns:** Warriors get Ironhold (40% damage reduction, 8 sec), Paladins get Sacred Bulwark (a guardian ward that denies a killing blow and restores 35% HP), and Druids get Primal Reflexes (50% dodge, 60 sec cooldown). Druid bear parity is also fixed ([#1912](https://github.com/levy-street/world-of-claudecraft/pull/1912)).
- **Windows desktop client:** the signed Windows installer is now live. The "Download for Windows" button appears on the website and play page, and the installer is Authenticode-signed via Azure Key Vault, removing the unsigned-publisher warning (SmartScreen reputation for the new signing identity builds over the first weeks of installs) ([#1961](https://github.com/levy-street/world-of-claudecraft/pull/1961), [#1944](https://github.com/levy-street/world-of-claudecraft/pull/1944)).
- **Gather nodes you can click:** ore, wood, and herb nodes were simulated but unharvestable from normal play. Click, tap, or press Interact to harvest within 5 yards; the per-player cooldown is now correctly mirrored online ([#1937](https://github.com/levy-street/world-of-claudecraft/pull/1937)).
- **Weapon sheathing:** press Z (rebindable) to stow your weapon on your back. Each weapon family has a hand-authored on-back pose; any combat action re-draws automatically. Persists through relog and is visible to other players ([#1765](https://github.com/levy-street/world-of-claudecraft/pull/1765)).
- **Production stability:** realm admission cap (`MAX_PLAYERS_PER_REALM`), same-account lease takeover, full-jitter reconnect backoff, self-clocked keepalive sweep, bounded Postgres pool timeouts, `/livez` and `/readyz` health endpoints, and a seven-step restart countdown ([#1930](https://github.com/levy-street/world-of-claudecraft/pull/1930)).

## Dungeon Finder

- Shift+I opens the Dungeon Finder with three panels: a Catalogue (boss portraits, mechanics previews, lockout type, and "Show on Map"), Quick Match (role queue), and Premade Board (leader-published listings with run-intent tags and application approval).
- Activities covered: all four Normal dungeons (levels 7 to 20), all four Heroic dungeons (level 20, daily lockout), Nythraxis Raid Arena Normal and Heroic (level 20, 10-player, attunement required), and Abandoned Crypt on the Premade Board only (no auto-queue).
- Automatic matching uses deterministic FIFO (candidate window 24, node budget 4000 per tick). Group proposals last 30 seconds; declining or expiring triggers a 60-second re-queue lockout.
- Before level 10, roles are assigned from a fixed class-capability table. From level 10 onward, the active specialization's role is used; no active spec means the finder is unavailable.
- Three parity gaps fixed alongside the finder: the partiesJoined deed stat, ready-check teardown on dissolved source parties, and the meta.leaving flag so a disconnecting player cannot be matched.
- The finder never teleports, never changes difficulty or loot, and draws no RNG, so it cannot perturb sim determinism. All matching runs end-of-tick ([#1789](https://github.com/levy-street/world-of-claudecraft/pull/1789)).

## Items and combat

- **Hit Rating stat:** 10 rating = 1% hit, reducing both melee/ranged miss and spell resist. Appears on the character sheet and all item tooltips. The above-level cap for Heroic (+3 level) falls from roughly 44%/43% to roughly 26%/25%.
- **Heroic itemization:** every ilvl-31 heroic boss-set piece gains one combat rating (roughly half Hit, the rest Crit or Haste by archetype; healer pieces never take Hit). The 10 Heroic Quartermaster rings and amulets each gain one combat rating (2.5%), chosen by archetype: Hit for melee and caster-DPS pieces, Haste for healer-leaning and caster pieces, or Crit for agility-DPS and throughput pieces. Ilvl-29 raid set pieces gain one rating; their ilvl-33 and ilvl-37 Heroic Nythraxis variants are the only dual-rating gear in the game and represent a genuine qualitative step up over ilvl-31. The three Nythraxis heroic weapons also carry dual ratings.
- **Four-piece bleed bonuses now grant +6% Hit:** the Strength melee T2 four-piece bonus and the Agility T2 four-piece bonus both add +6% Hit on top of their bleed effect, making previously marginal set bonuses meaningful for Heroic progression.
- **PvP gear rebalanced:** all PvP armor and weapons drop to 60% of the ilvl-28 slot primary-stat budget (jewelry drops further), freeing budget fully expressed as WARFARE ratings. PvP gear is no longer a PvE stat upgrade over same-tier PvE dungeon or badge gear; the 16.8% full-set PvP offense/defense target is unchanged ([#1860](https://github.com/levy-street/world-of-claudecraft/pull/1860)).
- **Tank defensive cooldowns:** Warrior gains Ironhold (40% all-damage reduction for 8 sec, 3-minute cooldown). Paladin gains Sacred Bulwark (guardian ward lasting 10 sec: denies a killing blow and restores 35% max HP on consumption, 3-minute cooldown). Druid gains Primal Reflexes (50% dodge for 6 sec, 60-second cooldown, usable while shapeshifted). Feral Dire Bruin talent buffed from +10%/+12% threat/armor to +20%/+15%, bringing specced bear tanks to parity with the shaman off-tank ([#1912](https://github.com/levy-street/world-of-claudecraft/pull/1912)).

## Production and operations

- **Realm admission cap:** new env var `MAX_PLAYERS_PER_REALM` (default 5000). The server counts both seated clients and in-flight handshakes before admitting a join. Refused joins receive a localizable "realm is full" frame; reconnecting sessions and admin accounts are exempt. Set to 0 to disable.
- **Same-account lease takeover:** when a client reconnects for the same account, the server claims the existing lease immediately instead of waiting out the TTL. The `character_leases` table gains a nullable `account_id` column (applied automatically at boot via `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`).
- **Full-jitter reconnect backoff:** `src/net/backoff.ts` implements full-jitter exponential backoff. Auth-timeout rejections during database brownouts are now classified as transient (bounded at 20 attempts, reset on successful hello) so a database blip no longer drops players to the login screen permanently.
- **Self-clocked keepalive sweep:** the keepalive sweep re-arms after a single event-loop stall instead of mass-terminating all sessions, preventing a transient stall from kicking the entire online population.
- **Bounded Postgres pool:** 5 s connect timeout, 15 s default statement timeout, 60 s elevated timeout for heavy reads and character-save paths, 65 s driver-level backstop. Boot DDL runs on a dedicated non-pool client.
- **`/livez` and `/readyz` health endpoints:** `/livez` returns 200 while the game loop is healthy, 503 if no tick has completed in 30 seconds. `/readyz` returns 503 with body "draining" once drain begins, so a load balancer stops routing new traffic during graceful restart. The docker-compose game service now has an exec-form `healthcheck` probing `/livez`, `stop_grace_period: 75s`, and memory limits of 5 g.
- **In-game restart countdown:** a scripted broadcast sequence announces an impending restart at 10 min, 5 min, 2 min, 1 min, 30 s, 10 s, and 0 s. Triggered via `POST /internal/restart-countdown` (secret-gated) ([#1930](https://github.com/levy-street/world-of-claudecraft/pull/1930)).
- **Automated daily payouts infrastructure:** three new database tables and internal API routes support the companion payout service claiming, voiding, restoring, and resending payouts idempotently. Tables are created at boot (`IF NOT EXISTS`). Requires `WOC_DAILY_REWARD_SERVICE_SECRET` matching `DAILY_REWARD_INTERNAL_SECRET` on the companion service ([#1936](https://github.com/levy-street/world-of-claudecraft/pull/1936)).
- **Player business analytics (Prometheus):** daily acquisition, first-character conversion, first-world-entry conversion, new and returning daily active accounts, average daily playtime, first-session duration, level activation rate, and D1/D7/D30 retention. Refreshed from Postgres every 15 minutes; Prometheus scrapes only the last good in-memory snapshot ([#1845](https://github.com/levy-street/world-of-claudecraft/pull/1845)).
- **Docker build context fixed for prod CPU scripts:** `.dockerignore` exceptions added so `scripts/prod_cpu_*` files are copied into the build context, fixing a broken prod image build ([#1858](https://github.com/levy-street/world-of-claudecraft/pull/1858)).

## Upgrade notes

- **`MAX_PLAYERS_PER_REALM`:** new env var, default 5000. Set explicitly in your compose override to change. Reconnecting sessions and admin accounts bypass the cap.
- **Database (lease takeover):** `ALTER TABLE character_leases ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS account_id INT` runs automatically at boot. Safe on a live database with no downtime required.
- **Database (daily payouts):** three new tables (`daily_reward_payouts`, `daily_reward_payout_moderation_audit`, `daily_reward_payout_attempts`) created at boot via `IF NOT EXISTS`. - **Memory limit:** set `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=4096` in your compose override before deploying. The new `mem_limit: 5g` in docker-compose is sized for a 4096 MiB V8 heap plus native overhead; leaving the heap unbounded risks OOM-kills mid-tick.
- **Health endpoints:** `/livez` and `/readyz` are now available. Configure your load balancer or watchdog to probe `/livez` for liveness and `/readyz` for readiness during deploys. The `healthcheck` in docker-compose uses an inline Node probe (no curl required in the Alpine image).
- **Postgres pool:** the pool now enforces a 5 s connect timeout and a 15 s default statement timeout that did not exist before. If your workload includes queries that legitimately exceed 15 s, verify they go through `runWithStatementTimeout` (which raises to 60 s) rather than the default pool path.
- **Windows publish secrets:** five new GitHub Actions secrets are required before the Windows publish job can run: `AZURE_TENANT_ID`, `AZURE_CLIENT_ID`, `AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET`, `AZURE_KEY_VAULT_URL`, and `AZURE_KEY_VAULT_CERTIFICATE`. Run `npm run i18n:gen` after adding catalog keys to also emit `translation_keys.generated.ts`; commit this file alongside any catalog change or the CI freshness gate will fail.

It adds the Book of Deeds achievement system, Heroic Nythraxis, real signature abilities and identity masteries for all 27 specializations, Honor and Warfare PvP progression, the Claudium storefront and Season 1 Armory cosmetics, a production sound workflow, richer world models and bag art, player mute and identity tools, a rebuilt online-only /play entry, and a broad reliability and operations pass.

# World of ClaudeCraft v0.24.2 Release Notes

**Release:** v0.24.2
**Previous release:** v0.24.1

## What changed

### Heroic rewards and mobile loot ([#1806](https://github.com/levy-street/world-of-claudecraft/pull/1806))

- Heroic final-boss kills no longer persist a lockout while losing the corresponding Heroic Mark, corpse loot, or Need/Greed award. Marks are now awarded directly at final-boss death and use the same realm-local reset boundary as the heroic lockout, removing the former UTC-day mismatch.

- Reward eligibility is frozen before the disconnect save yields: pending and master-loot items are conserved, corpse rights and party loot strategy are preserved when the original tapper leaves, and stale post-snapshot commands are rejected.

- On short landscape phones, only actionable roll cards are shown and Bags now sits above the mobile roll rail, so opening Bags during a roll no longer leaves the interface looking locked. Desktop stacking is unchanged.
- Heroic drop tables are intentionally unchanged. Each heroic final boss still has two guaranteed dedicated epic roll groups.

### Saved frame-position reset ([#1793](https://github.com/levy-street/world-of-claudecraft/pull/1793))

- A one-time, client-side reset of the saved unit-frame drag positions (`woc_player_frame_pos` and `woc_target_frame_pos`). Positions saved during the brief v0.24.0 overhaul replayed against the restored classic layout and left the player frame floating in a stale spot. The reset is gated by a `woc_layout_reset_epoch` marker so it clears exactly once and never re-clears on a downgrade.
